cards.front: Why did Germany end up in a worse position after the Algeciras Conference than before it started the crisis?
cards.answer: Germany expected international backing for open trade but instead Britain, Russia, Italy and the US all backed France, isolating Germany diplomatically.

cards.front: Why was Russia unable to get compensation over the Bosnian annexation despite feeling betrayed?
cards.answer: Aehrenthal had led Russia to expect compensation, but Germany then backed Austria-Hungary unconditionally, forcing Russia to accept the annexation with nothing.

title: Reversible Reactions and Le Chatelier's Principle
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Why does haemoglobin release oxygen to the tissues but combine with it at the lungs?
cards.answer: The equilibrium position shifts depending on local oxygen concentration — high at the lungs favours oxyhaemoglobin, low at the tissues releases oxygen.

cards.front: Why can equilibrium only be reached in a closed system?
cards.answer: If products escape they cannot react back, so the reaction keeps going forward until completion instead of reaching equilibrium.

cards.front: If the forward reaction in a reversible reaction is exothermic, what is true of the reverse reaction's energy change?
cards.answer: The reverse reaction is endothermic by the same amount of energy, equal in magnitude but opposite in sign.

cards.front: Why is 200 atm used in the Haber process rather than a much higher pressure?
cards.answer: Very high pressures would give more yield but are dangerous and too expensive to maintain, so 200 atm is a compromise.

cards.front: Name the four weaknesses historians point to that question whether the Stresemann years were a 'golden age'
cards.answer: Falling grain prices hurt farmers / Unemployment never fell below 1.3 million / Political extremism remained active / Coalition governments stayed unstable

cards.front: How did the Dawes Plan (1924) help Germany's economy recover?
cards.answer: American loans flowed in, industries modernised, unemployment fell and real wages rose after reparations were restructured into affordable instalments.

cards.front: Why did the German economy collapse so quickly after the Wall Street Crash in October 1929?
cards.answer: American banks demanded their short-term loans back, and Germany's recovery had been dangerously dependent on continued US investment.

cards.front: Why was Germany's admission to the League of Nations in 1926 seen as a major diplomatic achievement?
cards.answer: Germany was given a permanent Council seat equal to Britain, France, Italy and Japan, just seven years after being defeated and humiliated in 1919.

cards.front: What are the four types of neutralisation reaction the lesson gives, based on what the acid reacts with?
cards.answer: Acid + metal / Acid + metal oxide / Acid + metal hydroxide / Acid + metal carbonate

cards.front: Name the two pieces of apparatus the lesson says are needed for titration.
cards.answer: Burette / Pipette

cards.front: Why is the filtrate evaporated over a water bath rather than heated directly when making copper(II) sulfate crystals?
cards.answer: The gentle heat stops the crystals spitting or losing their water of crystallisation.

cards.front: Why is a concentrated weak acid able to have a lower pH than a dilute weak acid, even though both only partially ionise?
cards.answer: Acid strength depends on the degree of ionisation, not concentration, so a concentrated weak acid still has more H⁺ ions overall.

cards.front: Name the two verification techniques the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Double entry / Proofreading

cards.front: Why should a WHILE loop be used instead of a single IF statement to validate a score?
cards.answer: A WHILE loop keeps prompting until the score is valid, whereas a single IF only checks once and could still accept invalid data later.

cards.front: Why is proofreading used instead of double entry for checking a handwritten address against a database record?
cards.answer: Proofreading is used where computer checking is impractical, so a human reads through the entered data to check for errors.

cards.front: Why are low-level languages not portable between different computers?
cards.answer: They are tied to a specific processor architecture, giving direct control over memory and registers rather than hiding hardware detail.

cards.front: Name the three main track types in a DAW.
cards.answer: Audio tracks / Software instrument tracks / MIDI tracks

cards.front: Name the three uncompressed vs compressed file formats a DAW can export to.
cards.answer: WAV / AIF / MP3

cards.front: Why is a larger buffer size better for mixing than a small one?
cards.answer: A larger buffer gives stable processing with fewer glitches, which matters more than latency when mixing.

cards.front: Why do audio loops and MIDI loops differ in how much they can be changed?
cards.answer: Audio loops are fixed recordings, while MIDI loops store note data so they can be edited freely.

title: Jim Crow, the Klan and racial violence
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four ways Jim Crow laws in the South denied African Americans equal rights, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Denied equal access to education / Barred voting via literacy tests, poll taxes, grandfather clauses / Prohibited interracial marriage / Enforced segregation in public spaces
items: Barred voting via literacy tests, poll taxes, grandfather clauses

cards.front: Name the three groups, besides African Americans, targeted by the second Ku Klux Klan.
cards.answer: Catholics / Jews / Immigrants

cards.front: Why did federal anti-lynching laws never pass during this period?
cards.answer: Every anti-lynching bill was filibustered to death in the Senate by Southern politicians.

cards.front: How was the Great Migration itself a form of resistance to racial oppression?
cards.answer: Around 1.6 million African Americans moved from the South to northern cities, leaving the most oppressive conditions behind.

cards.front: How does the novel's three-part structure mirror Meena's coming-of-age arc?
cards.answer: First half shows desire for Anita's world, the middle is crisis (accident, racism, loss), the second half is resolution and self-acceptance.

cards.front: Why does Tollington's sense of community have limits for the Kumars?
cards.answer: Villagers share the Kumars' economic circumstances but never fully accept their culture, showing class and race intersecting.

title: Exam technique and synthesis: was it a Golden Age?
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name four reasons historical interpretations of Elizabeth's reign might differ, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Different sources used / Different time periods written in / Different purpose of the work / Different methodologies applied

cards.front: Name four pieces of high-value evidence the lesson says cut across multiple essay topics on Elizabeth's reign.
cards.answer: 1601 Poor Law / Armada defeat / Execution of Mary Queen of Scots / Essex rebellion
items: Execution of Mary Queen of Scots

cards.front: Why does the 1601 Poor Law count as evidence against the 'Golden Age' view, not just an achievement?
cards.answer: It was landmark legislation but also an acknowledgement that poverty and vagrancy had worsened significantly across the reign.

cards.front: Why is the Armada's defeat in 1588 not enough on its own to prove the war with Spain was won?
cards.answer: Because fighting between England and Spain actually continued until 1604, well beyond the Armada's defeat.

cards.front: Name the three key differences between tillite, conglomerate and breccia given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Conglomerate has rounded, water-transported clasts / Breccia has angular clasts but is better sorted and gravity-deposited / Tillite has chaotic unsorted mix with no grading or layering
items: Breccia has angular clasts but is better sorted and gravity-deposited
Tillite has chaotic unsorted mix with no grading or layering

cards.front: Name the three areas the lesson says are made of Cretaceous Chalk in Britain.
cards.answer: White Cliffs of Dover / North and South Downs / Yorkshire Wolds

cards.front: Why does tillite show no layering or grading?
cards.answer: Glaciers dump all particle sizes together at once without any sorting action from water or wind.

cards.front: Why did Pleistocene glacial deposits end up sitting directly above older greenhouse-phase sediments in Britain?
cards.answer: Britain drifted north into greenhouse conditions, then later experienced Pleistocene icehouse glaciation depositing till on top of older rocks.

cards.front: Name the five Arab armies that invaded Israel in May 1948.
cards.answer: Egypt / Jordan / Syria / Iraq / Lebanon

cards.front: Name the three Israeli offensives launched between October 1948 and January 1949.
cards.answer: Operation Yoav / Operation Hiram / Operation Horev

cards.front: Why did Israel build the 'Burma Road' during the fighting for Jerusalem?
cards.answer: To bypass Latrun, where Jordanian forces blocked the main route, so supply convoys could reach besieged West Jerusalem.

cards.front: Why did the military balance shift in Israel's favour the longer the 1948–49 war continued?
cards.answer: Israel mobilised its full population to over 100,000 soldiers under unified command, while Arab volunteer and expeditionary forces struggled to stay supplied at distance.

title: Two world wars and inter-war migration
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four British port cities where race riots broke out in 1919.
cards.answer: Cardiff / Liverpool / Glasgow / South Shields

cards.front: Why did race riots break out in British port cities in 1919?
cards.answer: White servicemen returning from demobilisation found jobs taken by Black and Asian workers recruited during the war, causing economic resentment and violence.

cards.front: Why did the British government limit Jewish refugee admissions in the early 1930s?
cards.answer: The Home Office feared antisemitism in Britain and worried about economic competition during the Depression.

cards.front: Why did around 120,000 Poles choose to remain in Britain after 1945?
cards.answer: Poland had come under Soviet control and some veterans were targeted for their wartime service if they returned, so many stayed under the Polish Resettlement Act.

cards.front: Name the four ways given to prevent enzymic browning on cut fruit or vegetables.
cards.answer: Coat with lemon juice or ascorbic acid / Submerge in cold water / Blanch briefly / Refrigerate
items: Coat with lemon juice or ascorbic acid

cards.front: What are the four possible causes given for a Victoria sandwich sinking in the middle?
cards.answer: Insufficient aeration during creaming / Too much raising agent / Opening the oven door too early / Under-baking
items: Opening the oven door too early

cards.front: Why does adding starch directly to hot liquid cause a lumpy sauce?
cards.answer: The outer granules gelatinise instantly, forming a sticky coating that traps dry starch inside, so it doesn't disperse evenly.

cards.front: Why must gluten formation be minimised when making shortcrust pastry?
cards.answer: Too much gluten makes the pastry tough and difficult to roll, so cold fat, cold water and minimal mixing are used to limit it.

cards.front: How does Malcolm know Macduff's grief and loyalty are genuine rather than fake?
cards.answer: A spy sent by Macbeth would have accepted a corrupt king, but Macduff reacts with despair, proving true patriotism.

cards.front: Why is Macduff's insistence on feeling grief 'as a man' significant to the play's view of masculinity?
cards.answer: It challenges Lady Macbeth's definition of masculinity as ruthlessness, showing true strength lies in emotional honesty, not violence.

cards.front: Name the seven typical speeds the lesson gives, from walking to sound in air.
cards.answer: walking ≈ 1.5 m/s / running ≈ 3 m/s / cycling ≈ 6 m/s / car in town ≈ 13 m/s / car on motorway ≈ 30 m/s / train ≈ 55 m/s / sound in air ≈ 330 m/s

cards.front: Why does an athlete who runs one full lap of a 400 m track have zero displacement?
cards.answer: Displacement is the net distance from the start in a direction, and the athlete finishes back where they started.

cards.front: Why is v² = u² + 2as the right equation to use when a problem gives distance but not time?
cards.answer: It links initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration and distance without needing time in the calculation.

cards.front: In the trolley-on-a-ramp experiment, why does plotting acceleration against force give a straight line through the origin?
cards.answer: Because this happens if F = ma holds, showing acceleration is proportional to the applied force.

title: Human Rights, Equality and Freedom of Religion
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the three religious groundings for human dignity given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Christian: made in God's image (Genesis 1:27) / Sikh: equality through Ik Onkar / Muslim: dignity conferred on all by God (Quran 17:70)
items: Muslim: dignity conferred on all by God (Quran 17:70)

cards.front: Why did Guru Nanak sit and eat with people of all social backgrounds?
cards.answer: To challenge the caste-based prejudice of his era and show the complete equality of all people.

cards.front: Why does the Roman Catholic Church say it does not recognise same-sex marriage?
cards.answer: It teaches marriage is a sacrament between a man and a woman, and same-sex relationships are not in keeping with natural law as it understands it.

cards.front: How can rights protected by UDHR Article 18 be limited, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Rights may only be limited to protect the rights of others or to meet just requirements of public order.

title: Core Beliefs: Six Articles & Five Roots
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the six Sunni Articles of Faith (Iman).
cards.answer: Tawhid / Malaikah / Kutub / Risalah / Akhirah / Al-Qadr

cards.front: Name the five Shi'a Roots of Usul ad-Din.
cards.answer: Tawhid / Adalat / Nubuwwah / Imamate / Al-Ma'ad

cards.front: Why did Islam split into Sunni and Shi'a branches after Muhammad's death?
cards.answer: Most Muslims accepted Abu Bakr as Caliph, while a minority believed Muhammad had appointed Ali, leading to a leadership dispute.

cards.front: Why is only the Qur'an considered fully reliable among the holy books (Kutub) in Sunni belief?
cards.answer: Because although Allah revealed several scriptures, only the Qur'an is believed to remain uncorrupted as God's unchanged word.

cards.front: Name the four marriages Austen presents in Pride and Prejudice to explore what makes a good union.
cards.answer: Mr and Mrs Bennet / Charlotte and Mr Collins / Lydia and Wickham / Elizabeth and Darcy

cards.front: Name the social ranks in Regency society's hierarchy, from top to bottom, as the lesson gives them.
cards.answer: Aristocracy / Landed gentry / Minor gentry / Professionals, merchants and tradespeople

cards.front: Why does Austen's opening line count as verbal irony?
cards.answer: It presents the Regency obsession with marriage and money as a universal truth, when it really reflects families' desperate need to marry off daughters.

cards.front: How does free indirect discourse let Austen show Elizabeth is wrong about Darcy while staying sympathetic to her?
cards.answer: The narrator's voice blends with Elizabeth's thoughts, drawing readers into her prejudice before planting clues that reveal her error.

cards.front: Name the six steps in the recommended structure for a 9-mark synoptic answer.
cards.answer: Opening sentence stating position / Body paragraph on sport psychology / Body paragraph on socio-cultural factor / Linking paragraph connecting both topics / Counter-argument / Conclusion with justified judgement

cards.front: Why does planning before writing improve a 9-mark synoptic answer?
cards.answer: Planning identifies the sport psychology and socio-cultural concepts needed, a linking sentence and a conclusion, giving better structure than writing unplanned.

cards.front: Name the four characteristic properties of ionic compounds caused by their giant lattice structure.
cards.answer: High melting and boiling points / Conduct electricity when molten or dissolved / Do not conduct when solid / Brittle
items: Conduct electricity when molten or dissolved

cards.front: List the three properties diamond has because each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds.
cards.answer: Extreme hardness / Very high melting point / No electrical conductivity

cards.front: Why are ionic compounds brittle?
cards.answer: If a force shifts a layer of ions, ions with identical charges align and repel strongly, shattering the crystal.

cards.front: Why do polymers have higher melting points than simple molecules?
cards.answer: Their long tangled chains experience stronger intermolecular forces than simple molecules, so more energy is needed to separate them.

cards.front: Name the four types of technical textiles covered in this unit.
cards.answer: Geotextiles / Micro-fibres / Breathable membranes / Interactive/wearable electronics

cards.front: How does a moisture-management fabric move sweat away from the skin?
cards.answer: A hydrophobic inner layer repels liquid water and pushes moisture into a hydrophilic outer layer, which spreads it out for evaporation.

cards.front: Why are carbon fibres almost pure carbon after manufacture?
cards.answer: Polyacrylonitrile is heated at high temperatures in a controlled atmosphere, driving off most non-carbon atoms and leaving a carbon fibre.

cards.front: Why is a hybrid CFRP-Kevlar composite used in some structures?
cards.answer: It balances the high stiffness of carbon fibre with the high toughness and impact resistance of Kevlar.

cards.front: Name the four things fabric width, weight and form are measured by in textile stock forms (roll size, width, weight, plus one more)?
cards.answer: Roll size / Width / Weight (gsm) / Sold by the roll or metre
items: Sold by the roll or metre

cards.front: Name the three ply ratings used to show the strength of corrugated card.
cards.answer: Single wall / Double wall / Triple wall

cards.front: Why is board measured by gsm (grams per square metre)?
cards.answer: Gsm shows the weight of the board per square metre, which indicates its thickness and stiffness.

cards.front: How does good nesting reduce waste when cutting panels from a standard MDF sheet?
cards.answer: Arranging panels closely together along the sheet's length and width leaves only small offcuts instead of large wasted areas.

title: Programming Languages: High-level, Low-level, Compilers and Interpreters
subject: computer-science-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three disadvantages of low-level languages given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Hard to read and write / Processor-specific, not portable / Take much longer to develop

cards.front: Why is it much harder to write programs directly in machine code?
cards.answer: Each instruction is a long binary string and the programmer must manually track every memory address.

cards.front: Why can the same Python program run on Windows, Mac and Linux without changes?
cards.answer: High-level languages abstract away hardware details, and a suitable interpreter or compiler translates it for each platform.

cards.front: Why are high-level languages much easier to debug than low-level languages?
cards.answer: Meaningful variable names, structured control flow and comments make programs readable to any developer, speeding up fixing errors.

cards.front: Name the three lines of evidence for evolution given in the lesson.
cards.answer: The fossil record / Comparative anatomy / DNA comparisons

cards.front: Why do comparative anatomy studies (like limb bones in humans, whales, bats and horses) support evolution?
cards.answer: Species sharing a common ancestor inherit similar underlying body structures even when used for different purposes.

cards.front: Why does completing a full course of antibiotics matter for preventing resistance?
cards.answer: Stopping early can leave the least affected, most resistant bacteria alive to survive and reproduce.

cards.front: Why was Darwin's proposal of a mechanism more powerful than simply gathering more observations?
cards.answer: A mechanism explains existing data and makes testable predictions, which were later confirmed independently across fields.

cards.front: In the model paragraph, how does the enjambment between 'leaves' and 'torn' create effect?
cards.answer: It mirrors the sudden tearing away, reinforcing the violent image of time destroying memories.

cards.front: Why should each comparison paragraph focus on one specific method used by both poets?
cards.answer: It keeps the response focused and proportionate, allowing tight analysis rather than describing poems separately.

cards.front: Name the three circuit assembly methods identified for producing a finished PCB.
cards.answer: Surface mount technology (SMT) / Through-hole construction / Manual soldering

cards.front: Name the three types of components the lesson gives as examples still using through-hole construction on modern PCBs.
cards.answer: Connectors (USB ports, power sockets) / High-power components (large electrolytic capacitors, power MOSFETs) / Mechanical mounting points needing an anchored joint
items: High-power components (large electrolytic capacitors, power MOSFETs)
Mechanical mounting points needing an anchored joint

cards.front: Why does a through-hole joint create a mechanically stronger connection than an SMT joint?
cards.answer: The lead passes through the drilled hole in the board, giving it a physical anchor rather than just sitting on the surface.

cards.front: How does a cold (dry) solder joint form during manual soldering?
cards.answer: The pad or lead is not heated enough before solder is applied, so the solder solidifies before flowing properly.

cards.front: How does eutrophication end up killing fish?
cards.answer: Excess nutrients cause algae to grow rapidly, blocking sunlight; algae then die and decompose, and decomposition uses up dissolved oxygen, suffocating aquatic life.

cards.front: Why is distillation more expensive than reverse osmosis for desalination?
cards.answer: Distillation requires boiling all the seawater, which is very energy-intensive, whereas reverse osmosis only needs high pressure to force water through a membrane.

cards.front: What happens to the sludge removed during waste water treatment? Give the three possible outcomes.
cards.answer: Digested by bacteria (anaerobic digestion, producing biogas) / Dried / Used as agricultural fertiliser
items: Digested by bacteria (anaerobic digestion, producing biogas)

title: The First and Second Noble Truths
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Why can no amount of getting what we crave ever finally satisfy us, according to the Second Noble Truth?
cards.answer: Because all conditioned things are impermanent, so satisfying craving cannot last and simply generates more craving.

cards.front: How does the Buddha's medical diagnosis analogy explain the structure of the Four Noble Truths?
cards.answer: The first identifies the illness, the second finds its cause, the third declares a cure exists, the fourth prescribes the treatment.

cards.front: Name the five stages Russell charts in Mickey's decline through the play's second half.
cards.answer: Factory work deadens his spirit / Redundancy strips his identity / Sammy leads him into crime / Prison breaks him / Antidepressants leave him emotionally numb

cards.front: Why does Russell show the Johnstones' hope about moving to Skelmersdale as only temporary?
cards.answer: The new environment cannot change the structural inequalities of class, so the council estate in the country is still a council estate.

cards.front: How does Eddie's education give him advantages that Mickey never gets?
cards.answer: University gives Eddie social capital — networks, confidence and polish — that opens doors in professional life, unlike Mickey's schooling.

cards.front: Why does Russell present the Mickey-Linda-Eddie love triangle as caused by inequality rather than betrayal?
cards.answer: If Mickey had Eddie's opportunities, like stable work and mental health support, the affair would never have happened.

cards.front: Why does Dharker describe lives as flying 'like paper kites' in 'Tissue'?
cards.answer: The simile imagines lives as light, free and joyful but fragile, celebrating impermanence rather than fearing it.

cards.front: Why does the mother lean against the war memorial 'like a wishbone' in 'Poppies'?
cards.answer: Tracing the memorial is a surrogate act of touching her son, and the wishbone image reveals her fragile hope.

cards.front: Why does Weir describe the poppy's petals as 'spasms of paper red'?
cards.answer: The visceral noun 'spasms' shows that even the symbol of remembrance carries violence within it.

cards.front: Name the six causes of deforestation the lesson gives for rainforest clearance.
cards.answer: Commercial agriculture / Subsistence farming (slash-and-burn) / Hardwood logging / Fuel wood collection / Mining / HEP dams

cards.front: Name the four levels of the rainforest food web described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Producers / Primary consumers / Secondary consumers / Decomposers

cards.front: Why does deforested rainforest land become infertile within a few years?
cards.answer: Because nutrients are stored in the trees not the soil, so once trees are removed the fast nutrient cycle collapses and soil holds little.

cards.front: How do unusual droughts lead to wildfires in the Amazon?
cards.answer: Hotter, drier conditions cause tree die-back through ecosystem stress, drying the forest enough to trigger wildfires despite normally being too damp to burn.

cards.front: Why must a fitness test be administered exactly the same way as the test used to build normative data?
cards.answer: If conditions differ, the comparison is invalid, so the performer's result cannot be meaningfully judged against the normative table.

cards.front: Why would the multistage fitness test have low validity if used to assess muscular strength?
cards.answer: It does not measure that component at all, so it fails to reflect what is required for strength.

title: Whitechapel 1888: housing, poverty and the inner city
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Give three features of Whitechapel's alleys and courts that made policing after dark almost impossible.
cards.answer: Very narrow cul-de-sacs (one or two feet wide) / Open sewers and broken paving / Gas lamps that did not reach the courts / Constables could be cornered or lose sight of suspects
items: Very narrow cul-de-sacs (one or two feet wide)
Gas lamps that did not reach the courts
Constables could be cornered or lose sight of suspects

cards.front: Name three 'sweated trades' Jewish migrants worked in around Whitechapel.
cards.answer: Tailoring workshops / Cigarette making / Boot finishing

cards.front: Why did the Peabody Estate exclude the very poorest residents of Whitechapel?
cards.answer: Its rents were higher than the rookeries and applicants had to be in regular employment to apply.

cards.front: Why did thousands of Whitechapel's poorest prefer sleeping in alleys or doorways to the casual ward?
cards.answer: The casual ward required bathing, handing over clothes and hours of stone-breaking, a deliberate deterrent that put people off.

cards.front: Why is 200 atmospheres used rather than a much higher pressure in the Haber process?
cards.answer: Very high pressures need expensive, reinforced equipment that is costly and dangerous, so 200 atm balances good yield with practicality.

cards.front: Why is nitrogen essential for plant growth?
cards.answer: Nitrogen is needed to make amino acids, proteins, and DNA in plants.

title: Attack the Block: Aesthetic and Genre Mixing
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Why does Cornish keep the alien indistinct in the first bin-cupboard encounter?
cards.answer: Keeping the creature indistinct and low-contrast creates more spectator unease than a fully lit monster reveal.

cards.front: Why does the swimming-pool flat sequence use one wide deep-focus shot of Moses and the creature together?
cards.answer: It holds both protagonist and threat visible simultaneously, showing they occupy the same unwanted social space in the block.

cards.front: Name the three light colours/sources the lesson gives for the estate's aesthetic across interior and exterior scenes.
cards.answer: Sodium orange street lamps outside / Fluorescent green corridor strip lighting / Cooler blue pool light inside

cards.front: How does Basement Jaxx's contribution combine with Steven Price's score to reflect the film's genre mix?
cards.answer: Basement Jaxx layers grime and electronic percussion over Price's Carpenter-style synth pulses, sounding both horror-indebted and specifically South London.

title: Road to the Six Day War, 1964–67
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What four consequences did the Samu raid have, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: King Hussein humiliated / Palestinians on West Bank rioted / Egypt accused of hiding behind UNEF / All three front-line states pushed closer to war
items: Egypt accused of hiding behind UNEF
All three front-line states pushed closer to war

cards.front: Why did Nasser act on the Soviet warning about Israeli troop movements in May 1967 even though it was false?
cards.answer: He could not risk pan-Arab opinion accusing him of abandoning Syria, even though he couldn't verify the intelligence.

cards.front: Why did the closure of the Straits of Tiran make war more likely in the longer term?
cards.answer: It escalated Arab confidence and pulled Jordan into the 30 May defence pact, making the West Bank a battlefield.

cards.front: Why did the dissolution of the monasteries (1536-40) strengthen Parliament's role in protecting the Protestant settlement?
cards.answer: It redistributed Church land to the gentry, giving them a financial stake in Protestantism and in Parliament defending it.

cards.front: Why could Elizabeth I not simply stop the 'Puritan choir' MPs from raising Church discipline bills?
cards.answer: She could veto the bills themselves but had no power to stop MPs from raising them in the first place.

cards.front: Why is mass conserved in a sealed container during a reaction?
cards.answer: Nothing can enter or leave the system, so no atoms are created or destroyed.

cards.front: How do you find the empirical formula of magnesium oxide experimentally?
cards.answer: Heat magnesium in a crucible, use the mass increase as oxygen mass, divide masses by Ar and simplify the ratio.

title: Health, Disease and the Immune System
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the four non-specific first-line defences the body uses against pathogens.
cards.answer: Skin / Mucus and cilia in respiratory tract / Stomach acid / Tears and saliva
items: Mucus and cilia in respiratory tract

cards.front: Name the four non-communicable diseases the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Cardiovascular disease / Type 2 diabetes / Cancer / Asthma

cards.front: How does the inflammatory response help fight infection at the site of damage?
cards.answer: Damaged cells release chemicals that dilate and make blood vessels more permeable, increasing blood flow and letting white blood cells migrate into the tissue faster.

cards.front: How do antibodies help destroy pathogens once they bind to antigens?
cards.answer: They clump pathogens together for easier destruction, neutralise toxins, and mark pathogens for engulfment by phagocytes.

cards.front: Name the three components of a lever system in the body, arranged around the pivot.
cards.answer: Fulcrum (the joint) / Load (the resistance) / Effort (the muscular force)

cards.front: Why does a first-class lever like the triceps extending the elbow give mechanical advantage or disadvantage depending on arm lengths?
cards.answer: Because the fulcrum sits between load and effort, so whichever arm (effort or load) is longer relative to the other determines the outcome.

cards.front: Why can a javelin thrower accelerate the javelin to high speed with only a short muscular contraction?
cards.answer: The long lever of the arm magnifies the small movement of the muscle into greater speed and range at the hand.

cards.front: Why is heading a football classed as a first-class lever action?
cards.answer: Because the fulcrum, the atlanto-occipital joint, lies between the effort (neck muscles behind it) and the load (face and forehead in front).

cards.front: Why is UK shoe size classed as discrete data even though it is a numerical measurement?
cards.answer: Shoe sizes are a labelling convention with genuine gaps between values (e.g. no size 7.3), unlike a truly continuous measurement.

cards.front: Why can distinguishing the effect of one variable be difficult with multivariate data?
cards.answer: If variables like revision and sleep both increase together, it's hard to tell which one caused the change in outcome.

cards.front: Name the two further types the lesson gives within qualitative data.
cards.answer: Categorical data / Ordinal data

cards.front: Name the two further types the lesson gives within quantitative data.
cards.answer: Discrete data / Continuous data

cards.front: Name the four things Prospero uses magic to control in Act 1, Scene 2, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Creates the storm / Puts Miranda to sleep / Summons and threatens Ariel / Punishes Caliban with cramps

cards.front: Why does Prospero keep interrupting his story to ask Miranda if she is listening?
cards.answer: It reveals his need for control, even over the narrative of his own suffering.

cards.front: Why is the word 'profit' in Caliban's line about learning language considered bitterly ironic?
cards.answer: Because the only profit his colonisation gained him is the ability to curse and voice his dispossession.

cards.front: Why does Prospero eventually have to give up his magic by the end of the play, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because his controlling use of magic isolates him and prevents genuine human connection, so he must trust relationships instead.

cards.front: Name the four explanations contemporaries gave for the cause of the 1665 plague.
cards.answer: Miasma (bad air) / Divine punishment for sin / The comet of 1664 / Unusual conjunctions of the planets

cards.front: Why did the Bills of Mortality probably underestimate the true number of plague deaths in 1665?
cards.answer: Families bribed searchers to record other causes to avoid shutting up, and Dissenters and Jews were buried outside the parish system.

cards.front: How did William Mompesson's response to plague in Eyam differ from the usual reaction to outbreaks?
cards.answer: He persuaded villagers to quarantine themselves voluntarily rather than flee, to avoid infecting neighbouring villages.

cards.front: Why did the practice of shutting up houses in 1665 probably increase deaths?
cards.answer: It kept infected families sealed inside together for forty days, so they often died together rather than escaping infection.

cards.front: Name the three structural causes the lesson gives for the early West being hard to police.
cards.answer: Distance from federal authority / Transient seasonal populations / Absence of women, families and settled property
items: Absence of women, families and settled property

cards.front: What four types of authority does the lesson list as covering law and order in the early West?
cards.answer: Town marshals / Sheriffs / US marshals / Vigilance committees

cards.front: Why did the misconception that 'Westerners were just lawless criminals' fail to explain frontier violence?
cards.answer: The same men were respectable at home; what changed was the absence of sheriffs, courts, jails and property lines restraining behaviour.

cards.front: Why was federal authority so thin in the early West even though marshals existed?
cards.answer: Government was tiny, telegraph and railroad had not reached the frontier, so a marshal with few deputies had to enforce huge territories alone.

title: The 6Cs — Qualities of a Service Practitioner
subject: health-social-care-ocr

cards.front: Name the nine person-centred values that are separate from the 6Cs.
cards.answer: Individuality / Choice / Rights / Independence / Privacy / Dignity / Respect / Partnership / Encouraging decision making

cards.front: Why is naming a 6C as if it were one of the nine person-centred values a mistake in an exam answer?
cards.answer: The 6Cs are the practitioner's own qualities, while the nine values are principles of care delivery for the service user, so they are different lists.

cards.front: Name the six threats to food security given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Increasing birth rate / Changing diets (more meat) / New pests and pathogens / Environmental change / Cost of agricultural inputs / Conflicts

cards.front: Name the four farming techniques the lesson gives for improving food security sustainably.
cards.answer: Biological control / Genetically modified crops / Hydroponics / Reducing food waste

cards.front: Why do rising fuel, fertiliser and seed costs threaten food security?
cards.answer: Rising prices of agricultural inputs affect farmers' ability to produce food.

cards.front: Why is mycoprotein production more efficient than rearing livestock for food?
cards.answer: The fungus grows and is harvested rapidly, and needs less land and water than livestock farming.

cards.front: Why does Papa never complain about the racism he faces?
cards.answer: He chooses dignity and grace over confrontation, representing the resilience of the immigrant experience.

cards.front: How does Mama represent the cost of immigration?
cards.answer: She has sacrificed her homeland, community and cultural context for her family's future, and feels homesick.

cards.front: Name the five key indicators of substance misuse problems given in the lesson.
cards.answer: using more or larger amounts over time / unable to stop despite wanting to / neglecting responsibilities like work or family / needing more for the same effect (tolerance) / withdrawal symptoms when not using
items: using more or larger amounts over time
unable to stop despite wanting to
neglecting responsibilities like work or family
needing more for the same effect (tolerance)

cards.front: What are the UK CMO physical activity guidelines for adults aged 19-64?
cards.answer: 150 minutes moderate activity per week / or 75 minutes vigorous activity / strength-building activity 2+ days per week / reduce extended sitting time

cards.front: Why are lifestyle indicators useful alongside physiological readings like high blood pressure?
cards.answer: They reveal the causes behind abnormal readings, so health professionals can recommend specific, targeted actions for improvement.

cards.front: Why do health professionals ask how many cigarettes a smoker has per day and for how long?
cards.answer: This data helps calculate the level of health risk and how urgently the person needs to quit.

title: The failure of Weimar democracy and Hitler's appointment
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three layers of cause the lesson gives for the failure of Weimar democracy.
cards.answer: Structural causes / Long-term causes / Contingent causes

cards.front: What four structural causes does the lesson give for Weimar's weakness?
cards.answer: Treaty of Versailles / Article 48 emergency provision / Proportional representation causing fragmented Reichstags / Survival of anti-democratic elites

cards.front: Why did Schleicher's attempt to govern as Chancellor in December 1932 fail within four weeks?
cards.answer: His plan to split Strasser's Nazi wing failed, he had no Reichstag majority, and trade unions distrusted an aristocratic general.

cards.front: Why did the Preussenschlag of July 1932 matter for Nazi power?
cards.answer: It destroyed the largest democratic stronghold and removed the SPD-controlled police force resisting Nazi street violence.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives that determine different interest rates.
cards.answer: Risk of the borrower defaulting / Time period of the loan / Competition and the base rate

cards.front: Why do longer-term loans often carry higher interest rates?
cards.answer: The lender's money is tied up for longer and faces greater uncertainty, so they charge more.

cards.front: Why might a very low interest rate fail to stimulate borrowing and investment after a financial crisis?
cards.answer: Banks may become unwilling to lend for fear of bad debts, so low rates don't lead to more borrowing.

cards.front: How does the Bank of England's base rate affect the rates commercial banks offer?
cards.answer: It acts as a benchmark, so when it rises or falls commercial banks typically adjust their mortgage, savings and loan rates accordingly.

cards.front: Name the five methods the lesson gives for reducing unwanted energy transfer from buildings.
cards.answer: Low thermal conductivity materials (foam/fibreglass/trapped air) / Double glazing / Cavity wall insulation / Loft insulation / Reflective surfaces to reduce radiation

cards.front: Name the three steps the lesson gives for measuring the density of a liquid.
cards.answer: Place measuring cylinder on balance and zero it / Pour in the liquid and read mass and volume / Use ρ = m/V
items: Place measuring cylinder on balance and zero it
Pour in the liquid and read mass and volume

cards.front: Why does increasing the temperature of a gas at constant volume increase its pressure?
cards.answer: Particles gain kinetic energy and move faster, hitting the walls more frequently and with greater force.

cards.front: Why does heating a substance not always raise its temperature?
cards.answer: If the substance is changing state, the energy is used to break bonds between particles instead of raising temperature.

title: The Berlin Blockade, Airlift and the Birth of NATO
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the twelve countries that signed the North Atlantic Treaty in 1949.
cards.answer: USA / Canada / Britain / France / Italy / Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Portugal
items: Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Portugal

cards.front: Why did Stalin blockade Berlin in 1948?
cards.answer: He saw the new Western currency as building a working West German economy that would draw East Germans toward the Western system, so he cut off access to force the West out.

cards.front: How did the Berlin Blockade lead to the permanent division of Germany?
cards.answer: Once Stalin tried to starve out West Berlin, no Western leader would trust the Soviet zone, so the Western zones became West Germany and the Soviet zone became East Germany.

title: Terror, the Three and Five Antis, and the Hundred Flowers, 1951-57
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three tools/methods the CCP used during these mass campaigns of 1950-57.
cards.answer: public denunciation / mass meetings / struggle sessions

cards.front: Why did local cadres end up denouncing large numbers of people during the 1950-52 terror campaign?
cards.answer: Local cadres met quotas, as each county was expected to identify a set proportion of 'enemies'.

cards.front: Why might the early stages of the Hundred Flowers Campaign have been a genuine reform rather than a trap, according to Dikötter and Spence?
cards.answer: Mao expected only mild criticism, was alarmed by the volume received, and reframed it as a trap afterwards.

cards.front: How did the Five Antis Campaign change China's economy by 1956?
cards.answer: Almost all private industry and commerce had been absorbed into the state or into joint state-private enterprises.

title: Racial policy: Nazi treatment of the Jews to 1939
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five stages of escalating persecution of Jews the lesson traces from 1933 to 1938.
cards.answer: 1933 boycott of Jewish businesses / Professional exclusions from jobs / Nuremberg Laws (legal racial separation) / Aryanisation of businesses / Kristallnacht violence

cards.front: Why did the 1933 boycott of Jewish businesses only last one day?
cards.answer: Because of international criticism and because many Germans did not observe it.

cards.front: Why did the international community's reaction to Kristallnacht encourage further Nazi persecution?
cards.answer: Because it produced only expressions of horror with no sanctions or military threat, signalling the regime could act with impunity.

cards.front: How did Hitler's ideas in Mein Kampf justify Nazi persecution of Jews?
cards.answer: He argued Jews were a separate, inferior race responsible for Germany's 1918 defeat and the evils of communism and capitalism.

cards.front: The lesson gives four recognised routes into manumission. Name all four.
cards.answer: Being included in the census as free / Being freed by a magistrate (manumissio iusta) / Being named as free in an owner's will / Being declared free before the owner's friends
items: Being included in the census as free
Being freed by a magistrate (manumissio iusta)
Being named as free in an owner's will
Being declared free before the owner's friends

cards.front: Why did service to the Roman state as a public slave sometimes lead to freedom faster than private slavery?
cards.answer: Public slaves like Scipio's captured workers were promised freedom if they actively helped provide equipment for war.

cards.front: Why did King Philip of Macedon praise the Romans for their manumission system, and where was he wrong?
cards.answer: He praised them for making slaves citizens who could hold important positions, but freedmen could not actually hold public office.

title: Glaciated Uplands: Economic Activity, Conflict & Tourism
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the four main economic activities in glaciated uplands like the Lake District.
cards.answer: Tourism / Farming / Forestry / Quarrying

cards.front: Name the three types of environmental impact of tourism listed for the Lake District.
cards.answer: Footpath erosion / Water pollution from boats and camping / Disturbance of ground-nesting birds
items: Water pollution from boats and camping

cards.front: Why does sheep grazing on the Lake District fells matter for tourism?
cards.answer: Sheep grazing keeps the fell slopes open; without it they would revert to scrub and woodland, losing the scenery tourists visit for.

cards.front: Why did mid-20th century conifer plantations in the Lake District cause controversy?
cards.answer: Non-native Sitka spruce was planted in geometrical blocks, which was seen as visually intrusive and damaging to biodiversity.

title: Interpreting Data on Participation and Performance
subject: physical-education-aqa

cards.front: Name the four steps of the method for interpreting data in an exam question.
cards.answer: Read / Compare / Calculate / Explain

cards.front: Name the four main formats for presenting data given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Table / Bar chart / Line graph / Pie chart

cards.front: Why does simply copying numbers from a table or graph fail to earn marks on an interpret-data question?
cards.answer: Because reading off figures shows the data but does not compare, calculate or explain what the pattern means.

cards.front: Why must both axes on a bar chart or line graph always be labelled?
cards.answer: So the variable being measured and its unit are clear, showing what the category and value axes represent.

cards.front: Name the three pillars of Stresemann's 1923-24 economic recovery.
cards.answer: Ending passive resistance in the Ruhr / Replacing the mark with the Rentenmark / Negotiating the Dawes Plan for US loans
items: Ending passive resistance in the Ruhr
Replacing the mark with the Rentenmark
Negotiating the Dawes Plan for US loans

cards.front: Name four terms Germany was forced to accept in the Treaty of Versailles.
cards.answer: Accept sole war guilt / Pay reparations of 132 billion gold marks / Lose 13% of territory and 10% of population / Reduce army to 100,000 men
items: Pay reparations of 132 billion gold marks
Lose 13% of territory and 10% of population

cards.front: Why did hyperinflation in 1923 destroy trust in the Weimar Republic?
cards.answer: It wiped out savings and ruined people on fixed incomes, generating deep distrust of democracy's ability to manage the economy.

cards.front: Why did the Wall Street Crash of 1929 destroy Weimar democracy's stability?
cards.answer: American banks recalled loans to Germany, causing businesses to collapse and unemployment to soar, destroying the fragile economic consensus.

cards.front: Name the four items offered before a shrine or Buddha image during puja.
cards.answer: Flowers / Candles or lamps / Incense / Food and water

cards.front: Name the three Tibetan Buddhist devotional practices mentioned alongside malas.
cards.answer: Prostrations / Mandala offerings / Prayer wheels

cards.front: Why do Buddhists bow during puja?
cards.answer: Bowing is an act of respect for the Buddha as teacher, cultivating humility and reducing pride, not worship of a god.

cards.front: Why is Samatha meditation seen as a foundation for other types of meditation?
cards.answer: It calms and steadies the mind through concentration, and without this tranquillity insight meditation is difficult to develop.

title: Learning Theories: Mindset and Learning Styles
subject: psychology-ocr

cards.front: Why do fixed-mindset learners avoid challenges and give up when work gets difficult?
cards.answer: Because failure feels like proof of a permanent limit, threatening their belief that ability is fixed.

cards.front: Why can praising a child for being 'clever' backfire, according to Dweck?
cards.answer: It signals intelligence is fixed and must be protected, making the child avoid risky, difficult work.

cards.front: What did Blackwell et al. (2007) find happened to fixed-mindset students' maths grades over the transition to secondary school?
cards.answer: Their achievement levelled off into a flat trajectory over that period.

cards.front: According to Willingham, why does teaching for meaning beat teaching for style?
cards.answer: Information connected to what a learner already understands is remembered far better than information merely matched to their preferred format.

cards.front: Name the three lean techniques beyond JIT that the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Kaizen / 5S / Cell production

cards.front: What do the five S's stand for in the 5S lean technique?
cards.answer: Sort / Set / Shine / Standardise / Sustain

cards.front: How does lean production help stop faulty cars being made at Toyota's Burnaston plant?
cards.answer: Workers can stop the line if they spot a defect, preventing faulty cars travelling further down the process.

cards.front: Why is flow production's set-up cost very high compared to its running cost?
cards.answer: It needs a continuous assembly line built for huge standardised volumes before any low-cost units can be made.

title: Passchendaele and the Tactical Learning Curve
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the six combined-arms tactics the BEF was using by the end of 1917.
cards.answer: Predicted artillery fire / Sound-ranging / Aerial reconnaissance / Platoon-level infantry organisation / Mass tank attacks / More accurate creeping barrage

cards.front: Why was aerial photography important for artillery attacks by 1917?
cards.answer: It produced detailed trench maps that let artillery fire accurately without registering shots in advance and giving away the attack.

cards.front: Name the five steps the lesson gives for drawing a geological cross-section from map data.
cards.answer: Draw a line along the section / Mark where boundaries cross the line / Read dip angle and direction at symbols / Project each boundary down at that dip angle / Connect projected boundaries between units
items: Draw a line along the section
Mark where boundaries cross the line
Read dip angle and direction at symbols
Project each boundary down at that dip angle

cards.front: Why did the unconformity at Siccar Point convince James Hutton the Earth was immeasurably old?
cards.answer: The nearly 65-million-year gap between the tilted and horizontal beds showed far more time had passed than any biblical timescale allowed.

cards.front: Name the three market data signals the lesson gives that tell a business when the marketing mix needs to change.
cards.answer: Changes in demand / Changes in market share / Effect of promotion on sales

cards.front: Why did the coffee chain's sales settle at £210,000 a week after its Instagram campaign ended, rather than dropping back to £200,000?
cards.answer: The campaign created a small lasting lift in sales even after the spending stopped.

cards.front: Why did Debenhams' marketing mix stop being integrated?
cards.answer: Its place (mainly high-street stores) fell behind as rivals invested in e-commerce, so only three Ps kept moving forward.

cards.front: Why would it be a problem if ASOS ran TV adverts aimed at over-60s while keeping its other Ps the same?
cards.answer: The promotion channel would not match the target customer the other three Ps were designed for, breaking the mix.

cards.front: Name the three components in a series circuit whose resistance and voltage give the equipment needed for the I-V characteristic practical, plus what the voltmeter connects across.
cards.answer: Variable resistor in series / Ammeter in series / Power supply / Voltmeter connected in parallel across the component
items: Voltmeter connected in parallel across the component

cards.front: Why does the resistor with the larger resistance get a bigger share of the voltage in a series circuit?
cards.answer: Because voltage is shared between components in proportion to their resistance, so a larger resistance takes a greater share.

title: Early modern crime: heresy, treason and witchcraft
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three new categories of crime that defined the early modern period.
cards.answer: Heresy / Vagabondage / Witchcraft

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives for the surge in English witchcraft prosecutions.
cards.answer: Religious anxiety after the Reformation / Fear of social disorder and bad harvests / The printing press spreading sensational stories / James I's personal interest via Daemonologie
items: Fear of social disorder and bad harvests
The printing press spreading sensational stories
James I's personal interest via Daemonologie

cards.front: Why did the dissolution of the monasteries (1536–41) contribute to the rise in vagabondage?
cards.answer: It closed the largest providers of poor relief almost overnight, leaving more people homeless and jobless.

cards.front: Why were most people accused of witchcraft poor, elderly, single women?
cards.answer: They were the people most easily suspected by their neighbours.

cards.front: What three factors does personal space vary with, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Culture / Gender / Social status

cards.front: Why does eye contact matter for regulating conversation?
cards.answer: We use gaze to signal when we are ready to speak, want the other to continue, or are handing over our turn.

cards.front: Why do people from different cultures read the eyes or mouth differently when judging emotion, according to Yuki?
cards.answer: If NVC were entirely innate everyone would read the same features the same way, so the difference shows cultural learning shapes interpretation.

cards.front: Name the three character pairings the lesson gives to show Shakespeare's deliberate contrasts.
cards.answer: Beatrice and Hero / Benedick and Claudio / Don Pedro and Don John

cards.front: The lesson lists three stages of Beatrice's language across the play — what are they?
cards.answer: Witty prose in Acts 1-2 / Dignified verse after the gulling / Raw, violent anger in Act 4

cards.front: Why does the lesson say Hero stays almost silent during the church scene?
cards.answer: Because patriarchy silences women, giving her no language to defend herself against the accusation.

cards.front: Why does the lesson say Benedick's failed love poem in Act 5 Scene 2 is endearing rather than embarrassing?
cards.answer: Because it shows a prose speaker stepping outside his comfort zone into verse, proving his love is genuine even though clumsy.

title: Peterloo, the Great Reform Act and Chartism, 1819-1858
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the six demands of the People's Charter (1838).
cards.answer: Votes for all adult men / Secret ballots / Equal-sized constituencies / Paid MPs / No property qualification for MPs / Annual parliaments

cards.front: What three pressures forced parliamentary reform onto the agenda by the late 1820s/early 1830s, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Catholic Emancipation in 1829 / July Revolution in France, 1830 / Riots in Bristol, Nottingham and Derby, 1831
items: Riots in Bristol, Nottingham and Derby, 1831

cards.front: Why did the government use repression rather than reform after Peterloo in 1819?
cards.answer: The government was terrified of a French-style revolution, so it pushed through the Six Acts to restrict radical activity instead of conceding reform.

cards.front: Why did the 1832 Reform Act lead working-class radicals to form Chartism?
cards.answer: The Act only gave the vote to the middle class, betraying working men who had marched and petitioned but remained excluded.

cards.front: Name six situations the lesson gives when parents should seek medical attention for a sick child.
cards.answer: High fever not responding to paracetamol/ibuprofen / Under three months with any fever / Difficulty breathing / Unusually pale, limp or unresponsive / Rash or persistent vomiting / Illness lasting longer than expected
items: High fever not responding to paracetamol/ibuprofen
Under three months with any fever

cards.front: Why does a non-blanching rash appear in meningococcal disease?
cards.answer: It is caused by bleeding under the skin from septicaemia, which is why it does not fade under pressure.

cards.front: Why can mumps cause orchitis?
cards.answer: Mumps causes swelling of the parotid glands and can also cause testicular swelling (orchitis) in post-pubertal males.

cards.front: The lesson names seven key attributes of Allah among the 99 names — what are they?
cards.answer: Tawhid (Oneness) / Omnipotent (Al-Qadir) / Benevolent / Fair and Just (Al-'Adl) / Transcendent / Immanent

cards.front: Why do Muslims regard polytheistic religions as committing shirk, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because dividing divine power and worship among several beings contradicts the reality of Allah's unique oneness.

title: Contemporary Music Videos: Stormzy and Justin Bieber
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the two well-known media texts that Superheroes references through intertextuality.
cards.answer: Toy Story (Buzz Lightyear carrying Woody) / The Matrix (Neo's telekinetic powers)

cards.front: Name the three ways Superheroes challenges stereotypes about Black British family and identity, according to the lesson's key fact.
cards.answer: Rashford shirt challenges football stereotypes / father doing his daughter's hair challenges fatherhood stereotypes / protest scene reflects Black Lives Matter and Covid-19
items: father doing his daughter's hair challenges fatherhood stereotypes
protest scene reflects Black Lives Matter and Covid-19

cards.front: Why does Superheroes use a soft pink sky and gold highlights on the bones of characters?
cards.answer: The pink sky suggests optimism, while gold highlights reflect the song's lyrics about courage and inner strength.

cards.front: Why did the director choose Adidas tracksuit costume for the boy in Superheroes?
cards.answer: To echo the style of Stormzy's earlier Sounds of the Skeng video, giving the character authenticity for a young audience.

title: Solo Artists 1990 to Now: Producers, Studio Technology and the Streaming Era
subject: music-ocr

cards.front: Name the four studio techniques the lesson gives as examples of technology used as a compositional tool.
cards.answer: Programmed beats / Sampling / Layering / Pitch correction

cards.front: What three steps does the lesson recommend for answering exam questions on any strand of pop?
cards.answer: Name the convention you can hear / place it in its decade or genre / give specific musical evidence from the excerpt
items: Place it in its decade or genre

cards.front: Why did the solo artist's image become as important as the music itself from the 1990s onwards?
cards.answer: Image, music videos and choreography became central to marketing, so musical decisions were often made with visual performance and media impact in mind.

cards.front: How does pitch correction technology affect a vocal by the 2000s?
cards.answer: It adjusts a vocal so it sits perfectly in tune, and can also be used deliberately to create a robotic vocal timbre.

title: Formation of Planetary Systems and Gravitational Forces
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives three effects of tidal forces in the Solar System. Name them.
cards.answer: Ring systems / Tidal heating / Synchronous rotation

cards.front: Name the two impact effects the lesson describes on planets' axial tilt or spin.
cards.answer: Uranus knocked onto its side / Venus spinning retrograde

cards.front: Why does the Moon always show the same face to Earth?
cards.answer: Earth's tidal forces gradually slowed the Moon's rotation until it matched its orbital period, causing synchronous rotation.

cards.front: Why has Mars lost most of its original atmosphere over billions of years?
cards.answer: Mars has a relatively low escape velocity (5.0 km/s), so gas molecules exceeding this speed gradually escaped into space over geological time.

cards.front: Name the four attempted overthrows of the Weimar Republic between 1919 and 1923.
cards.answer: Spartacist uprising, January 1919 / Kapp Putsch, March 1920 / Erzberger assassination, 1921 / Munich Putsch, November 1923

cards.front: Why did the Spartacist uprising of January 1919 fail?
cards.answer: It lacked majority support, the SPD opposed it, and the far smaller Spartacist force was crushed by the well-armed Freikorps.

cards.front: How did Hitler's trial after the Munich Putsch help him despite his defeat?
cards.answer: A sympathetic judge let him give long speeches reported nationally, giving him a platform and a light sentence.

cards.front: Why did the army refuse to stop the Kapp Putsch in 1920?
cards.answer: General von Seeckt said the army would not fire on fellow soldiers, so it refused to act against the Ehrhardt Brigade.

cards.front: Name the ten forms of media that use sound creation given in the lesson.
cards.answer: radio broadcasts / movies / TV shows / video games / advertisements / jingles / podcasts / animations / theatre / installations

cards.front: Why must dialogue sometimes be re-recorded using ADR?
cards.answer: Because if on-set recording is unusable, actors re-record their lines in a studio to replace it.

cards.front: What three refusals show Jane Eyre asserting her independence in the novel?
cards.answer: Refuses to become Rochester's mistress / Refuses St John Rivers's loveless proposal / Only marries Rochester as his equal
items: Refuses St John Rivers's loveless proposal
Only marries Rochester as his equal

cards.front: What features make Thornfield Hall a classic Gothic setting?
cards.answer: Grand and isolated / Locked rooms / Mysterious laughter from the attic / A fire in Rochester's bed / A secret that threatens everyone

cards.front: Why does Jane refuse to become Rochester's mistress even though she loves him?
cards.answer: Because it would mean sacrificing her moral autonomy for comfort, which she will not accept.

cards.front: How does Jane's inheritance let her return to Rochester out of love rather than need?
cards.answer: Her £20,000 inheritance gives her financial independence, so she chooses to return out of love, not economic necessity.

title: Beliefs about Death and the Afterlife
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three Christian afterlife beliefs given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Heaven / Hell / Purgatory

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say Islamic burial involves, reflecting belief in akhirah?
cards.answer: Body washed and shrouded / Buried promptly / Placed facing Makkah

cards.front: Why is Jewish burial traditionally preferred over cremation?
cards.answer: Because it expresses the hope of resurrection reflected in Jewish belief about the afterlife.

cards.front: How does the Buddhist candle-flame analogy explain rebirth without a fixed soul?
cards.answer: Something is transmitted from one life to the next, but it is neither the same flame nor a completely different one, showing kamma carries forward without an unchanging soul.

title: Vietnam protests, Great Society and Nixon's America
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the five key pieces of Great Society legislation the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Medicare and Medicaid / Elementary and Secondary Education Act / Voting Rights Act / Housing Act / Immigration and Nationality Act

cards.front: What three cover-up actions did Nixon take during Watergate, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Paying hush money / Ordering the CIA to obstruct FBI investigations / Firing the special prosecutor
items: Ordering the CIA to obstruct FBI investigations

cards.front: Why did Johnson announce in March 1968 that he would not seek re-election?
cards.answer: The Tet Offensive destroyed his war claims and he faced a serious challenge in his own party's primaries.

cards.front: Why did Nixon's Family Assistance Plan fail to become law?
cards.answer: Conservatives thought it too generous while liberals thought it too stingy and feared it would undermine union wages.

cards.front: What four conditions must line up for a tropical cyclone to form?
cards.answer: Sea-surface temperature above 26.5°C / Warm ocean air rising rapidly / Low vertical wind shear / Coriolis effect giving spin

cards.front: What four ways can wealthier countries prepare for tropical cyclones, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Hurricane-resistant building codes / Early-warning satellite systems / Mass-evacuation transport networks / Well-equipped emergency services

cards.front: Why is the eye of a tropical cyclone eerily calm?
cards.answer: Air is sinking in the eye, warming by compression, so cloud evaporates and skies briefly clear.

cards.front: Why did poorer Black neighbourhoods in New Orleans struggle to evacuate before Hurricane Katrina?
cards.answer: They had less car ownership, making evacuation before the storm much harder.

cards.front: Why does Brontë make Jane wander the moors starving and destitute after leaving Thornfield?
cards.answer: To strip Jane of everything so Brontë can test whether her principles can sustain her with nothing else.

cards.front: How does St John Rivers differ from Brocklehurst as a religious character?
cards.answer: St John genuinely practises his ascetic faith, unlike the hypocritical Brocklehurst, but his devotion is life-denying.

title: Moments, Levers, Gears and Momentum Changes
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name three examples of levers given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Crowbar / Wheelbarrow / Scissors

cards.front: Name four car safety features that reduce collision force, given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Crumple zones / Seat belts / Airbags / Cycle helmets

cards.front: Why does a small gear driving a large gear increase the turning moment?
cards.answer: The larger gear has a bigger radius, so the force acts at a greater distance from the axle.

cards.front: In an explosion where objects start at rest, why do they move in opposite directions with equal and opposite momenta?
cards.answer: Because total momentum before the explosion is zero, so momentum must stay zero after, requiring equal opposite momenta.

title: Stellar Evolution: Birth, Life and Death of Stars
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six stages in the lifecycle of a Sun-like (low-mass) star, in order.
cards.answer: Nebula / Protostar / Main-sequence star / Red giant / Planetary nebula / White dwarf

cards.front: Name the two pieces of evidence for black holes given, besides X-ray binaries.
cards.answer: Gravitational lensing / Supermassive black holes at galaxy centres
items: Supermassive black holes at galaxy centres

cards.front: Why does a red giant form once hydrogen runs out in a Sun-like star's core?
cards.answer: Core fusion stops so the core contracts and heats under gravity, while the outer layers expand and cool from shell fusion around it.

cards.front: Why does a massive star's core collapse into a black hole rather than a neutron star?
cards.answer: If the collapsing core exceeds about 3 solar masses, even neutron degeneracy pressure cannot resist gravity, so it collapses into a black hole.

cards.front: Name the five main formation routes for minerals given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Crystallisation from a melt / Metamorphic recrystallisation / Evaporation / Precipitation from pore waters / Deposition from hydrothermal fluids

cards.front: Name the three temperature zones of hydrothermal fluids and what each deposits.
cards.answer: High temperature deposits gold and tungsten / Mid temperature deposits copper and lead sulphides / Coolest deposits carbonates
items: High temperature deposits gold and tungsten
Mid temperature deposits copper and lead sulphides

cards.front: Why do minerals like chlorite, mica and garnet appear in a mudstone that has undergone deep regional metamorphism?
cards.answer: Increasing temperature and pressure make original clay minerals break down and atoms reorganise into new minerals stable under the new conditions.

cards.front: Why is a silica-cemented sandstone harder and less permeable than a calcite-cemented one?
cards.answer: The type of cement precipitated from pore waters affects rock strength and permeability, and silica cement binds grains more strongly than calcite.

title: Telescopes Across the Spectrum and in Space
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the two main atmospheric windows that let radiation reach ground level.
cards.answer: Optical window (visible light) / Radio window (1 mm to 10 m)

cards.front: What four things does infrared astronomy reveal, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Molecular clouds and protostars hidden by dust / Starburst galaxies emitting mainly infrared / Thermal glow of brown dwarfs / Thermal glow of exoplanets
items: Molecular clouds and protostars hidden by dust

cards.front: Why is dust largely transparent to infrared telescopes but blocks visible light?
cards.answer: Dust absorbs visible light but is largely transparent in infrared, letting infrared telescopes see through it.

cards.front: Why do X-ray telescopes use grazing-incidence mirrors instead of normal mirrors?
cards.answer: X-rays only bounce off mirrors at very shallow angles, so mirrors must be angled to reflect them.

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives that affect the rate of decomposition.
cards.answer: Temperature / Moisture / Oxygen / Surface area

cards.front: Name the three things gardeners do when composting to speed up decomposition.
cards.answer: Shred material / Turn compost heaps regularly / Keep it moist and warm

cards.front: Why does rising atmospheric CO2 cause ocean acidification?
cards.answer: Oceans act as a carbon sink, dissolving CO2 from the atmosphere, and rising CO2 levels increase ocean acidity.

cards.front: Why do waterlogged landfill sites produce methane instead of CO2?
cards.answer: Without oxygen, decomposition occurs anaerobically, which is slower and produces methane rather than CO2.

cards.front: Name the four stages covered by a life cycle assessment (LCA).
cards.answer: Raw material extraction / Manufacture and transportation / Use by the consumer / Disposal or recycling

cards.front: Why should measurements be checked regularly during manufacture rather than only at the end?
cards.answer: So small errors are spotted and corrected before they build up into large errors that cannot be fixed later.

cards.front: Why is it better to explain why a material or tool was chosen rather than just listing what was used?
cards.answer: Justifying the choice shows more understanding and is what lifts the quality of the answer.

cards.front: How is accuracy different from quality when checking a finished prototype?
cards.answer: Accuracy is how closely it matches the working drawing and specification, while quality also includes finish, assembly and how well it performs.

cards.front: Why does Macbeth order the murder of Macduff's family even though Macduff has already fled?
cards.answer: Emboldened by false confidence from the prophecies, Macbeth acts on impulsive cruelty with no strategic purpose.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare stage the killing of Lady Macduff's young son on stage?
cards.answer: To maximise audience horror and destroy remaining sympathy for Macbeth, so the audience supports Malcolm and Macduff's overthrow.

cards.front: Name the six key themes of A Christmas Carol identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Redemption / Social responsibility / Family / Isolation / Poverty / The spirit of Christmas

cards.front: What five items should a 5-minute extract-question plan list?
cards.answer: Extract thesis / Two methods from the extract / Two supporting moments from other staves / Context strand / Closing argument
items: Two supporting moments from other staves

cards.front: Why is embedding a short quotation inside your own sentence stronger than dropping in a long block quote?
cards.answer: It lets you pick a single word or short phrase and analyse it closely, rather than just describing what is said.

cards.front: Why does Dickens present Scrooge's loneliness as a self-imposed penalty?
cards.answer: Because his isolation, shown through the word "solitary", is a punishment he brought on himself through his own chosen behaviour.

title: Analysing Performers: Vocal and Physical Choices
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Why does a sudden drop in volume followed by a shout create impact for an audience?
cards.answer: Dropping to near-inaudible draws the audience forward physically, so a sudden shout after quiet becomes a physical shock.

cards.front: Why does a performer freezing mid-action in a tableau grab audience focus?
cards.answer: Stillness contrasts with surrounding chaotic movement, so every audience member's eye is drawn immediately to the frozen performer.

cards.front: Name the three broad categories of contraception methods described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Barrier methods / Hormonal methods / Natural/other methods

cards.front: Name the four female causes of infertility the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Problems with ovulation e.g. PCOS / Blocked or damaged fallopian tubes / Endometriosis / Age-related decline in egg quality

cards.front: Why does copper in the IUD prevent pregnancy?
cards.answer: Copper ions are toxic to sperm.

cards.front: Why does sickle cell disease cause pain and anaemia?
cards.answer: A mutation in the haemoglobin gene produces abnormally shaped red blood cells that block blood vessels.

cards.front: Name the four areas of life the lesson says Shari'ah covers.
cards.answer: Worship (ibadat) / Relationships and family (muamalat) / Criminal law (uqubat) / Social ethics

cards.front: Give three subtle forms of shirk the lesson describes, beyond idol worship.
cards.answer: Trusting or fearing humans over Allah / Following desires as if divine commands / Giving devotion owed to Allah to humans / Hidden shirk: acting for human approval
items: Trusting or fearing humans over Allah
Following desires as if divine commands
Giving devotion owed to Allah to humans
Hidden shirk: acting for human approval

cards.front: Why does the golden calf story in Surah 7:148-150 count as shirk?
cards.answer: The Israelites worshipped a created, speechless idol that could not guide or help them, instead of the invisible eternal God.

cards.front: Why do atheists and Humanists say laws should not come from Shari'ah?
cards.answer: They argue laws should come from democratic consent and human reason, not divine revelation, and question if God's command alone justifies law.

cards.front: Name the five market segmentation bases named in the specification.
cards.answer: Age / Gender / Income / Location / Lifestyle

cards.front: Why does a business use market segmentation instead of trying to please every customer?
cards.answer: Trying to be cheapest, most luxurious, most ethical and most convenient at once means being none of them well.

cards.front: Why do businesses often combine more than one segmentation base, as Boots does?
cards.answer: Combining bases like age, gender, income and location gives a sharper, more detailed picture of the customer than one base alone.

cards.front: How can segmentation let a smaller firm compete with bigger businesses?
cards.answer: By owning one tight segment rather than fighting across the whole market against giants.

title: Characters and Relationships: Proctor, Abigail, Elizabeth
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the three men through whom Miller shows Abigail's only routes to power in Salem.
cards.answer: Parris (her uncle and protector) / Proctor (her former lover) / The court

cards.front: Why does Judge Danforth refuse to admit the trials are unjust?
cards.answer: He has already signed death warrants, so admitting error would mean admitting he has murdered innocent people.

cards.front: Why does Miller make Rebecca Nurse one of the accused?
cards.answer: Her piety and community standing make her the most improbable of the accused, making the court's injustice most damning.

title: The Statistical Enquiry Cycle: Reviewing the Whole Investigation
subject: statistics-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five stages of the Statistical Enquiry Cycle in order.
cards.answer: Planning / Sourcing Data / Processing and Presenting Data / Interpreting Results / Communicating Findings and Evaluating

cards.front: Name the three parts a full-mark evaluation point must have.
cards.answer: Identify the weakness at a named stage / Explain why it undermines the conclusion / Suggest a specific improvement
items: Identify the weakness at a named stage
Explain why it undermines the conclusion

cards.front: Why does a bigger symbol in a pictogram mislead a reader, even if the key is correct?
cards.answer: Because a reader may judge the area of the symbol rather than reading the key, making the value look bigger than it is.

cards.front: Why can't a vague hypothesis be tested properly during planning?
cards.answer: Because it has no measurable variables, so no data collection method can confirm or reject it.

title: Case Study: Development in an Emerging Country (India)
subject: geography-edexcel-b

cards.front: Name the four megacities the lesson gives for India and their roles.
cards.answer: Mumbai - financial / Delhi - political / Bengaluru - IT / Kolkata - cultural-historical

cards.front: Name the four countries the lesson gives as India's largest sources of FDI.
cards.answer: Singapore / USA / Mauritius / Japan

cards.front: Why has India's rural-urban migration happened as the economy has grown?
