cards.answer: He trusts Iago absolutely / It touches his insecurities about being an outsider / Jealousy has already corrupted his judgment
items: It touches his insecurities about being an outsider
Jealousy has already corrupted his judgment

cards.front: Why is Act 3 Scene 3 called the play's pivotal scene?
cards.answer: It is the longest scene in the play, where Iago plants suspicion through insinuation and turns Othello against Desdemona.

cards.front: How does Iago use insinuation rather than direct accusation to provoke Othello in Act 3 Scene 3?
cards.answer: He says little, feigns reluctance to speak, and echoes Othello's own words back as suspicious questions, making Othello imagine the worst.

cards.front: Name the four physical changes the lesson gives for pregnancy in adulthood.
cards.answer: Blood volume increases 40-50% / Uterus expands from pear-size to full-term / Weight increases by 10-12 kg / Major hormonal and cardiovascular changes
items: Uterus expands from pear-size to full-term

cards.front: Name the three cardiovascular and respiratory changes the lesson gives for later adulthood.
cards.answer: Heart muscle weakens slightly / Blood vessels lose elasticity / Lung capacity reduces

cards.front: Why can delays in fine motor development in childhood lead to a referral to an occupational therapist?
cards.answer: Delays in fine motor development can indicate conditions such as dyspraxia, prompting practitioners to refer the child.

cards.front: Why do older adults tire more quickly with exertion?
cards.answer: The heart muscle weakens slightly, blood vessels lose elasticity, and lung capacity reduces, lowering stamina.

title: Factors Affecting Food Choice & Sensory Evaluation
subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four control factors needed to set up a proper sensory test, for full marks.
cards.answer: Defined method (preference, ranking or profiling) / Samples coded to prevent bias / Controlled environment (no competing aromas, consistent lighting, palate-cleansing water) / Results recorded on a standard proforma
items: Controlled environment (no competing aromas, consistent lighting, palate-cleansing water)
Results recorded on a standard proforma

cards.front: Name the four senses, beyond taste and smell, involved in evaluating food.
cards.answer: Texture (mechanoreceptors) / Sound / Appearance / Taste and smell combine to give flavour
items: Taste and smell combine to give flavour

cards.front: Why is 'I asked my friends if they liked it' not valid sensory evaluation?
cards.answer: It describes informal opinion, without a defined method, coded samples, controlled environment or standard recording, so bias distorts results.

cards.front: Why might a working parent choose a ready meal over a slow-cooked stew, even knowing the stew is more nutritious?
cards.answer: Time and lifestyle pressures, such as arriving home late, make convenience more important than nutritional value at that moment.

cards.front: Name the three overlapping groups that made up the Iraqi insurgency.
cards.answer: Sunni Ba'athist remnants / Foreign jihadists (al-Qaeda in Iraq) / Shia militias linked to Iran

cards.front: Name the two attacks the lesson cites as global blowback from the Iraq War, before the 2007 surge.
cards.answer: 2004 Madrid train bombings / 2005 London bombings (7/7)

cards.front: How did the CPA's May 2003 orders help create the insurgency?
cards.answer: De-Ba'athification and disbanding the army removed a generation of Sunni Arabs from public life, creating a pool of trained, humiliated recruits.

cards.front: Why did the 2007 surge succeed in reducing civilian deaths?
cards.answer: It paired extra troops with a counter-insurgency doctrine protecting civilians, while the Sunni Awakening turned Anbar tribes against al-Qaeda in Iraq.

title: The Atom Bomb, Ideologies, and the Iron Curtain
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the six areas the Red Army occupied by the end of 1945, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Poland / Hungary / Romania / Bulgaria / Eastern Germany / Parts of Czechoslovakia and Austria

cards.front: What four features did the lesson give for US-style capitalism and liberal democracy?
cards.answer: Free elections / Multi-party politics / Freedom of the press / Competing private businesses

cards.front: Why did the Yalta promise of free elections in Eastern Europe end up broken by 1948?
cards.answer: Elections between 1945 and 1948 were rigged or manipulated so local communist parties took power in every Soviet-occupied state.

cards.front: Why did Stalin barely react when Truman mentioned the new weapon at Potsdam?
cards.answer: Soviet intelligence had already penetrated the Manhattan Project years earlier, so Stalin already knew the bomb existed.

title: Editing: Cuts, Continuity, Pace and Visual Effects
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Why does breaking the 180-degree rule disorient the spectator?
cards.answer: Characters appear to have switched sides of the frame without moving, breaking the spectator's spatial orientation.

cards.front: How does cross-cutting build tension in a chase-or-rescue sequence?
cards.answer: Cutting faster between pursuer and escaper as the strands converge makes the spectator experience mounting tension neither strand alone creates.

title: Circuits: Current, Resistance and Potential Difference
subject: separate-sciences

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives that affect the resistance of a wire.
cards.answer: Length of the wire / Cross-sectional area / Material / Temperature

cards.front: In a series circuit, name the three rules the lesson gives for current, potential difference and resistance.
cards.answer: Current is the same everywhere / Potential difference is shared between components / Total resistance equals sum of resistances
items: Potential difference is shared between components
Total resistance equals sum of resistances

cards.front: Why does the whole circuit stop working if one bulb fails in an old set of series-connected Christmas lights?
cards.answer: Series circuits have only one path for current, so a broken component breaks the whole current path.

cards.front: Why are household appliances connected in parallel rather than in series?
cards.answer: In parallel each branch gets the full supply voltage, so each appliance gets 230V regardless of other appliances.

cards.front: Name six types of grave goods found in the shaft graves of Grave Circle A.
cards.answer: Gold death masks / Inlaid bronze daggers and swords / Amber beads/jewellery / Rock crystal drinking vessels / Silver cups / Gold animal-head drinking cups (rhytons)

cards.front: Why does the scale of the Treasury of Atreus suggest greater royal power than the earlier shaft graves?
cards.answer: Building it required moving enormous stone blocks and organising many workers over a long time, showing far greater resources and authority than earlier shaft-grave kings.

cards.front: Why did desktop 3D printing spread to schools and hobbyists even though consumers hadn't asked for it?
cards.answer: It was technology push — FDM was developed for industrial prototyping, then matured and became cheaper, pushing into new markets.

cards.front: Why can legislation force designers to innovate even without consumer demand?
cards.answer: Legislation sets minimum standards, like safety or energy efficiency rules, that products must legally meet regardless of consumer preference.

cards.front: How does modular electronics design extend a product's life cycle?
cards.answer: It lets manufacturers update individual components rather than replace the entire device, delaying decline.

cards.front: Name the three tactics Mrs Lyons uses to secure the pact with Mrs Johnstone.
cards.answer: Exploits her poverty ('you already have seven') / Makes her swear on the Bible / Invents a superstition about the twins dying
items: Exploits her poverty ('you already have seven')
Makes her swear on the Bible
Invents a superstition about the twins dying

cards.front: Name the three superstitious omens the Narrator links to the pact.
cards.answer: Shoes on the table / A broken mirror / A magpie

cards.front: Why does Mrs Lyons use the imperative 'Give one to me' rather than asking?
cards.answer: Russell uses the imperative to show the power imbalance between the middle-class employer and her working-class employee.

cards.front: Why does Mrs Johnstone believe Mrs Lyons's invented superstition so completely?
cards.answer: She is deeply superstitious and, having no real control over her life, looks to irrational beliefs to explain events.

cards.front: Name the seven mechanical properties every engineer must know.
cards.answer: Strength / Stiffness / Toughness / Hardness / Ductility / Malleability / Brittleness

cards.front: Why is mild steel chosen for structural beams that carry suspended loads?
cards.answer: It has excellent tensile strength, so it can bear a load without permanently deforming or fracturing.

cards.front: Why must stiffness be considered alongside strength when designing bridge decks and machine frames?
cards.answer: Excessive deflection can cause misalignment and fatigue cracking even when the material has not yet yielded.

cards.front: Why do hardness and toughness often trade off in cutting tools?
cards.answer: A very hard steel tool resists surface wear well but can shatter under impact because it lacks toughness.

cards.front: In Required Practical 9, name the three gas tests used to identify products at the electrodes.
cards.answer: Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop / Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper / Oxygen relights a glowing splint
items: Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop

cards.front: How does PANIC help you remember which ions go to which electrode in electrolysis?
cards.answer: It reminds you the Positive electrode is the Anode, and Negative Is the Cathode.

cards.front: In aqueous electrolysis, how do you decide what is produced at the anode?
cards.answer: If a halide ion is present the halogen is produced, otherwise oxygen is produced from the OH⁻ ions.

cards.front: [HIGHER] Why is the anode half-equation for molten lead bromide written as 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻?
cards.answer: Because two negative bromide ions each lose one electron (oxidation) to form a bromine molecule.

cards.front: Name the four connective words the lesson gives for linking weather and activities in German.
cards.answer: weil (because) / deshalb/deswegen (therefore) / als (when - past) / wenn (when/if - present/future)

cards.front: Name the seven places of interest (Sehenswürdigkeiten) listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: das Schloss (castle) / der Dom/die Kathedrale (cathedral) / der Freizeitpark (theme park) / der Zoo/Tierpark (zoo) / der Hafen (harbour/port) / die Altstadt (old town) / der Marktplatz (market square)

cards.front: How do you change 'Es ist sonnig' to talk about weather in the past?
cards.answer: You change ist to war, giving Es war sonnig (it was sunny).

cards.front: How do you decide whether to use als or wenn for 'when' in German?
cards.answer: Use als for a single past event and wenn for repeated events or present/future situations.

cards.front: What are the two rehabilitation approaches named in the lesson?
cards.answer: Restorative justice / Positive role models

cards.front: What are the three types of punishment/deterrent named in the lesson?
cards.answer: Prisons / Community sentences / Fines

cards.front: Why might a fine have little deterrent value for a wealthier offender?
cards.answer: Because a fine easily afforded by a wealthier offender does not create an unpleasant enough consequence to put them off reoffending.

cards.front: Why does restorative justice aim to build empathy in the offender?
cards.answer: Because bringing the offender into contact with the victim forces them to face the real human impact of what they did.

title: Nigeria: Aid, Environmental Cost & Quality of Life
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the three big environmental costs of Nigeria's development given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Oil spills and gas flaring in the Niger Delta / Desertification in the north / Air and water pollution in fast-growing cities like Lagos
items: Oil spills and gas flaring in the Niger Delta
Air and water pollution in fast-growing cities like Lagos

cards.front: Name the three negative impacts of aid on Nigeria given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Corruption can divert aid money / Aid can create dependency / Donors may attach self-serving conditions

cards.front: Why are oil spills so damaging to people in the Niger Delta?
cards.answer: They kill the fish and crops that around 60% of Delta residents rely on for food.

cards.front: Why does quality of life in Nigeria vary so much depending on where someone lives?
cards.answer: Wealth flows to Abuja and abroad while poor regions like Sokoto and the Niger Delta face poverty, pollution and violence.

cards.front: Name the four main opposition currents in Russia by 1905.
cards.answer: Kadets (liberal, parliamentary) / Octobrists (conservative liberal) / Socialist Revolutionaries (peasant-focused, used assassination) / Social Democrats (Bolsheviks and Mensheviks)

cards.front: Name three methods the Okhrana used to control opposition, besides infiltrating groups.
cards.answer: Censorship of newspapers / Banning trade unions / Laws against public meetings of more than three people
items: Laws against public meetings of more than three people

cards.front: Why did the regime prefer exiling agitators to Siberia rather than executing them?
cards.answer: Punishment was harsh but selective because the regime wanted to avoid creating martyrs for the opposition.

cards.front: How did Russification end up strengthening revolutionary movements rather than uniting the empire?
cards.answer: It created angry educated minorities, especially Poles and Jews, who supplied many of the empire's most determined revolutionaries.

title: Characters: The Hashimoto Family and Their Captors
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Give the three vocal/physical tools a performer uses to track Hanako's ageing across the play.
cards.answer: Pace of speech / Range of movement / Quality of stillness

cards.front: How might a performer show early-captivity Hanako differently from Hanako a decade later?
cards.answer: Early on she has fast, shallow breath, higher pitch and restlessness; later, slower speech, longer pauses and stillness show contained survival, not defeat.

cards.front: Why might a director have Jung Sun and Hanako start far apart in the teaching scenes and gradually move closer?
cards.answer: The reducing distance physically narrates their reluctant trust developing despite both being controlled by the same state machinery.

cards.front: Why might a performer play early-scene Etsuko as busy and routine-driven rather than simply sad?
cards.answer: Increased pace and volume of housekeeping shows denial as a defence against grief, making her stillness later carry more emotional weight.

cards.front: Why does Fleance's escape matter for the witches' prophecy?
cards.answer: Because he survives, Banquo's descendants can still become kings, so Macbeth's attempt to defeat fate has failed.

cards.front: Why does the collapse of the banquet matter symbolically?
cards.answer: The banquet symbolises order and legitimate rule, so its collapse shows a throne built on murder cannot sustain stability.

cards.front: Why can a falling market share be a warning sign even when a retailer's sales are rising?
cards.answer: Because the overall market may be growing faster than the business, meaning rivals are gaining ground.

cards.front: What is the difference between competing on price and competing on value?
cards.answer: Price means simply charging less, while value means ensuring quality, service and convenience feel worth what customers pay.

cards.front: Name the four rows found in a cash-flow forecast.
cards.answer: Cash inflows / Cash outflows / Net cash flow / Opening and closing balances

cards.front: Name the four common causes of cash-flow problems given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Overspending on stock or equipment / Slow-paying customers / Seasonal sales dips / Growing too fast

cards.front: Why can a profitable business still collapse due to cash flow?
cards.answer: Wages, rent and bills must be paid in actual cash on the day, but sale cash may not arrive for weeks if customers use trade credit.

cards.front: Why can't a structural cash-flow shortfall be fixed by borrowing?
cards.answer: If outflows are consistently higher than inflows, borrowing just makes the debt grow instead of solving the underlying problem.

title: Amrit Sanskar, the Khalsa and the Five Ks
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: What does Kachera symbolise for an amritdhari Sikh?
cards.answer: Self-control and moral restraint, particularly chastity and fidelity, while being practical for readiness to serve.

cards.front: What does Kangha symbolise for an amritdhari Sikh?
cards.answer: Spiritual discipline and order, reminding the wearer to keep their mind as ordered and focused on God as their hair.

title: Performance Interpretation: Acting Proctor's Final Choice
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Why does the lesson say 'I would play Proctor angrily' earns almost nothing?
cards.answer: It names the emotion but does not translate it into concrete physical or vocal choices an audience can read.

cards.front: How does the linen scene's staging show the emotional distance between Proctor and Elizabeth?
cards.answer: Keeping Proctor on the opposite side of the central table from Elizabeth uses proxemics as a physical sign of their distance.

title: Sources, Style and the Whole-Theme Answer
subject: latin-eduqas

cards.front: In a strong plan for 'Can women be heroes?', name the three pieces of evidence used to show ambitious women were remembered as villains or condemned rather than heroic.
cards.answer: Sempronia condemned for breaking convention / Tullia driving over her father's body / Cleopatra described only as 'the woman'
items: Tullia driving over her father's body

cards.front: Why does asyndeton in Sallust's list of Sempronia's crimes create a breathless rhythm?
cards.answer: Because leaving out connecting words between the three clauses makes the accusations pile up rapidly, one after another.

cards.front: Why is 'the coin shows a man carrying someone' considered a weak source answer?
cards.answer: Because it only describes what is shown without linking the detail to a specific fact about the hero or event.

cards.front: Name the three models of marriage the play presents.
cards.answer: Maggie and Willie's partnership of equals / Alice/Vickey's conventional matches / Hobson's patriarchal model
items: Maggie and Willie's partnership of equals

cards.front: Name the four key contexts the lesson lists for embedding into an essay on the play.
cards.answer: Victorian class system / women's limited rights in 1880 / the suffragette era / the 1870 Education Act

cards.front: Why does Hobson's downfall serve as a warning in the play?
cards.answer: His pride and refusal to adapt to change mean he is overtaken by those who embrace it, like Maggie and Willie.

cards.front: Why does the play show Alice and Vickey gaining independence through conventional marriage rather than Maggie's route?
cards.answer: It shows independence means different things to different women, and the most courageous path isn't always the conventional one.

title: The Breadwinner: Narrative and Animation Under Occupation
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Why does the film withhold non-diegetic score during the disguise-haircut scene?
cards.answer: The silence marks the moment as needing no emotional amplification, so the spectator feels its weight through withheld music.

cards.front: How does the prison-wall composition use figure-to-space ratio to affect the spectator?
cards.answer: The walls fill four-fifths of the frame and Parvana is tiny, making the institution feel dominant and impersonal against the individual.

cards.front: Why does the storybook level resolve before the realist reunion in the closing sequence?
cards.answer: Resolving the symbolic journey first emotionally prepares the spectator to receive the literal reunion between Parvana and her father.

cards.front: How does the storybook hero's quest relate structurally to Parvana's own story?
cards.answer: The hero's quest to retrieve stolen bones from the Elephant King mirrors Parvana's quest to recover her imprisoned father.

title: Elizabethan government: court, Privy Council and Parliament
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three duties Justices of the Peace carried out in Elizabethan counties, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Enforced law at quarter sessions / Collected taxes / Regulated wages / Oversaw poor relief / Ensured royal proclamations carried out

cards.front: Why did nobles compete so intensely to attend the Royal Court?
cards.answer: Proximity to Elizabeth gave access to patronage such as offices, land grants and trade licences, and losing favour meant losing everything.

cards.front: How did Elizabeth manage Parliament to keep control over its debates?
cards.answer: She used privy councillors sitting as MPs to manage debates and relied on the Crown-appointed Speaker to steer business.

cards.front: Name the four synthetic fibres described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Polyester / Nylon / Acrylic / Elastane

cards.front: Why does linen crease severely compared with other fabrics?
cards.answer: Linen is a stiff stem fibre that lacks elasticity, so it creases severely when worn or handled.

cards.front: How does drawing (stretching) affect synthetic filaments after melt spinning?
cards.answer: Drawing stretches the filaments under tension to align the polymer chains, increasing strength and reducing extensibility.

cards.front: Why is a mixed fabric different in each direction, unlike a blended fibre?
cards.answer: A mixed fabric uses different fibres in the warp and weft yarns rather than blending them within the same yarn.

title: Daily Life: Towns, Villages and Economic Change
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four peasant food staples described for daily life in the lesson.
cards.answer: Coarse bread of barley, rye or maslin / Pottage of dried peas and beans / Onions or herbs for flavour / Cheese and meat at festivals
items: Coarse bread of barley, rye or maslin
Pottage of dried peas and beans

cards.front: Name the three areas the lesson identifies as the big shifts caused by the Norman conquest.
cards.answer: Urban (French quarters, new markets) / Legal (forest law, murdrum fine, primogeniture) / Architectural (castles and cathedrals)

cards.front: Why does the lesson describe the Norman conquest's effect on peasant life as a 'crust on a loaf'?
cards.answer: Because the ruling class and landscape changed completely, but most peasants kept ploughing the same strips, church and food unchanged.

cards.front: How did Norman inheritance customs reduce the legal position of higher-status English women?
cards.answer: Norman customary law restricted widows to dower-portions and channelled estates through male primogeniture, unlike wider Anglo-Saxon land and will rights.

cards.front: Name the three bullet prompts given to shape a part (a) comparison answer.
cards.answer: Ideas and attitudes in each poem / Tone and atmosphere in each poem / Effects of language and structure used
items: Ideas and attitudes in each poem
Tone and atmosphere in each poem
Effects of language and structure used

cards.front: Name the four ways students lose marks before they even write an answer in the poetry section.
cards.answer: Writing about only one poem in part (a) / Choosing a part (b) poem from a different or outdated cluster / Re-using the part (a) poem in part (b) / Comparing poems in part (b)
items: Writing about only one poem in part (a)
Choosing a part (b) poem from a different cluster
Re-using the part (a) poem in part (b)

cards.front: Why does comparing in part (b) of the poetry section waste time?
cards.answer: Comparison is not required there, and it eats the time needed for close analysis of one poem.

cards.front: Why is naming a technique alone not enough to lift a poetry answer?
cards.answer: Strong answers comment on the effect of a technique rather than simply naming it.

title: Walby on Patriarchy and Power Relationships
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: How does the male violence structure of patriarchy affect women's behaviour in public, according to Heidensohn?
cards.answer: Fear of male violence makes women avoid travelling alone at night and limit where they go and how they dress.

cards.front: How did Walby respond to the Marxist criticism that patriarchy is rooted in class conflict?
cards.answer: She argued patriarchy predates capitalism and persists in socialist societies, so it cannot be reduced to class conflict.

cards.front: Why does the state structure count as a form of patriarchy according to Walby?
cards.answer: It weakly enforces equal pay laws, under-represents women in power, and historically treated domestic violence and rape as private matters.

title: Act 3: Eric, the Speech & the Twist
subject: english-literature-eduqas

cards.front: Give the three interpretations the lesson offers for the cyclical ending's meaning.
cards.answer: Inspector was a supernatural warning giving them a chance / the evening was a moral rehearsal before a real test / a political warning that 1912 warnings were ignored, causing catastrophe
items: Inspector was a supernatural warning giving them a chance
the evening was a moral rehearsal before a real test
a political warning that 1912 warnings were ignored, causing catastrophe

cards.front: Why does Eric say his father is not someone 'a chap could go to when he's in trouble'?
cards.answer: Birling's obsession with business, reputation and status left Eric unable to seek help from him.

cards.front: Why are Birling and Mrs Birling relieved after Gerald discovers no girl died at the Infirmary?
cards.answer: They believe the Inspector was a hoax, so they can escape scandal without facing moral accountability.

cards.front: How does the repetition of 'millions and millions and millions' work in the Inspector's final speech?
cards.answer: It hammers home the scale of social injustice, showing Eva represents an entire class of exploited people.

title: Al-Qadr, Akhirah & the Day of Judgement
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: What three questions do the angels Munkar and Nakir ask the deceased in the grave?
cards.answer: Who is your Lord? / What is your religion? / Who is your prophet?

cards.front: What two events happen when the angel Israfil blows the trumpet on the Day of Judgement?
cards.answer: First blast kills all living things / Second blast resurrects everyone who has lived
items: First blast kills all living things
Second blast resurrects everyone who has lived

cards.front: How does the teacher-and-student analogy explain predestination and human freedom?
cards.answer: Like a teacher who knows a student will fail, Allah's foreknowledge doesn't cause actions — the person's own choice does.

cards.front: Why does receiving your book of deeds in the right or left hand matter on the Day of Judgement?
cards.answer: The right hand means entering paradise, while the left hand means facing punishment, based on the deeds recorded.

cards.front: What four immediate outcomes made up the aftermath of the Peasants' Revolt of 1381?
cards.answer: Poll Tax never levied again / Mile End charters revoked / serfdom remained legal / hundreds of rebels executed

cards.front: Why did wage control legislation after 1381 have limited practical effect?
cards.answer: The labour shortage from the Black Death persisted into the fifteenth century, and economic forces pushing wages up were stronger than the law.

cards.front: Name the three positive impacts sponsors gain from sport association given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Brand visibility among large loyal audiences / Association with high-performance and health values / Access to global markets via major events
items: Brand visibility among large loyal audiences
Association with high-performance and health values
Access to global markets via major events

cards.front: Give the two examples the lesson uses of rule changes made to suit television schedules.
cards.answer: Cricket introducing Twenty20 (T20) / Diamond League cutting disciplines from 32 to 24
items: Diamond League cutting disciplines from 32 to 24

cards.front: Why did cricket introduce the Twenty20 (T20) format?
cards.answer: It was designed to fit television schedules and attract new, younger audiences who would not watch a five-day Test match.

cards.front: Why can commercial pressure be psychologically demanding for elite performers?
cards.answer: Pressure to perform increases when sponsors are watching, and athletes must maintain a public image and avoid controversy.

cards.front: How does the offstage final stage direction (the shell's whine and the dugout's collapse) affect the audience?
cards.answer: Being heard rather than shown makes the ending more powerful, forcing the audience to imagine the destruction.

cards.front: How does dramatic irony in the letter scene affect the audience's experience of Stanhope?
cards.answer: The audience suspects Raleigh's letter praises Stanhope while Stanhope fears the worst, creating tension the characters cannot feel.

cards.front: Name the three effects the lesson gives for keeping violence offstage in Journey's End.
cards.answer: Keeps focus on characters' reactions / Mirrors officers hearing not seeing war / Makes violence more frightening through imagination
items: Mirrors officers hearing not seeing war
Makes violence more frightening through imagination

title: Values in Sport — Team Spirit, Fair Play & National Pride
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-studies

cards.front: Name the seven sporting values identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Team spirit / Fair play / Citizenship / Tolerance and respect / Inclusion / National pride / Excellence

cards.front: How does strong team spirit affect a team's performance in high-pressure situations?
cards.answer: Teams with strong team spirit tend to outperform their expected ability level in high-pressure situations.

cards.front: How does the Paralympic movement show the value of inclusion?
cards.answer: It insists people with disabilities have equal opportunities to compete at the highest level, not just modified recreational activities.

cards.front: How can national pride bring communities together during a major tournament?
cards.answer: People who would otherwise have little in common find shared identity through supporting their national team.

cards.front: Name the five daily prayer times in Salah.
cards.answer: Fajr / Zuhr / Asr / Maghrib / Isha

cards.front: Name the six acts in the Ten Obligatory Acts that go beyond the Five Pillars.
cards.answer: Khums / Jihad / Amr-bil-Maroof (commanding good) / Nahy-anil-Munkar (forbidding evil) / Tawalla / Tabarra

cards.front: Why are some Muslims excused from fasting during Ramadan?
cards.answer: The Qur'an does not demand fasting where it would cause genuine harm, so the ill, pregnant, travelling, elderly or menstruating are excused and can compensate later or give charity.

cards.front: Why does Ashura mean something different for Shi'a Muslims than for Sunni Muslims?
cards.answer: Shi'a Muslims mark it as a day of mourning for Imam Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala, while Sunnis treat it as voluntary fasting recalling Moses's rescue from Pharaoh.

title: Catholic Beliefs: Trinity, Incarnation and Creation
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three moments in Catholic life where the lesson says the Trinity is invoked.
cards.answer: Baptism / Marriage / Final blessing at Mass

cards.front: Why do Orthodox Christians agree with Catholics on the Incarnation but some liberal Protestants differ?
cards.answer: Orthodox share the Chalcedon view of one Person with two natures, while some liberal Protestants see it only symbolically, not a metaphysical change.

cards.front: How does the Incarnation show that Jesus is fully God and fully human?
cards.answer: The eternal Word, who was God, became flesh and lived among us, uniting two natures in one Person.

title: Improving Lagos: The Makoko Floating School & Self-Help
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the three self-help features that made the Makoko Floating School a community project rather than an imposed one.
cards.answer: Local fishermen towed it into place / Residents helped run the school / Built using salvaged plastic barrels
items: Local fishermen towed it into place

cards.front: Why did the original Makoko Floating School collapse in 2016?
cards.answer: A heavy storm caused it to collapse, showing self-help architecture's limits without long-term funding and engineering support.

cards.front: Why do the most successful improvements in Lagos combine top-down and self-help approaches?
cards.answer: Top-down delivers large-scale projects, while self-help delivers relevance by reaching families in slum areas that big schemes miss.

title: Principles of Training and Programme Design
subject: physical-education-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four FITT variables that can be manipulated to create progressive overload.
cards.answer: Frequency / Intensity / Time / Type

cards.front: Why does a sprinter need short, explosive training rather than long, slow jogging?
cards.answer: Specificity means training must develop the fast-twitch fibres and anaerobic energy system the sport actually demands.

cards.front: Why does lactic acid limit how long an athlete can work in the anaerobic training zone?
cards.answer: At 80-90% max HR the body cannot supply oxygen fast enough, so anaerobic pathways are used and lactic acid accumulates, limiting duration.

cards.front: Why is 'working harder every session' a misconception about progressive overload?
cards.answer: It risks overtraining; overload should be built gradually over weeks with recovery weeks, since adaptation happens during rest, not the session itself.

cards.front: Name the five location factors the lesson says every business weighs against each other.
cards.answer: Proximity to the market / Availability of raw materials / Availability of labour / Level of competition / Costs

cards.front: Why do restaurants often benefit from clustering together on a 'restaurant row'?
cards.answer: Diners come to the area to eat and then choose which venue to visit, so clustering draws more customers overall.

cards.front: How does the cost of transporting raw materials decide whether a business locates near materials or near its market?
cards.answer: If transporting raw materials costs more than transporting the finished product, the business should locate near the materials instead of the market.

cards.front: Why might a family furniture business stay near home even if a different location could offer benefits?
cards.answer: Moving would mean losing skilled craftspeople who cannot commute further.

cards.front: Name the five stages of Jane's growing independence and their settings, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Dependence at Gateshead / Education at Lowood / Employment at Thornfield / Financial freedom at Moor House / Free choice at Ferndean

cards.front: What four things does the lesson say to focus on when analysing an extract?
cards.answer: Word-level analysis / Sentence structure / Literary techniques / Structural choices

cards.front: Why does Brontë use the supernatural moment of Jane hearing Rochester's voice across the moors?
cards.answer: It has no rational explanation, suggesting the connection between Jane and Rochester is spiritual rather than physical or social.

cards.front: How does the inheritance affect Jane and Rochester's relationship when they marry?
cards.answer: It makes Jane his financial equal, though she was always his spiritual and intellectual equal even as his employee.

cards.front: Why did many first-generation Caribbean immigrants suppress their cultural identity in Britain?
cards.answer: To survive in a racist Britain, many felt they had to suppress their cultural identity, language and spiritual practices.

cards.front: Why is Leave Taking significant in centring Caribbean-British women's experiences?
cards.answer: It centres motherhood, cultural identity and generational conflict rather than presenting Caribbean-British women as secondary to male or white narratives.

cards.front: Name the eight operating systems named in the specification.
cards.answer: Windows / Apple macOS / Apple iOS / Android / Chrome OS / Ubuntu / Linux / Unix

cards.front: Why must HCI designers plan carefully when targeting Linux environments?
cards.answer: Linux can be configured so freely that its interfaces vary widely, from graphical desktops to command-line interfaces.

cards.front: Why should a finance department modelling budget forecasts use a spreadsheet platform rather than another digital platform?
cards.answer: Spreadsheets present data in a grid of cells with formula input and chart generation for numeric analysis.

cards.front: Why does Holmes use cocaine at the start of the novel?
cards.answer: His mind rebels at stagnation, so without a case to occupy his intellect he uses cocaine to escape boredom.

cards.front: Why does Watson's deduction about his pocket watch upset him?
cards.answer: Holmes coldly reveals from scratches, dents and a pawnbroker's mark that Watson's late brother was an alcoholic who wasted his inheritance.

cards.front: Why does Doyle have Watson react with disapproval to Holmes's cocaine use?
cards.answer: Watson's medical perspective and disapproval show the reader the habit is harmful rather than glamorous or heroic.

cards.front: How does Doyle build suspense across chapters 1 to 5?
cards.answer: He structures the chapters as a crescendo, from a slow domestic scene to the mystery, the fog, Thaddeus's revelation, then the shock of murder.

title: Reactions of Acids, pH and Neutralisation
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the four types of reaction of acids given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Acid + metal / Acid + metal oxide / Acid + metal hydroxide / Acid + metal carbonate

cards.front: Why does a metal oxide reacting with an acid produce a salt and water rather than a gas?
cards.answer: Because the reaction of an acid with a metal oxide produces a salt and water, with no gas released.

cards.front: Why does the same concentration of a weak acid have a higher pH than a strong acid?
cards.answer: A weak acid only partially ionises, so it produces fewer H+ ions than a strong acid at the same concentration.

cards.front: Name the three key waveform properties described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Amplitude / Frequency / Periodic time

cards.front: Why can a noisy digital signal be restored to a clean signal, but a noisy analogue signal cannot?
cards.answer: Digital signals have only two states, so if a noisy signal is clearly above the threshold it can be regenerated to a clean 1, unlike continuous analogue signals.

cards.front: Why does converting an analogue signal to digital introduce quantisation error?
cards.answer: Because the continuous analogue signal is approximated using discrete steps when converted, causing a small quantisation error.

title: Narrative Structure: Plot, Story and Three-Act Form
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the seven character roles ('spheres of action') Propp identified in Russian folk tales.
cards.answer: Hero / Villain / Donor / Helper / Dispatcher / Princess / False hero

cards.front: Why does disrupting cause and effect (jumping scenes with no explained connection) affect the spectator?
cards.answer: It makes the spectator aware of the narration itself, which can feel disorienting or thought-provoking depending on the filmmaker's intent.

cards.front: How should Todorov's or Propp's models be used to get analytical credit, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: By pinning the theory to a named moment in the film and explaining specific filmic choices, not describing the theory abstractly.

title: Medieval warfare: knights, archers and the feudal army c1250–c1500
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three battles the lesson gives where mounted French knights charged into a wall of English arrows.
cards.answer: Crécy (1346) / Poitiers (1356) / Agincourt (1415)

cards.front: How were the Scottish schiltrons at Falkirk eventually destroyed?
cards.answer: Not by horsemen but by English longbowmen, who shot the schiltrons apart from a safe distance.

cards.front: Why does the lesson say the longbow alone should not be credited with winning Agincourt?
cards.answer: It worked alongside funnel terrain, deep mud, French command failures and Henry V's choice to fight on a narrow front between two woods.

cards.front: How did gunpowder cannon and the longbow together squeeze the mounted knight from two sides?
cards.answer: Cheap missile troops broke up cavalry charges while cannon broke the castle walls that had been the knight's refuge.

cards.front: Name all four benefits for service users given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Standardisation of care / Improved quality of care / Maintains or improves quality of life / Supports service users to develop their strengths
items: Maintains or improves quality of life
Supports service users to develop their strengths

cards.front: How does applying the value of individuality lead to improved quality of care for a service user?
cards.answer: A practitioner asks about preferences, history and culture, shaping a care plan that genuinely fits the person, giving better health outcomes.

cards.front: How does the value of individuality support a practitioner's skill development?
cards.answer: Recognising each service user has unique communication needs pushes practitioners to learn new skills, such as Makaton or sign language.

cards.front: Name the four upland areas the lesson gives as examples of high ground in the UK.
cards.answer: Scottish Highlands / Lake District / Snowdonia / Pennines / Dartmoor

cards.front: Name the four processes the lesson gives that shape UK landscapes on top of the underlying geology.
cards.answer: Past glaciation / ongoing weathering / slope processes / centuries of human activity

cards.front: Why do hard rocks like granite and slate form upland areas in the UK?
cards.answer: They resist erosion better than surrounding rocks, so softer rock wears away while the hard rock stays standing.

cards.front: Why does upland Britain run roughly NW-SE?
cards.answer: Ancient mountain-building (the Caledonian and Variscan orogenies) folded rocks along this line, forming a geological backbone, while younger rocks stayed flatter.

cards.front: Why is the moral ending of Twelfth Night unbalanced regarding Malvolio and his tormentors?
cards.answer: Malvolio suffers while Maria and Sir Toby are rewarded with marriage, creating a moral asymmetry between victim and pranksters.

cards.front: How does Feste's mock examination of Malvolio show irony in the Sir Topas scene?
cards.answer: Malvolio answers Feste's questions about Pythagoras correctly and coherently, yet Feste still declares him mad.

title: Young King Henry and the Rise of Wolsey
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three main aims Henry VIII had as a young king.
cards.answer: Military glory in France / A male heir to secure the dynasty / Personal control without doing daily admin
items: A male heir to secure the dynasty
Personal control without doing daily admin

cards.front: What four factors does the lesson give for why Wolsey rose so fast?
cards.answer: Sheer administrative ability / He understood and flattered Henry / Independent clerical income / No powerful family to rival the king
items: No powerful family to rival the king

cards.front: Why did Henry VIII need someone like Wolsey to manage his government?
cards.answer: Henry preferred hunting, jousting and music to daily administration, so he needed someone else to do the detailed work of ruling.

cards.front: Why does the lesson say Wolsey was not simply Henry's puppet?
cards.answer: Wolsey shaped foreign policy, drove the Eltham Ordinances and ran the law courts on his own initiative, while Henry only set broad goals.

title: The Mitzvot and Key Moral Principles
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the three prohibitions that Pikuach Nefesh cannot override, even to save a life.
cards.answer: Murder / Sexual immorality / Idol worship

cards.front: Why do ethical Mitzvot require people to treat others with dignity, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because all humans are created in the image of G-d, so they deserve dignity and fair treatment.

cards.front: How does Judaism resolve the tension between Divine Providence and human free will?
cards.answer: Thinkers like Maimonides argue G-d's foreknowledge does not cancel human freedom, even though this is hard to fully explain.

cards.front: Name the four phases of clinical trials described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Phase 1: healthy volunteers, test safety / Phase 2: patients, initial effectiveness evidence / Phase 3: large-scale comparison against best treatment / Phase 4: post-approval surveillance in general population
items: Phase 3: large-scale comparison against best treatment
Phase 4: post-approval surveillance in general population

cards.front: Why is a placebo control essential in a clinical trial?
cards.answer: It separates the true drug effect from the placebo effect, since belief in receiving treatment alone can improve symptoms.

cards.front: Why has the pipeline for new antibiotics slowed in recent decades?
cards.answer: Because development costs are high but commercial returns are lower than for drugs used long-term, discouraging investment.

cards.front: Why does post-approval surveillance (Phase 4) matter even after a drug is approved?
cards.answer: It can detect rare side effects that were too uncommon to appear during clinical trials, once the drug is used by the wider population.

cards.front: How does becoming a mother change identity in Duffy's "Before You Were Mine"?
cards.answer: The mother's glamorous, independent past self was surrendered and replaced by belonging to her child.

cards.front: Why does the son's memory in "Walking Away" still "gnaw" at Day-Lewis eighteen years on?
cards.answer: The pain of watching his son separate from him remains permanent even after many years.

cards.front: How does the verb "stumbling" create the reversal in Heaney's "Follower"?
cards.answer: It transfers from the clumsy child following his father to the now ageing, dependent father following his son.

cards.front: Why is the reversal in "Follower" described as both tender and uncomfortable?
cards.answer: Heaney remembers his own loving devotion as a child but feels frustration at his father now being burdensome.

cards.front: Name the first six of the Seven Commandments (excluding 'All animals are equal').
cards.answer: Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy / Whatever goes upon four legs or has wings is a friend / No animal shall wear clothes / No animal shall sleep in a bed / No animal shall drink alcohol / No animal shall kill any other animal
items: Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy
Whatever goes upon four legs or has wings is a friend
No animal shall sleep in a bed
No animal shall kill any other animal

cards.front: Why does Squealer say the pigs must have the milk and apples?
cards.answer: He claims the pigs need them because they do 'brainwork' and warns Jones would come back if the pigs failed.

cards.front: How does the speed of the Rebellion parallel the October Revolution?
cards.answer: Both happened quickly and with relatively little resistance, as Jones's neglect let the animals seize power easily, mirroring the Bolsheviks' seizure of power.

cards.front: Name the two weaknesses the lesson gives for using ARR to judge an investment.
cards.answer: Ignores timing of returns / Based on forecasts that may be wrong / ignores risk
items: Based on forecasts that may be wrong / ignores risk

cards.front: Name the three strengths the lesson gives for the ARR method.
cards.answer: Simple to calculate and explain / Gives a percentage comparable to interest rates / Uses the full life of the project
items: Gives a percentage comparable to interest rates
Uses the full life of the project

cards.front: Why does a healthy margin of safety help protect a business?
cards.answer: It gives a cushion so sales can fall (from bad weather, new rivals or lower demand) before the business starts losing money.

cards.front: Why is a 30% ARR on a risky project considered worse than a 15% ARR on a safe project?
cards.answer: Because ARR ignores risk, so a high return on a reckless venture can be worse than a lower return on a safe one.

cards.front: The lesson gives three reasons the division of labour raises output for firms. What are they?
cards.answer: Workers become highly skilled at the task / Less time wasted switching between tasks / Machinery designed for repetitive jobs
items: Workers become highly skilled at the task
Less time wasted switching between tasks

cards.front: Name the four functions of money given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Medium of exchange / Store of value / Unit of account / Standard of deferred payment

cards.front: Why can a region become vulnerable if it relies heavily on specialising in one industry?
cards.answer: If demand for its main product collapses, workers have narrow skills, firms have few alternative markets, and the region can decline long-term.

cards.front: Why does money remove the need for a double coincidence of wants?
cards.answer: Everyone accepts money, so a seller doesn't need to want what the buyer produces, only the money itself.

cards.front: How does Austen show Darcy's pride and Elizabeth's prejudice feeding each other?
cards.answer: Darcy's pride causes Elizabeth's prejudice, and her prejudice then reinforces her resistance to seeing his true character.

cards.front: Why does Jane and Bingley's relationship break down despite their genuine connection?
cards.answer: External forces (Darcy and Bingley's sisters) separate them because one or both lack strength to resist social pressure.

cards.front: Why does the moors sequence strip Jane of money, shelter, identity and status?
cards.answer: To reduce her to her most basic self, proving her worth doesn't depend on Thornfield or Rochester.

cards.front: Why must Diana and Mary Rivers work as governesses?
cards.answer: Their family lost its money, mirroring Jane's own situation and showing poverty doesn't diminish worth.

title: Video Games: Fortnite — Industry and Audience
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three examples the lesson gives of Fortnite's cross-media collaborations to stay in the news.
cards.answer: Avengers: Infinity War segment with Marvel / Godzilla tie-in / Promotion by celebrities Drake and Ben Simmons
items: Avengers: Infinity War segment with Marvel
Promotion by celebrities Drake and Ben Simmons

cards.front: How does Fortnite's technological convergence work across devices?
cards.answer: It can be played on consoles, PCs, laptops, smartphones and tablets, and players can switch device mid-game without interruption.

cards.front: Why does Fortnite appeal to a wider audience than realistic violent games like Call of Duty?
cards.answer: Its unrealistic, cartoon-style violence and focus on construction alongside combat draw in younger and more diverse players.

cards.front: Why is Fortnite seen as an example of active audience theory?
cards.answer: Gameplay is interactive and collaborative, letting players deconstruct and rebuild environments and design content, encouraging creativity over passive consumption.

cards.front: Why must vague specification criteria like 'the product must be strong' be avoided?
cards.answer: Vague criteria cannot be tested objectively, so they produce vague evaluation and no clear basis for deciding if the design succeeds.

cards.front: Why does a stacking toy specification need both quantitative and qualitative criteria?
cards.answer: A toy passing all quantitative tests but looking unappealing won't sell, and one looking perfect but failing strength tests is unsafe, so both are needed.

cards.front: Name the four physical properties the lesson gives that distinguish transition metals from Group 1 metals.
cards.answer: Higher melting points / Harder and stronger / Much denser / Less reactive

cards.front: Name the four uses of nanoparticles given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Medicine (wound dressings) / Sunscreens / Electronics / Catalysis

cards.front: Why does cutting a material into smaller cubes increase its total surface area for the same volume?
cards.answer: Splitting a solid into smaller pieces exposes more surface for the same total volume, increasing the surface area to volume ratio.

cards.front: Why are nanoparticle catalysts more effective than bulk catalysts using the same mass of material?
cards.answer: Their very high surface area to volume ratio means more surface is exposed for reactions, so less material is needed.

cards.front: Give the two main types of source used to study insula life.
cards.answer: Material remains (Insula of Diana) / Literary descriptions (Juvenal and Petronius)

cards.front: Why did fires spread so rapidly through the upper floors of a Roman insula?
cards.answer: There was no running water upstairs, no kitchens so residents cooked on open braziers, and buildings were partly built of timber.

cards.front: Why was the ground floor of an insula usually used for shops and taverns rather than housing?
cards.answer: Ground level with street frontage was the most accessible and commercially valuable space, so landlords rented it for business.

cards.front: Why is material evidence like the Insula of Diana limited on its own for understanding insula life?
cards.answer: It shows building design, scale and materials but cannot reveal daily experience like noise, smells or social tensions.

title: The Gurdwara, Langar and Daily Worship
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five prayers that make up the Nitnem.
cards.answer: Japji Sahib (morning) / Jaap Sahib (morning) / Tav-Prasad Savaiye (morning) / Sodar Rahiras Sahib (evening) / Kirtan Sohila (bedtime)

cards.front: Name the three forms Nam Japna can take.
cards.answer: Silent personal meditation / Recitation during daily prayers / Communal singing of hymns (kirtan)

cards.front: Why was the langar instituted by the Sikh Gurus?
cards.answer: As a direct rejection of the caste system, dissolving social distinctions by having everyone eat together on the floor.

cards.front: How does the Harmandir Sahib's care for the Guru Granth Sahib show it is treated as a living presence?
cards.answer: It is placed there through the day with hymns sung almost continuously, then carried by palanquin to rest each night and returned at dawn.

title: A female ruler: Parliament, marriage and the succession
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What three drawbacks did each of Elizabeth's potential marriage matches bring, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Catholic husband risked the religious settlement / Foreign prince risked drawing England into wars / Domestic noble risked civil war between rival factions
items: Catholic husband risked the religious settlement
Domestic noble risked civil war between factions

cards.front: Why did Elizabeth use marriage negotiations as a diplomatic tool rather than aiming to actually marry?
cards.answer: While Spain and France believed she might wed their candidate, neither dared invade, so delay bought safety.

cards.front: Why did Elizabeth call Parliament rarely and limit what it discussed?
cards.answer: She needed Parliament for taxation and law but disliked its Protestant views and pressure over marriage and the succession, so she restricted its role.

title: Benefits to Health & Wellbeing When Rights Are Maintained
subject: health-social-care-ocr

cards.front: Name the four main benefits produced when rights are maintained, as grouped in the lesson.
cards.answer: Empowerment / High self-esteem / Needs being met / Trust

cards.front: Why does trust depend particularly on confidentiality and protection from abuse and harm?
cards.answer: Knowing personal information stays private and staff are properly trained reassures the service user that providers have their best interests in mind.

cards.front: How does a lack of equal treatment affect a service user's self-esteem?
cards.answer: Without equal treatment, self-esteem drops and the service user may feel worthless or discriminated against.

cards.front: Why does a breach of confidentiality lead to worse clinical outcomes?
cards.answer: Breaching confidentiality destroys trust, so the service user may withhold health information from practitioners, worsening clinical outcomes.

title: African Americans before Brown v Board
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the two practices the lesson gives that caused housing and employment inequality for African Americans outside the South.
cards.answer: Restrictive covenants in housing deeds / Redlining by banks and insurers

cards.front: Why did Southern states target graduate and professional education first, rather than school segregation, in the NAACP's early legal strategy?
cards.answer: Because inequality of facilities was starkest there and courts were more likely to be receptive to challenges.

cards.front: How did Massive Resistance show the gap between the Brown ruling and daily reality in the South?
cards.answer: Southern states signed the Southern Manifesto and Virginia closed schools, so by 1964 fewer than 2% of Black students attended desegregated schools.

cards.front: Why must a designer avoid internal corners and recesses when designing for finishing processes?
cards.answer: Internal corners and recesses trap residues and prevent even coating, spoiling the finish.

cards.front: Why is injection moulding uneconomical for a 50-unit batch prototype but viable for 100,000 units per year?
cards.answer: The expensive mould tool cost can only be recovered when spread across a very large production run.

cards.front: Why does forming a sheet metal part by bending require the designer to account for spring-back?
cards.answer: Forming deforms material without removing it, and the metal partially returns towards its original shape after bending.

title: Chemical Equations and Conservation of Mass
subject: science-ocr-b

cards.front: Name the four state symbols used in chemical equations and what each means.
cards.answer: (s) solid / (l) liquid / (g) gas / (aq) dissolved in water

cards.front: Why must a symbol equation be balanced when a word equation does not need to be?
cards.answer: Symbol equations show the actual ratio of atoms reacting, so both sides must have equal atom numbers to obey conservation of mass.

cards.front: How do you work out the formula of an ionic compound like Al2O3 from the ion charges?
cards.answer: You combine ions in whatever ratio makes the total positive and negative charge cancel out, e.g. Al3+ and O2- combine 2:3.

cards.front: [HIGHER] Why do electrolysis reactions use half-equations showing electrons instead of a normal balanced equation?
cards.answer: Because each half-equation shows electrons gained or lost at one electrode, and must balance for both atoms and charge.

cards.front: Name the four periods the thematic study of migration covers.
cards.answer: Medieval, c800-c1500 / Early modern, c1500-c1700 / Industrial, c1700-c1900 / Modern, c1900-present

cards.front: Name the five turning points the lesson lists for the migration thematic study.
cards.answer: 1290 expulsion / 1685 Huguenot wave / 1905 Aliens Act / 1948 British Nationality Act / 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act

cards.front: Why does the 1290 expulsion of England's Jewish population mix several key factors together?
cards.answer: It combined institutions (a royal decree from Edward I), religion (Christian hostility) and economics (royal debts owed to Jewish lenders).

cards.front: Why does the 1948 British Nationality Act mix several key factors together?
cards.answer: It combined institutions (Parliament passing the Act) with end-of-Empire politics and post-war labour shortages.

title: Birmingham, Washington and the Civil Rights Act, 1963-64
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Why did King and Wyatt Tee Walker choose Birmingham as the 1963 campaign target?
cards.answer: They expected police commissioner Bull Connor to react with public violence, forcing the country to see what segregation actually was.

cards.front: Why did Freedom Summer deliberately recruit mainly white Northern student volunteers?
cards.answer: Organisers knew violence against Black activists alone was ignored, but violence against white students would generate national news.

cards.front: How did the murder of the three Freedom Summer volunteers help the civil rights movement, despite no murder convictions at the time?
cards.answer: It put the lack of Black voting rights in the national news and led to the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party's convention challenge.

cards.front: Name the three things the 1964 Civil Rights Act banned segregation in.
cards.answer: Public accommodations / Federally funded programmes / Employment

title: The Impact of War on Others
subject: english-literature-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three poems in the lesson about war's impact on people beyond the battlefield, and their poets.
cards.answer: Poppies by Jane Weir / War Photographer by Carole Satyamurti / What Were They Like? by Denise Levertov
items: What Were They Like? by Denise Levertov

cards.front: Why does the photographer in Satyamurti's War Photographer find 'the reassurance of the frame' fragile?
cards.answer: Because the photographs later force the photographer to confront what they witnessed, even in the safety of the darkroom.

cards.front: How does the word 'crimped' in Poppies add to the poem's meaning?
cards.answer: It suggests the poppy is carefully handmade, fragile and easily damaged, mirroring the mother's fragile emotions.

cards.front: Name the three skills the lesson says Cromwell learned working on Wolsey's monastery project.
cards.answer: How to value monastic property / How to draft Acts of Parliament / How to manage royal commissioners on the ground
items: How to draft Acts of Parliament
How to manage royal commissioners on the ground

cards.front: Name the three offices/roles Cromwell held by 1535 that let him run government from one desk.
cards.answer: Principal Secretary / Master of the Rolls / Vicegerent in Spirituals

cards.front: How did Cromwell's statutory argument let Henry get his annulment without going through Rome?
cards.answer: Parliament could declare England a self-sufficient empire whose king answered to no foreign prince, so no English court needed papal permission on the marriage.

cards.front: Why did Henry promote Cromwell so quickly through 1530–1533?
cards.answer: Cromwell's promotions tracked his usefulness, offering Henry a route to the annulment via statute that Wolsey, More and the bishops could not provide.

cards.front: In the truth table for (A AND B) OR (NOT C), why is the output True whenever C is False?
cards.answer: When C is False, NOT C is True, so the OR output is True regardless of A and B.

cards.front: Why does a bank transfer example use AND rather than OR to check authentication and funds?
cards.answer: Because both conditions (authenticated AND sufficient funds) must hold for the transfer to be authorised.

title: English sailors: Hawkins, Drake, Raleigh and exploration
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four connected reasons the lesson gives for why the Roanoke colony failed.
cards.answer: Site poorly chosen with shallow inlets / Arrived too late to plant crops / Violent breakdown with the Algonquian / War with Spain took ships away
items: Site poorly chosen with shallow inlets
Arrived too late to plant crops
War with Spain took ships away

cards.front: Name the three trading companies the lesson lists as part of England's wider sea power.
cards.answer: Muscovy Company (1555) / Levant Company (1581) / East India Company (1600)

cards.front: Why did the second Roanoke colony's food supply break down into violence with the Algonquian?
cards.answer: The colonists became dependent on the Algonquian for food after arriving too late to plant their own crops.

cards.front: Why is Hawkins's redesign of the navy from 1577 seen as his most lasting contribution?
cards.answer: His race-built galleons — lighter, faster and more heavily gunned — were the ships that defeated the Armada eleven years later.

cards.front: Name the three steps to measure the density of a liquid.
cards.answer: Measure mass of empty measuring cylinder / Pour in liquid and measure total mass / Read volume at bottom of meniscus, then apply ρ = m/V
items: Measure mass of empty measuring cylinder
Pour in liquid and measure total mass
Read volume at bottom of meniscus, then apply ρ = m/V

cards.front: Why does a liquid have a fixed volume but no fixed shape?
cards.answer: Particles are close together but the weaker forces between them let them slide past each other, so they flow into the container's shape while staying close together.

cards.front: Why does pressure in a fluid increase with depth?
cards.answer: A deeper column of fluid has more fluid weight above it, pressing down and increasing the force on any surface at that depth.

cards.front: Why is the density of a gas much lower than the same substance as a liquid?
cards.answer: Gas particles are very widely spaced compared to liquid particles, so the same mass occupies far more volume, making density about a thousand times lower.

cards.front: Name the four Catholic grievances in Northern Ireland listed by the lesson.
cards.answer: Discrimination in council housing allocation / Gerrymandered electoral boundaries / Discrimination in employment / Special powers act allowing detention without trial
items: Special powers act allowing detention without trial

cards.front: Why did the march in Londonderry/Derry on 5 October 1968 mark the start of the Troubles?
cards.answer: The RUC attacked the march with batons and it was filmed and broadcast, shocking British and international audiences.

cards.front: Why did internment in 1971 fail to suppress the IRA?
cards.answer: It used outdated intelligence, arrested mostly Catholics with no paramilitary links, which fuelled anger and swelled IRA recruitment.

cards.front: Why did the Sunningdale power-sharing executive collapse in 1974?
cards.answer: Unionists opposed the Irish dimension and the Ulster Workers' Council general strike brought Northern Ireland to a standstill, forcing its collapse.

cards.front: Name the three addition reactions alkenes undergo, given in the lesson (with hydrogen, water, and bromine).
cards.answer: With hydrogen to produce an alkane / With water/steam to produce an alcohol / With bromine to produce a dibromo compound
items: With hydrogen to produce an alkane
With water/steam to produce an alcohol
With bromine to produce a dibromo compound

cards.front: Why are alkenes more reactive than alkanes?
cards.answer: Because alkenes have a C=C double bond that can open up and react with other atoms.

cards.front: Why don't alkanes decolourise bromine water?
cards.answer: Because alkanes have no double bonds for bromine to add across.

cards.front: Why is the reaction of ethanol with sodium less vigorous than sodium with water?
cards.answer: The lesson states this reaction is less vigorous than sodium reacting with water.

title: Christian Beliefs: God, Creation and Jesus
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six events in the sequence of Jesus' last days given in Luke 22–24.
cards.answer: Last Supper / Betrayal and arrest in Gethsemane / Trial before High Priest and Pilate / Crucifixion on Golgotha / Burial / Resurrection
items: Trial before High Priest and Pilate

cards.front: How does substitutionary atonement explain how the cross achieves salvation?
cards.answer: Jesus took humanity's punishment for sin in their place.

cards.front: How does the moral influence theory explain how the cross achieves salvation?
cards.answer: The cross shows God's love so powerfully that it draws humanity to repentance.

title: The Depression and the rise of the Nazis 1929-1933
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the five intersecting factors the lesson gives for Hitler's rise to power.
cards.answer: The Depression (economic) / Failure of parliamentary government (political) / The divided left (party politics) / Nazi propaganda (movement strength) / Elite miscalculation by Hindenburg and von Papen (individual decisions)
items: Elite miscalculation by Hindenburg and von Papen (individual decisions)

cards.front: Name the three scapegoats the lesson says Nazi propaganda offered voters.
cards.answer: Jews / Marxists / The 'November criminals'

cards.front: Why did the collapse of the Grand Coalition in March 1930 end parliamentary government in Germany?
cards.answer: The SPD and Centre Party could not agree on funding unemployment benefits, so from then Germany was ruled by presidential decree under Article 48.

cards.front: Why did Germany's conservative elite support Hitler's appointment as Chancellor in January 1933?
cards.answer: The KPD's growth terrified them, so they believed they could use Hitler as a weapon against communism and then control him.

title: Pioneer Farmers, the Journey West and the Miners
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four types of hardship/danger the lesson gives for pioneers on the trail.
cards.answer: Disease (cholera, typhoid, dysentery) / Accidents (children run over, drownings, gunshots) / Weather (hailstorms, lightning, blizzards) / Oxen stampedes

cards.front: Name the two push factors and two pull factors the lesson gives for pioneer farmers going west.
cards.answer: Soil exhaustion in the east / The 1837 Panic (banking crisis) / Fertile Willamette Valley land / Free or cheap land

cards.front: Why did the Donner Party get trapped by snow in the Sierra Nevada in 1846?
cards.answer: They took an untested shortcut from a guidebook that cost about a month, so they reached the mountains just as heavy snow hit the passes.

cards.front: Why did the Gold Rush speed up calls for a transcontinental railroad?
cards.answer: Because the months-long sea route around Cape Horn was no longer fit for purpose given the huge numbers travelling to California.

cards.front: Name the three examples of juxtaposition the lesson gives from Julius Caesar.
cards.answer: Brutus's prose beside Antony's verse / Portia's courage beside Calpurnia's fear / conspirators' idealism beside triumvirate's ruthlessness

cards.front: Why does Antony's funeral speech overpower Brutus's, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Antony's verse gives his words musical, emotional power that overwhelms the reasoned appeal of Brutus's plain prose.

cards.front: How does dramatic irony make Brutus's decision to spare Antony land more powerfully?
cards.answer: The audience knows sparing Antony and letting him speak will be catastrophic, so each misjudgement carries force Brutus cannot see.

cards.front: How does the crowd's behaviour reveal the play's political message about democracy?
cards.answer: Their fickleness shows democracy is only as stable as the people's judgement, which a skilled speaker can manipulate.

title: Kingship, Succession and Ruling England in Richard's Absence
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five reasons the lesson gives for why royal government did not collapse during Richard's ten-year absence.
cards.answer: Strong existing institutions from Henry II / Hubert Walter's outstanding administration / Eleanor of Aquitaine as political fixer / John's failed 1191-94 power grab united barons / Pope and Archbishop anchored Richard's legitimacy
items: Strong existing institutions from Henry II
Eleanor of Aquitaine as political fixer
John's failed 1191-94 power grab united barons
Pope and Archbishop anchored Richard's legitimacy

cards.front: Name the four tasks the sheriff performed in each shire, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Collected royal revenues / Banked money at the Exchequer / Presided over the shire court / Led the county levy in arms
items: Led the county levy in arms

cards.front: Why did Richard sell offices, charters and castles soon after becoming king in 1189?
cards.answer: He needed money quickly to fund his crusade, so he raised cash by selling offices, charters and castles.

cards.front: Why did John's 1191-94 attempt to seize power actually help hold Richard's government together?
cards.answer: It gave the loyal barons a clear enemy to unite against, pushing them to defend Richard's government.

cards.front: Name the four forces the lesson gives for the growth of spectator sport in Victorian Britain.
cards.answer: Industrialisation creating concentrated working-class populations / Railways enabling travel to away matches / Legal reforms giving workers free time / Codification of rules by educated men
items: Railways enabling travel to away matches
Legal reforms giving workers free time
Codification of rules by educated men

cards.front: How did the 1885 legalisation of professional football change who could play the sport?
cards.answer: It opened the game to working-class players who could not afford to play as unpaid amateurs.

cards.front: How did the 1992 Premier League TV deal change English football?
cards.answer: Selling broadcast rights to Sky Sports raised wages sharply, brought overseas players, and turned clubs into global commercial brands.

cards.front: Why did the Football League's growth lead clubs to build enclosed grounds?
cards.answer: So they could charge admission to matches and use the income to fund their activities.

cards.front: Name the three types of evidence for evolution given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Fossil record / Comparative anatomy / DNA analysis

cards.front: List the four steps of Darwin's theory of natural selection.
cards.answer: Individuals show variation / Individuals compete for limited resources / Best suited survive and reproduce / Advantageous alleles passed to offspring

cards.front: Why did dark peppered moths become more common during the Industrial Revolution?
cards.answer: Pollution killed lichens and darkened tree bark, so dark moths were better camouflaged from predators and survived more.

cards.front: How does selective breeding make a population more vulnerable to disease?
cards.answer: It reduces genetic variation within the population, leaving fewer different traits to cope with disease.

title: Atoms, Elements and the Development of the Atomic Model
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three subatomic particles found in an atom.
cards.answer: Proton / Neutron / Electron

cards.front: Give the relative charges of the proton, neutron and electron.
cards.answer: Proton: +1 / Neutron: 0 / Electron: -1

cards.front: Why was the plum pudding model replaced after Rutherford's gold foil experiment?
cards.answer: A small fraction of alpha particles bounced back sharply, which the plum pudding model of diffuse positive charge could not explain.

cards.front: How did the discovery of isotopes refine Dalton's atomic theory?
cards.answer: Isotopes showed that not all atoms of an element are identical in mass, contradicting Dalton's claim that they were.

cards.front: Why does Jane refuse to accept jewels and silks from Rochester after the engagement?
cards.answer: Accepting his gifts would make her financially dependent on him and therefore unequal.

cards.front: How does the split chestnut tree act as pathetic fallacy for the relationship?
cards.answer: The tree torn in two by lightning symbolises the couple being torn apart by a destructive force.

cards.front: How does Bertha express her anger differently from Jane, according to the dark double reading?
cards.answer: Jane channels her anger into words, while Bertha expresses it through physical violence like tearing the veil and setting fires.

cards.front: Why does Gavin leave Otis Gaddarn's ultimate fate unknown at the end of the novel?
cards.answer: To show the system that enabled his crimes carries on unchanged, even though he himself is gone.

cards.front: How did Otis escape hanging earlier in the novel before becoming Philip Gaddarn?
cards.answer: He bribed officials to have an innocent man hanged in his place.

cards.front: Name the four defensive features of Krak des Chevaliers given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Two rings of walls / Towers projecting for enfilading fire / A glacis to deflect siege engines / Internal cisterns for water storage
items: A glacis to deflect siege engines

cards.front: Name the three siege weapons attackers used against crusader castles.
cards.answer: Trebuchets / Mangonels / Battering rams

cards.front: Why did the crusader states need military orders rather than relying on ordinary crusaders?
cards.answer: The Latin settler population was too small to garrison the frontier, and reinforcements from Europe often left after a short pilgrimage, so permanent professional soldiers were needed.

cards.front: How did a concentric castle design help defenders survive an attack?
cards.answer: If attackers breached the outer wall they were trapped in a narrow passage under fire from the higher inner wall, letting the garrison hold out longer.

cards.front: Name the four contrasting character pairs the lesson identifies for exam use.
cards.answer: Beatrice and Hero / Benedick and Claudio / Don Pedro and Don John / Dogberry and the aristocrats

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare give Don John a vague motivation rather than a developed psychology?
cards.answer: Because his function is to test other characters' trust and morals, not to be the real source of the play's problems.

cards.front: Name the three purposes the lesson gives for the Christian family.
cards.answer: Procreation / Security / Education

cards.front: Name three rites of passage the lesson says parishes hold for family life.
cards.answer: Infant baptism or dedication / Confirmation / Marriage services / Funerals

cards.front: Why does Catholic teaching hold that a validly sacramental marriage cannot be dissolved?
cards.answer: Because marriage is sacramental and conveys God's grace through the ritual itself, so it can only be annulled, not dissolved.

cards.front: Why do Quakers not need a priest for their marriage to be valid before God?
cards.answer: Because God is understood to be present directly in the gathered silence of worship, so no priestly mediation is required.

title: Performance Enhancing Drugs and Blood Doping
subject: physical-education-aqa

cards.front: Name the five main categories of prohibited substance the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Stimulants / Narcotic analgesics / Anabolic agents / Diuretics / Peptide hormones such as EPO

cards.front: What three counter-points does the lesson give against the 'level playing field' argument for doping?
cards.answer: Not all athletes dope, so clean athletes are disadvantaged / Wealthier athletes/nations dope more safely and effectively / It normalises a race to ever-higher health risks
items: Not all athletes dope, so clean athletes are disadvantaged
