Wealthier athletes/nations dope more safely and effectively
It normalises a race to ever-higher health risks

cards.front: Why can EPO use during sleep be especially dangerous?
cards.answer: Heart rate is low and blood flows slowly during sleep, so the thickened blood is more likely to cause clots, stroke or heart attack.

cards.front: Why is blood doping considered riskier than EPO use alone?
cards.answer: It carries the same blood-thickening risks as EPO but also risks infection from contaminated equipment and embolism from the transfusion process.

title: Scale and Ownership of Retail Businesses
subject: l12-retail-business

cards.front: Name the four business scale categories used to classify retail businesses by employee count.
cards.answer: Micro (fewer than 10) / Small (10-49) / Medium (50-249) / Large (250 or more)

cards.front: Name the four forms of business ownership described for retail businesses.
cards.answer: Sole trader / Partnership / Private limited company (Ltd) / Franchise

cards.front: Why is a franchise a lower-risk way to start a retail business than starting independently?
cards.answer: The brand is already known and its products are proven, and the franchisor provides training, marketing and operational support.

cards.front: Why does a private limited company (Ltd) face more pressure to maximise profit than a sole trader?
cards.answer: It has shareholders who expect returns on their investment, pushing the business to grow profit and market share.

title: Plot and Structure: Five Acts, One Week
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the five days across which the action of Romeo and Juliet unfolds, in order, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Lovers meet Sunday evening / Marry on Monday / Romeo banished Tuesday / Juliet drinks potion Wednesday night / Tragedy ends early Thursday

cards.front: Why does the lesson say the true dramatic climax is Act Five, not Act Three?
cards.answer: Act Three is the turning point where fortune reverses, but the highest stakes are only resolved in the Act Five tomb scene.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare have the prologue tell the audience the ending before the play begins?
cards.answer: He is not interested in suspense over the lovers' deaths but in the audience watching how and why it happens, knowing it cannot be stopped.

cards.front: How does the compressed five-day timeline affect the audience's feeling about the play's events?
cards.answer: It makes every action feel irreversible and every delay feel fatal, building urgency into the play's structure.

cards.front: Name the three main meals of the day given in the lesson, in German.
cards.answer: das Frühstück / das Mittagessen / das Abendessen

cards.front: Name the four German dishes the lesson lists as popular German food culture examples.
cards.answer: Bratwurst / Wiener Schnitzel / Käsespätzle / Brezel

cards.front: Why does 'du' change to 'isst' instead of 'esst' when conjugating essen?
cards.answer: Essen is a strong verb, so its stem vowel changes from 'e' to 'i' in the du and er/sie forms.

cards.front: Why is 'Ich gern Cola' grammatically wrong in German?
cards.answer: Because gern and its variants must come after a conjugated verb, so you need 'Ich trinke gern Cola.'

cards.front: Name the five steps for drawing a ray diagram for reflection off a mirror.
cards.answer: Draw the mirror as a straight line / Draw the normal at 90° to the surface / Draw the incident ray arriving at the surface / Measure the angle of incidence / Draw the reflected ray at the same angle
items: Draw the mirror as a straight line
Draw the normal at 90° to the surface
Draw the incident ray arriving at the surface
Draw the reflected ray at the same angle

cards.front: In the glass block core practical, why does light bend towards the normal when entering the glass?
cards.answer: Because light slows down when it moves from the less dense air into the denser glass.

cards.front: How do electrons in atoms produce electromagnetic radiation?
cards.answer: When electrons move from a higher energy level to a lower one, they emit EM radiation, with frequency depending on the energy difference.

cards.front: Name four practical changes that de-Stalinisation involved.
cards.answer: Gulag prisoners released / Terror victims rehabilitated / Stalin's body removed from mausoleum / Stalin's portraits and statues removed

cards.front: Name four factors that weakened Khrushchev's position by 1964.
cards.answer: Failure of Virgin Lands scheme / Cuban Missile Crisis humiliation / Deteriorating relations with China / Erratic leadership style

cards.front: Why did the Politburo have Beria arrested and executed so quickly after Stalin's death?
cards.answer: Other Politburo members feared him above all other potential successors as the powerful secret police chief.

cards.front: Why did the Hungarian Uprising of 1956 show that de-Stalinisation had strict limits?
cards.answer: Political reform was tolerated within the USSR, but Hungary's attempt at genuine independence was crushed by Soviet tanks.

title: The Black Death & Public Health in Medieval England
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four explanations medieval people gave for what caused the Black Death.
cards.answer: God's punishment / Miasma (bad air) / Astrology / Imbalance of the Four Humours

cards.front: Name the three prevention attempts used against the Black Death.
cards.answer: Fleeing infected areas / Quarantine measures / Cleaning streets

cards.front: Why did flagellants whip themselves in public during the Black Death?
cards.answer: Because they believed the plague was God's punishment for sin and hoped whipping would earn forgiveness.

cards.front: How could prevention measures based on miasma theory still reduce the spread of plague?
cards.answer: Cleaning streets and quarantine accidentally improved hygiene and limited contact between people, even though the theory behind them was wrong.

cards.front: Name the four things Kristallnacht (November 1938) destroyed or caused, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: 7,500 Jewish-owned businesses destroyed / 1,400 synagogues burned / At least 91 Jews killed / 30,000 Jewish men arrested

cards.front: Name the three ways Nazi schools changed subjects to fit Nazi ideology.
cards.answer: History rewritten to glorify Germany / Biology taught racial theory / Physical education expanded

cards.front: How did the Nazis reduce official unemployment figures without necessarily creating real jobs?
cards.answer: They removed women from unemployment statistics by encouraging them to leave work, and conscription from 1935 removed men from the count.

cards.front: Why did Nazi policy on women shift towards drawing them back into the workforce from the late 1930s?
cards.answer: Rearmament created labour shortages, showing the tension between Nazi ideology and economic reality.

title: The Human Personality and Human Destiny
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Why does Theravada Buddhism teach that no permanent self exists in a person?
cards.answer: Experience is made up of the Five Aggregates constantly arising and interacting, and no single one nor all combined form a fixed, unchanging 'I'.

cards.front: Why do Bodhisattvas delay their own final liberation?
cards.answer: Because they generate bodhicitta and vow to remain in the cycle of existence until every sentient being has been liberated.

cards.front: How does Pure Land Buddhism teach that a person can be reborn in the Pure Land?
cards.answer: Through devotion to Amitabha Buddha and reciting his name, which brings rebirth in a realm ideal for attaining Enlightenment.

title: RC Time Delays and the 555 Monostable
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four internal parts of the 555 timer IC described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Internal comparator / Bistable latch / Discharge transistor / Voltage divider

cards.front: List the sequence of steps in a 555 monostable cycle from stable state to reset, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Output LOW, capacitor held discharged / Trigger pulse takes pin 2 below one-third supply / Output goes HIGH, discharge transistor turns off / Capacitor charges through R towards supply / Capacitor reaches two-thirds supply, bistable resets / Output LOW, discharge transistor discharges capacitor
items: Trigger pulse takes pin 2 below one-third supply
Output goes HIGH, discharge transistor turns off
Capacitor charges through R towards supply
Capacitor reaches two-thirds supply, bistable resets
Output LOW, discharge transistor discharges capacitor

cards.front: Why does a plain RC delay circuit have an uncertain threshold compared to a 555 monostable?
cards.answer: Its output is just a gradual rising voltage with no comparator or latch to give a sharp, precise switching point.

cards.front: Why can the 555 monostable output drive loads like LEDs or relays directly without extra transistors?
cards.answer: Because its output is buffered and can source or sink up to 200 mA.

cards.front: Name the four quotations the lesson says to prepare, one for each theme (identity, religion/sexuality, mother-daughter, storytelling)
cards.answer: everyone has a demon / I miss God / friends and enemies / everyone tells a story differently

cards.front: Why does the mother's controlling behaviour towards Jeanette count as both sympathetic and destructive?
cards.answer: Her control comes from genuine devotion, believing she is saving Jeanette's soul, yet it still damages Jeanette.

cards.front: Why does the novel suggest belonging and freedom are a false choice?
cards.answer: The church offers belonging but demands surrendered freedom, whereas a more compassionate community, like Elsie, could offer both.

cards.front: How should you use context when answering the extract-based prose question?
cards.answer: Only embed it inside an analytical point, since context alone earns no marks on this question.

title: Linking the Unseen Poem to Your Anthology Cluster
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Name the three kinds of connection between poems that the lesson says are worth writing about.
cards.answer: Same idea, different feeling / Same feeling, different method / Direct disagreement

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson tells you not to do in this comparison.
cards.answer: Summarise the poems before comparing / Save comparison for the conclusion / Invent context for the unseen poem
items: Invent context for the unseen poem

cards.front: Why is direct disagreement called the strongest structure available for a comparison paragraph?
cards.answer: Because the unseen poem contradicts the anthology poem outright, so the whole response can be built around that clear disagreement.

cards.front: Why does inventing context for the unseen poem not help your comparison?
cards.answer: You cannot actually know who wrote it or when, and background about it earns no marks anyway.

cards.front: Name the four sources of background radiation the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Rocks (especially granite) / Cosmic rays from space / Radon gas in the air / Food and drink / Medical procedures

cards.front: Name the four non-ionising types of radiation listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Visible light / Infrared / Microwaves / Radio waves

cards.front: Why can inhaling or swallowing an alpha-emitting substance be dangerous even though alpha can't penetrate skin?
cards.answer: Once inside the body the alpha particles deliver their full energy directly to sensitive tissue close by.

cards.front: Why can low doses of ionising radiation cause cancer without killing the cell?
cards.answer: The radiation can alter the cell's DNA without killing it, causing the mutated cell to divide uncontrollably.

cards.front: How does attention move information from the sensory register into short-term memory?
cards.answer: Selectively attending to something, like hearing your name in a noisy room, transfers it into STM for conscious processing.

cards.front: How does the Clive Wearing case study challenge the multi-store model's view of long-term memory?
cards.answer: His hippocampal damage disrupted new episodic memories but left procedural memory intact, suggesting LTM is not one unitary store.

cards.front: According to the lesson, over what four areas does Jesus show authority through his miracles in Mark?
cards.answer: The natural world / The spirit world / Disease / Death

cards.front: What five miracle passages does the lesson identify as the ones to know for Mark's Gospel?
cards.answer: Calming the storm / Feeding the five thousand / Walking on water / Healing of Legion / Raising of Jairus's daughter

cards.front: Why does the calming of the storm suggest Jesus has divine power, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: In Old Testament scripture God alone stills seas and storms, so Jesus doing this implies he has God's power over nature.

cards.front: How does Mark use the twelve baskets in the feeding of the five thousand to add meaning?
cards.answer: The twelve baskets of leftovers may represent the twelve tribes of Israel, giving the miracle extra theological significance.

title: Twentieth-Century Colour: Orchestration, Dynamics and Space
subject: music-aqa

cards.front: Name the five clues the lesson gives for spotting twentieth-century colour in an unfamiliar extract.
cards.answer: Is timbre doing more than decorating a tune / Is texture wide open or densely packed / Are dynamics building over a long span / Is there any trace of jazz or blues / Could the forces be a wind band
items: Is timbre doing more than decorating a tune
Is texture wide open or densely packed
Are dynamics building over a long span
Is there any trace of jazz or blues
Could the forces be a wind band

cards.front: Why can the same melody sound completely different in two performances, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because it depends on which instrument plays it, how loudly, and how many other parts surround it.

cards.front: How does a widely spaced, open texture differ in effect from a dense, layered one?
cards.answer: Open texture uses a single line with few sustained notes and a wide gap between parts, sounding spacious and calm, while dense texture crowds many independent lines together for contrast.

cards.front: How is extended tonality or modal writing different from fully atonal music like twelve-note serialism?
cards.answer: Extended tonality and modal music still point towards a home key, while fully atonal music abandons a home key altogether.

cards.front: Why does Juliet refuse to leave the tomb with the Friar and choose to die instead?
cards.answer: She has the option to escape but chooses to join Romeo, making her death a decisive choice, not despair.

cards.front: How does the failure of the Friar's letter reflect the play's theme of fate?
cards.answer: An impersonal, random event (plague quarantine) intervenes at the worst moment, suggesting fate conspires against the lovers.

title: High-tech warfare and the Iraq War 2003
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four tactics the lesson gives for the insurgency's asymmetric campaign against coalition troops.
cards.answer: IEDs on main supply routes / sniper attacks / mortar fire on bases / suicide bombings of police and civilians
items: suicide bombings of police and civilians

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why the Iraq occupation failed.
cards.answer: high-tech tools unsuited to street-level intelligence work in Arabic / de-Baathification threw 400,000 trained men onto the streets / political reconstruction planned with optimism rather than rigour
items: high-tech tools unsuited to street-level intelligence work in Arabic
de-Baathification threw 400,000 trained men onto the streets
political reconstruction planned with optimism rather than rigour

cards.front: Why did British and American forces succeed quickly in the 2003 Iraq invasion?
cards.answer: They had near-total air dominance, GPS-guided artillery, satellite and drone reconnaissance, encrypted communications and a professional volunteer force.

cards.front: Why couldn't precision weapons and ISTAR defeat the insurgency in Basra?
cards.answer: They could destroy a confirmed target but could not identify which civilians were militia or which ditch hid an IED.

cards.front: Name the four overlapping pressures the lesson gives for the break with Rome.
cards.answer: Failure of the annulment / King's claim to imperial sovereignty / Wealth of the English Church / Evangelical sympathies of Cromwell, Cranmer and Anne Boleyn
items: Evangelical sympathies of Cromwell, Cranmer and Anne Boleyn

cards.front: Name the three roles Cromwell used to enforce the break with Rome, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Administered the oath of supremacy to clergy / Set up an information network on dissident speech / Issued royal injunctions in 1536 for English teaching
items: Administered the oath of supremacy to clergy
Set up an information network on dissident speech
Issued royal injunctions in 1536 for English teaching

cards.front: Why did Henry conclude by 1530 that Rome could not solve his annulment problem?
cards.answer: Because Blackfriars collapsed in 1529 and Pope Clement VII revoked the case to Rome, leaving no English answer available through Roman channels.

cards.front: Why was cutting ties with Rome financially attractive to Henry?
cards.answer: The English Church owned about a fifth of the country's landed wealth and paid annual fees to Rome, which cutting off could transform royal finance.

title: Wave Interaction: Reflection, Refraction and Lenses
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the three principal rays used to draw a converging-lens ray diagram.
cards.answer: Ray parallel to axis refracts through far focal point / Ray through optical centre passes straight through / Ray through near focal point emerges parallel to axis
items: Ray parallel to axis refracts through far focal point
Ray through optical centre passes straight through
Ray through near focal point emerges parallel to axis

cards.front: Give the three properties of the image formed when an object is beyond 2f from a converging lens.
cards.answer: Real / Inverted / Diminished

cards.front: Why does violet light spread out from red light when white light passes through a prism?
cards.answer: Violet light slows down more than red light when entering glass, so it refracts by a different amount, spreading the colours.

cards.front: Why does a red jumper appear red?
cards.answer: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours of light.

cards.front: Name the five materials the lesson says Mycenaean craftsmen worked in.
cards.answer: Gold / Silver / Bronze / Ivory / Glass paste

cards.front: Name the three shapes of Mycenaean terracotta figurines given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Phi figurines / Psi figurines / Tau figurines

cards.front: Why can't archaeologists say who personally owned the gold objects from the shaft graves?
cards.answer: Archaeology gives us objects, not individual lives, so ownership and personal meaning cannot be confirmed from the finds alone.

cards.front: Why do the phi, psi and tau figurines suggest they were not exclusively elite items?
cards.answer: They are found in enormous numbers across graves, houses and sanctuaries, suggesting mass production accessible across social levels.

cards.front: Name the four vehicle safety features the lesson describes that use momentum principles.
cards.answer: Crumple zones / Airbags / Seat belts / ABS brakes

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives that increase braking distance.
cards.answer: Higher vehicle speed / Greater vehicle mass / Poor road conditions / Poor brake or tyre condition

cards.front: Why does greater vehicle mass increase braking distance?
cards.answer: A greater mass means the vehicle has more kinetic energy that needs to be removed to stop it.

cards.front: How does seat belt stretch reduce injury in a collision?
cards.answer: The seat belt stretches slightly, increasing the time over which momentum changes, reducing peak forces on the body.

cards.front: Name the five prescribed books of the Odyssey and what happens in each.
cards.answer: Book 9: the Cyclops episode / Book 10: encounter with Circe / Book 19: recognition by nurse Eurycleia / Book 21: the contest of the bow / Book 22: slaughter of the suitors
items: Book 21: the contest of the bow

cards.front: Why does Homer make Odysseus tell his own adventures (Books 9-12) as a flashback rather than narrating them directly?
cards.answer: It lets Odysseus be his own storyteller, showing he is a man of words as much as deeds, which is part of his heroism.

cards.front: Name the three body responses the lesson gives for warming the body when it is too cold.
cards.answer: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to skin / Muscles shiver to generate heat / Body hairs stand up to trap air
items: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to skin
Body hairs stand up to trap air

cards.front: What two signals does the thermoregulatory centre in the brain receive to monitor temperature?
cards.answer: Skin receptors monitoring external temperature / Blood receptors monitoring core temperature

cards.front: Why does urine become concentrated when a person is dehydrated?
cards.answer: Dehydration triggers more ADH release, so the kidneys reabsorb more water, leaving less water in the urine.

cards.front: Why is severe hypothermia dangerous for the body's cells?
cards.answer: Core temperature drops well below 37°C, making enzymes work too slowly, slowing reflexes and risking organ failure.

cards.front: Name the four things that make Owen's soldiers' deaths so futile in 'Exposure', according to the 'nothing happens' refrain.
cards.answer: Cold / Boredom / Neglect / Waiting

cards.front: How does the structure of 'Exposure' mirror the soldiers' physical state?
cards.answer: Eight five-line stanzas end in a shortened half-line, creating a 'dying fall' that mirrors soldiers slowly losing strength and life.

cards.front: Why does Heaney describe the barren earth as an advantage in 'Storm on the Island'?
cards.answer: Because nothing grows there, the wind has nothing (like hay) to destroy, turning the barren landscape into unexpected protection.

cards.front: How do Owen and Heaney both use the pronoun 'we' to shape the reader's response?
cards.answer: Both use 'we' to create collective, communal experience, showing shared vulnerability rather than individual suffering.

cards.front: Name the four scales of production for timber products given in the lesson.
cards.answer: One-off (bespoke) production / Batch production / Mass production / Continuous (flow) production

cards.front: Name the six principles of the 6 Rs framework applied to timber.
cards.answer: Refuse / Rethink / Reduce / Reuse / Recycle / Repair

cards.front: Why does batch production use jigs and templates for a set of identical oak chairs?
cards.answer: Jigs and templates ensure consistency across all units in the batch.

cards.front: Why is thermally modified timber considered more environmentally responsible than pressure-treated timber?
cards.answer: It uses only heat with no added chemicals, so it is safe near gardens and water and needs no specialist disposal.

cards.front: What three arguments did Phyllis Schlafly's STOP ERA campaign use against the amendment, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Would remove beneficial protections for women / Would remove exemption from military draft / Would lead to unisex toilets and other alarming outcomes
items: Would remove beneficial protections for women
Would remove exemption from military draft
Would lead to unisex toilets and other alarming outcomes

cards.front: Why is Roe v Wade (1973) seen as a limited victory for the feminist movement?
cards.answer: It was framed around privacy rather than sex equality, and immediately triggered a powerful conservative counter-movement.

title: Pilgrimage, Festivals and the Local Church Community
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the three key events in the Easter narrative, in order.
cards.answer: Last Supper (Matthew 26:17-29) / Crucifixion (Matthew 27:45-55) / Resurrection (Matthew 28:1-10)

cards.front: Name four ways the local church supports its community beyond Sunday services and rites of passage.
cards.answer: Sunday schools for children / Youth clubs and after-school groups / Mother-and-child groups / Visiting the elderly and sick

cards.front: Why are many Protestant Christians cautious about pilgrimage?
cards.answer: They argue God is equally accessible anywhere, the Bible doesn't command it, and it risks becoming superstitious idolatry.

cards.front: Why is Easter considered the most important festival in the Christian year?
cards.answer: It confirms that death has been defeated and salvation is available to all, uniting denominations who disagree on other things.

cards.front: Name the four instances of manipulation the lesson gives across the play.
cards.answer: Cassius manipulates Brutus into the conspiracy / Decius manipulates Caesar by reinterpreting Calpurnia's dream / Antony manipulates the crowd into rioting / Brutus manipulates himself in his orchard soliloquy
items: Cassius manipulates Brutus into the conspiracy
Decius manipulates Caesar by reinterpreting Calpurnia's dream
Antony manipulates the crowd into rioting
Brutus manipulates himself in his orchard soliloquy

cards.front: Name the four characters' loyalties the lesson describes as tested in the play.
cards.answer: Brutus loyal to Rome over Caesar / Cassius loyal to himself over the republic / Antony loyal to Caesar's memory but not moral principles / Portia loyal to Brutus to self-destruction
items: Brutus loyal to Rome over Caesar
Cassius loyal to himself over the republic
Antony loyal to Caesar's memory but not moral principles
Portia loyal to Brutus to self-destruction

cards.front: How does Antony turn the word 'honourable' into an insult when describing the conspirators?
cards.answer: He repeats it sarcastically about their killing of Caesar until the word's meaning is exposed as false.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare present rhetoric as the play's most dangerous force?
cards.answer: A skilled speaker can make murder seem like patriotism, turn grief into a weapon, or disguise jealousy as principle.

title: Electronic Configuration & Trends in the Periodic Table
subject: science-edexcel

cards.front: What are the maximum electron capacities of the first three electron shells?
cards.answer: First shell: 2 electrons / Second shell: 8 electrons / Third shell: 8 electrons

cards.front: The lesson gives four examples of Period 3 elements showing changing reactivity across the period. What are they and their types?
cards.answer: Sodium - highly reactive metal / Silicon - metalloid / Chlorine - reactive non-metal / Argon - unreactive noble gas

cards.front: How can you tell if an element is a metal or non-metal just from its outer-shell electron count?
cards.answer: Metals typically have 1, 2 or 3 outer-shell electrons, easily lost to form positive ions, while non-metals have 4 or more (or a full shell).

cards.front: Why does the type of element change from reactive metal to unreactive noble gas across a period?
cards.answer: The number of outer-shell electrons increases by one across the period while the number of shells stays the same, changing reactivity.

cards.front: Name the four steps the lesson gives for structuring a theme-based Shakespeare answer.
cards.answer: Extract analysis / Whole-play links / Embed context / Explore ambiguity

cards.front: Name the four assessment objectives the lesson says Shakespeare essays are judged across.
cards.answer: AO1 (informed personal response using well-chosen textual references) / AO2 (analysis of how Shakespeare uses language, form and structure) / AO3 (understanding of the play in its contexts) / AO4 (accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar)
items: AO1 informed personal response with textual references
AO2 analysis of language, form and structure
AO4 accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar

cards.front: Why does the lesson say human relationships should matter more than wealth, even though money decides every outcome?
cards.answer: Because the play shows love, loyalty and trust as truly valuable through Shylock's bond, Portia's giving and Antonio's risk, despite money still controlling events.

cards.front: How should context be used in a Shakespeare essay, according to the exam technique advice?
cards.answer: Woven into analysis rather than written as a separate context paragraph, showing how different audiences might read the same moment.

cards.front: What are the four steps of the Extract Analysis Method for the language/structure task?
cards.answer: Read the extract twice / Identify 3-4 language features / Analyse, don't identify / Embed context where it fits naturally
items: Embed context where it fits naturally

cards.front: What are the four steps of the Whole Text Method for the wider-text question?
cards.answer: Plan for range across the novel / Memorise key quotations / Analyse language within wider points / Compare characters or ideas
items: Plan for range across the novel

cards.front: How does Godfrey's pursuit of wealth and status lead to his suffering?
cards.answer: He prioritises wealth and social standing over his daughter, resulting in a childless, guilt-ridden marriage.

cards.front: Why does 'naming' a language feature earn few marks in the extract task?
cards.answer: Because identifying a feature without explaining its effect on the reader shows no real analysis, unlike explaining what it makes the reader think and feel.

cards.front: Why does Posner reject Dakin's comparison of the death camps to the Dissolution of the Monasteries?
cards.answer: Because Posner says, 'I didn't lose any relatives in the Dissolution of the Monasteries,' making the Holocaust personal not abstract.

cards.front: Why is Posner unable to accept the boys' use of 'context' in the Holocaust lesson?
cards.answer: Because he sees putting something in context as a step towards explaining it, and explaining it as a step towards explaining it away.

cards.front: Why does Bennett suggest Irwin's contrarian approach to history is dangerous beyond the classroom?
cards.answer: Because if history is just argument and perspective, there is no objective truth, so Holocaust denial becomes just another contrarian position.

cards.front: Why does neither Hector's reverence nor Irwin's analysis fully serve the boys, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Hector's reverence is inadequate for an exam system needing analysis, while Irwin's analysis is inadequate for a subject demanding reverence.

cards.front: Why does Wells have the artilleryman talk about selecting the 'strong' to survive?
cards.answer: To satirise Social Darwinism as a self-serving fantasy that justifies abandoning others while doing nothing.

cards.front: How does the curate's collapse show the failure of religion in the novel?
cards.answer: His faith offers no comfort or guidance and collapses into hysteria under the pressure of the invasion.

title: The UK in the World: International Organisations
subject: citizenship-aqa

cards.front: Name the UK's five main international organisations.
cards.answer: United Nations / NATO / Commonwealth / Council of Europe / World Trade Organisation

cards.front: Name the five permanent members of the UN Security Council.
cards.answer: UK / United States / China / France / Russia

cards.front: Why can UN peacekeepers use force during a mission?
cards.answer: Only in self-defence or to protect civilians, and they must act with the host nation's consent where possible.

cards.front: Why do critics argue the UN Security Council veto can be a problem?
cards.answer: Because it can prevent timely action when permanent members have conflicting interests, as seen in several conflicts since 1945.

title: Family Life, Women and the Marriage Law
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four aspects of pre-1949 family life shaped by Confucian patriarchy that the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Arranged child marriage / Bride prices / Legal concubinage in wealthy households / Female infanticide in poor villages / Foot binding

cards.front: The lesson gives four 'genuine gains' for women under Mao's rule — what are they?
cards.answer: End of foot binding / Legal right to divorce / Mass literacy / Near-universal urban employment by 1976

cards.front: Why did the 1950 Marriage Law provoke violent backlash in rural China?
cards.answer: Husbands, mothers-in-law and clan elders saw it as an attack on the family economy since a divorced wife could take property and remarry.

cards.front: How did the 1958 communes disrupt traditional family life?
cards.answer: They banned family cooking for communal mess halls, made childcare collective and abolished private plots under the slogan 'production over kinship'.

title: Cold War End, the Gulf War and Oslo, 1989–95
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four conditions the lesson gives that together made Oslo possible.
cards.answer: End of Cold War removed Soviet support for rejectionism / Gulf War cost the PLO its funding / Madrid Conference brought all regional states together / Rabin's 1992 election win
items: End of Cold War removed Soviet support for rejectionism
Gulf War cost the PLO its funding
Madrid Conference brought all regional states together

cards.front: Name the three final-status issues the lesson says Oslo deferred and never resolved (plus one more).
cards.answer: Refugees / Jerusalem / Settlements / Borders

cards.front: Why was the thirty-five-state Gulf War coalition of 1990-91 significant for Middle East diplomacy?
cards.answer: It included Arab states like Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Morocco alongside NATO allies, a line-up impossible during the Cold War.

cards.front: How did Rabin's restraint during the Gulf War Scud attacks benefit Israel afterwards?
cards.answer: Israeli restraint was visibly valuable to the US, creating a debt the next administration could later collect in peace diplomacy.

cards.front: Name the four impacts of production technology on a business that the lesson gives.
cards.answer: lower unit costs / higher productivity / more consistent quality / faster product flexibility (smart systems)

cards.front: Why does getting batch size wrong reduce the cost savings of batch production?
cards.answer: Too small a batch means changeover costs dominate, while too large a batch leaves unsold stock.

cards.front: Why can modern 'smart' factories with reprogrammable robots be more flexible than older flow lines?
cards.answer: Reprogrammable robots can be switched to make different products faster than people could, unlike rigid old lines.

title: The Nervous System and Fight or Flight
subject: psychology-aqa

cards.front: Name the four physical changes the lesson gives for when the sympathetic branch activates.
cards.answer: heart beats faster / breathing quickens / pupils dilate / digestion slows / adrenaline released

cards.front: Why can chronic stress harm physical health, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Chronic stress keeps the sympathetic ANS activated, raising blood pressure and suppressing the immune system.

cards.front: Why does the James–Lange theory struggle to explain how we tell fear and excitement apart?
cards.answer: Fear and excitement produce similar bodily states, so interpreting bodily changes alone can't distinguish between them.

cards.front: Name the four sources of support for McCarthy that the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Republican politicians attacking Democrats / business conservatives resenting the New Deal / ordinary Americans frightened by events / religious groups fearing Communism as atheist threat
items: business conservatives resenting the New Deal
religious groups fearing Communism as atheist threat

cards.front: Name the three types of workplace the blacklist operated in.
cards.answer: Hollywood / the civil service / universities

cards.front: Why did McCarthy's accusation at Wheeling in 1950 land so powerfully with the public?
cards.answer: It came right after Alger Hiss's conviction, the Soviet atomic bomb test, and China 'falling' to Communism, fuelling existing fear.

cards.front: How did McCarthy silence people who criticised his methods?
cards.answer: He called his critics Communist sympathisers, making it dangerous for anyone to publicly oppose him.

title: Magnets, Electromagnetism and the Motor Effect
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the four magnetic materials given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Iron / Steel / Cobalt / Nickel

cards.front: Name the three ways given to increase the speed of a d.c. motor.
cards.answer: Increasing the current / Using a stronger magnet / Adding more turns to the coil
items: Adding more turns to the coil

cards.front: Why are permanent magnets made from steel rather than soft iron?
cards.answer: Soft iron loses its magnetism as soon as it leaves a magnetic field, unlike steel.

cards.front: Why does a d.c. motor coil rotate continuously instead of stopping after 180°?
cards.answer: The split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn, keeping the force acting in the right direction.

title: Mechanical Calculations: Stress, Strain, Young's Modulus and Factors of Safety
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Why does a thin cable snap before a thick cable under the same load?
cards.answer: A thinner cable has a smaller cross-sectional area, so the same force produces higher stress.

cards.front: Why are brittle materials used for bricks in walls but avoided where tensile impact loads occur?
cards.answer: Brittle materials cope well with compressive loads but fracture suddenly with no warning under tensile impact.

cards.front: Why might choosing a higher factor of safety make a component less desirable?
cards.answer: Higher factor of safety values can mean heavier and more expensive components.

title: Deep Time and the Age of the Earth
subject: geology-eduqas

cards.front: Why was John Joly's ocean salinity estimate for Earth's age too low?
cards.answer: It assumed salt only accumulated, ignoring that salt is removed by evaporite formation and subduction into the mantle.

cards.front: Why did geologists conclude Ussher's 6,000-year estimate was wrong?
cards.answer: Processes like sedimentation, erosion and uplift observed in rock strata could not have produced the geological record in only 6,000 years.

cards.front: In the toilet-roll analogy, what does the lesson say each part represents?
cards.answer: Each sheet = one million years / Whole roll (500 sheets) = 500 million years / Full Earth history = about nine rolls / Human history = thinner than the printed ink
items: Full Earth history = about nine rolls
Human history = thinner than the printed ink

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson says drive change in the fight against lung cancer.
cards.answer: Science and technology / Government and institutions / Attitudes in society / Individuals

cards.front: Name the four modern treatment methods for lung cancer given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Surgery / Chemotherapy / Radiotherapy / Immunotherapy

cards.front: Why does chemotherapy often cause severe side effects?
cards.answer: Because the powerful drugs used to kill cancer cells also damage healthy cells.

cards.front: Why is early detection of lung cancer so important for survival?
cards.answer: Early detection significantly improves survival rates, and lung cancer is often diagnosed late, lowering overall survival.

title: Characters: Rani, Hari, Abdul and the Queen
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the three betrayals in Rani's arc that the lesson describes as repeated betrayal.
cards.answer: Susan Matthews abandons her at Tilbury with no contract / Lord Oakham seduces her then denies the child / She leaves her newborn on the docks from desperation
items: Susan Matthews abandons her at Tilbury with no contract
Lord Oakham seduces her then denies the child
She leaves her newborn on the docks from desperation

cards.front: Name the four stages of Hari's journey a designer could show through costume changes.
cards.answer: barefoot undernourished lascar in rough cotton / beaten bloodied figure thrown ashore at the Cape / man digging in a diamond mine / well-fitted brown suit in the final Tilbury scene
items: barefoot undernourished lascar in rough cotton
beaten bloodied figure thrown ashore at the Cape
man digging in a diamond mine
well-fitted brown suit in the final Tilbury scene

cards.front: Why does Victoria retract the honour she wanted to give Abdul?
cards.answer: Her household threatens to declare her insane if she continues to honour him, so she keeps him as Munshi but withdraws the honour.

cards.front: Why does Abdul's promotion to munshi fail to protect him after Victoria's death?
cards.answer: The wider royal household, especially Lady Sarah, never accepts the promotion, and this lasting hostility destroys him once Victoria dies.

cards.front: Name the five common validation checks the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Presence check / Range check / Type check / Length check / Format check

cards.front: Name the five examples of misuse the lesson gives that a program must anticipate.
cards.answer: Leaving a required field empty / Typing letters where a number is expected / Entering an impossible value like -5 / Giving a date that does not exist / Pasting in an enormous amount of text
items: Typing letters where a number is expected
Giving a date that does not exist
Pasting in an enormous amount of text

cards.front: Why does a range check fail to catch a wrong year of birth like 1999 instead of 2000?
cards.answer: Because a range check only confirms the year is a sensible four-digit number, not that it is actually correct.

cards.front: Why does consistent indentation help make code maintainable?
cards.answer: It shows the shape of the code so readers can see which lines sit inside a loop or condition.

cards.front: Why can deflation lead to a damaging downward spiral in the economy?
cards.answer: Consumers delay spending expecting further price falls, demand drops, so firms cut output and jobs, worsening the economy.

cards.front: Why does the Bank of England Governor sometimes have to write a letter to the Chancellor?
cards.answer: Because CPI inflation has moved more than 1 percentage point above or below the 2% target.

cards.front: In the required practical on acceleration, name the two pieces of apparatus used to measure motion of the trolley.
cards.answer: Light gate / Ticker tape timer

cards.front: Why do two cars travelling at 30 m/s in opposite directions have different velocities but the same speed?
cards.answer: Speed only measures how fast they move, but velocity includes direction, and their directions are opposite.

cards.front: How can you show that F = ma using the required practical results?
cards.answer: Plotting force against acceleration gives a straight line through the origin, showing they are directly proportional.

cards.front: What does a downward sloping line on a velocity-time graph show about the object's motion?
cards.answer: The object is decelerating, meaning its velocity is decreasing over time.

title: Yalta, Potsdam and the changing order 1945-1948
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Why did the atmosphere at Potsdam become much cooler than at Yalta?
cards.answer: Truman had replaced Roosevelt, the USA had tested the atomic bomb, and Stalin's Soviet-dominated buffer in Eastern Europe was already visible.

cards.front: Why did the February 1948 Czech coup shock Western opinion and push towards NATO?
cards.answer: Czechoslovakia had kept a coalition government and free press longer than others, so its forcible takeover alarmed the West into discussing a defence pact.

cards.front: Name the four countries where salami tactics dismantled coalition governments between 1945-1948.
cards.answer: Poland / Hungary / Romania / Bulgaria

cards.front: Give the six deaths or losses caused by the Agra treasure that Doyle uses to show greed's consequences.
cards.answer: The merchant is murdered / The four conspirators are imprisoned / Sholto dies tormented by guilt / Morstan dies in an argument over it / Bartholomew is murdered for it / Small loses the treasure and his freedom
items: Morstan dies in an argument over it
Small loses the treasure and his freedom

cards.front: Why does Jonathan Small throw the Agra treasure into the Thames rather than let it be captured?
cards.answer: He realises he cannot escape and would rather destroy the treasure than let anyone else have it.

cards.front: How does the contrast between Watson and Holmes's endings reflect the novel's dual structure?
cards.answer: Watson moves forward into marriage and emotional fulfilment while Holmes stays trapped in a cycle of cases and cocaine, showing emotion versus intellect.

cards.front: Why is journalism a meaningful choice of career for Dante within the novel's structure?
cards.answer: Journalism means telling the truth and giving people a voice, ironic since Dante is now silenced by his circumstances.

cards.front: How does Blackman use Tyler to present single fatherhood in the novel?
cards.answer: Tyler shows single fatherhood is not extraordinary but simply what men in this family do.

title: Pre-production Documents: Mood Boards, Mind Maps & Visualisation Diagrams
subject: cambridge-nationals-creative-imedia

cards.front: Name the five things a visualisation diagram should include, as stated in the lesson.
cards.answer: Overall dimensions and orientation / Placeholder boxes for images / Positions and sizes of text elements / The planned colour scheme / Annotations explaining design choices
items: Positions and sizes of text elements

cards.front: Why are mind maps described as non-linear thinking tools?
cards.answer: Because they let a creator jump between ideas and notice unexpected connections instead of thinking in a straight line.

title: The Red Guards and the Red Terror, 1966-68
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives three reasons why young people responded so completely to Mao's call. What are they?
cards.answer: Lin Biao's PLA cult of Mao already in schools / education reform offering loyalty over exam merit / 'Bombard the Headquarters' poster naming enemies inside CCP
items: Lin Biao's PLA cult of Mao already in schools
education reform offering loyalty over exam merit
'Bombard the Headquarters' poster naming enemies inside CCP

cards.front: Why did the reform of education make peasant and worker children keen to join the Red Guards?
cards.answer: It told them academic exams favoured the bourgeoisie, so joining offered a different ladder of merit based on revolutionary loyalty.

cards.front: Why did Mao turn to Lin Biao and the PLA to demobilise the Red Guards from late 1967?
cards.answer: Red Guards had split into rival factions, seized PLA weapons and fought each other, threatening to topple the regime itself.

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why young children are at particular risk of accidents.
cards.answer: Naturally curious / Lack awareness of danger / Developing motor control / Cannot assess risk independently

cards.front: Name four ways the lesson gives to prevent falls in young children.
cards.answer: Fit stair gates top and bottom / Fit window restrictors (max 6.5cm opening) / Use non-slip mats / Keep furniture away from windows
items: Fit stair gates top and bottom

cards.front: Why should a rear-facing car seat never be placed in the front passenger seat with an active airbag?
cards.answer: Because the airbag could injure the child in a collision, so rear-facing seats must not be used there.

cards.front: Why does a spilt mug of tea still pose a scald risk 15 minutes after being made?
cards.answer: Because the liquid stays hot enough for long enough to still scald a child even after standing for 15 minutes.

title: Atomic Structure and the Development of the Atom
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the five scientists/models in order in the development of the atomic model, from Dalton to Chadwick.
cards.answer: Dalton's solid sphere model / Thomson's plum pudding model / Rutherford's nuclear model / Bohr's model with fixed shells / Chadwick's neutron

cards.front: Why did the large-angle deflections in the alpha scattering experiment disprove the plum pudding model?
cards.answer: Large deflections needed a concentrated positive charge, but plum pudding spread charge out so wouldn't deflect particles much.

cards.front: How did Bohr's model improve on Rutherford's nuclear model?
cards.answer: Bohr placed electrons in specific fixed energy levels at set distances, explaining why atoms emit light at particular wavelengths.

title: Ancient Astronomy: Eratosthenes, Aristarchus and Precession
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three things Aristarchus tried to measure or estimate about the Moon and Sun using geometry.
cards.answer: Diameter of the Moon / Distance to the Moon / Distance to the Sun and diameter of the Sun
items: Distance to the Sun and diameter of the Sun

cards.front: Why does Stonehenge's Heel Stone still align with the summer solstice sunrise today?
cards.answer: Because the alignment depends on Earth's axial tilt, which has changed very little since Stonehenge was built, not on precession.

cards.front: How did Aristarchus use a lunar eclipse to estimate the Moon's diameter?
cards.answer: He timed the Moon crossing Earth's shadow versus crossing its own diameter, giving the ratio of Earth's shadow width to the Moon's diameter.

cards.front: How did Aristarchus work out that the Sun's diameter is about 400 times the Moon's?
cards.answer: Since the Sun and Moon have almost the same angular diameter, being 400 times further away means the Sun must be 400 times larger.

cards.front: Name the three stages of Pip's Bildungsroman journey in Great Expectations.
cards.answer: Childhood at the forge (Chs 1-19) / Gentleman in London (Chs 20-39) / Disillusionment and moral recovery (Chs 40-59)

cards.front: Why did Dickens use first-person narration in Great Expectations?
cards.answer: To force the reader to share Pip's shame, ambition, and painful realisation directly.

title: Windrush, Commonwealth Migration & the Legacy of Empire
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three sectors/employers the lesson gives for Caribbean migrants who came to Britain 1948-1962.
cards.answer: National Health Service / London Transport / British Rail and textile mills

cards.front: Which four immigration-related Acts/events does the lesson give for the narrowing of Commonwealth citizenship rights (1948-1971)?
cards.answer: 1948 British Nationality Act / 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act / 1968 restriction / 1971 Immigration Act

cards.front: Why did the Home Office cause the 2018 Windrush Scandal even though the Windrush generation had lived legally in Britain for decades?
cards.answer: It had destroyed its archive of landing cards in 2010, leaving people unable to prove their legal status.

cards.front: Why did Claudia Jones organise the January 1959 indoor Caribbean Carnival?
cards.answer: It was organised in response to the August 1958 Notting Hill attacks on Caribbean residents.

cards.front: Why does eye contact often reveal a person's true feelings even when they try to hide them?
cards.answer: Because the eyes are hard to consciously control, so they leak genuine emotion despite attempts to mask it.

cards.front: Why did Yuki et al.'s findings challenge a purely innate view of reading facial emotion?
cards.answer: If reading emotion were entirely innate, culture should not change which facial feature people rely on, but it did.

cards.front: Name the two groups of evidence Darwin's theory draws on to show facial expressions are innate.
cards.answer: Neonate (newborn) evidence / Sensory-deprived (blind and deaf) evidence

title: The Sanctity of Life, Abortion and Euthanasia
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: What are the three Jewish movements the lesson describes as having different views on abortion?
cards.answer: Orthodox Judaism / Conservative Judaism / Reform Judaism

cards.front: Under the Abortion Act 1967, what two grounds allow abortion after 24 weeks in exceptional circumstances?
cards.answer: Continuing pregnancy would endanger the woman's life / Serious foetal abnormality
items: Continuing pregnancy would endanger the woman's life

cards.front: Why did the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Act 1990 set the abortion time limit at 24 weeks?
cards.answer: Because 24 weeks roughly corresponds with the point of foetal viability outside the womb.

cards.front: Why might the Dalai Lama see euthanasia as an act of compassion despite the first Precept?
cards.answer: Because karuna (compassion) means working with suffering rather than simply prolonging it in some circumstances.

cards.front: Name the four groups the lesson gives as opponents of Jenner's vaccination.
cards.answer: Inoculators / Sceptical doctors / Religious groups / Anti-vaccinators

cards.front: Name the four areas of continuity in 18th-century medicine given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Treatments (bloodletting, purging, herbs) / Training / Hospitals / Disease causes (miasma theory)

cards.front: Why did inoculators oppose Jenner's vaccination?
cards.answer: Vaccination threatened their profitable inoculation businesses and they stood to lose customers.

cards.front: Why did religious groups object to vaccination?
cards.answer: They argued it was wrong to interfere with God's will by preventing a disease He had sent.

cards.front: The lesson names four features that Gothic novels typically have. What are they?
cards.answer: Dark and isolated settings / Transgressive acts violating boundaries / Supernatural or monstrous elements / Intense psychological states

cards.front: Why does the Creature seem more 'Romantic' than Victor in the novel?
cards.answer: Denied access to human society, the Creature finds his only comfort in the natural world, unlike Victor who tries to conquer nature.

cards.front: How did the Industrial Revolution shape the anxieties explored in Frankenstein?
cards.answer: It raised fears that unchecked scientific and technological progress, pursued without ethical reflection, would lead to catastrophe.

cards.front: Why did Shelley transform the traditional Gothic 'monster' in Frankenstein?
cards.answer: She made the monster a scientifically created being rather than a supernatural demon, so horror comes from Victor's creation and abandonment, not the Creature itself.

title: The Atlantic Economy: Trade, Tobacco and Piracy
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What three things did the Navigation Acts require or protect, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Trade shipped through England first / Trade carried in English ships / Only certain valuable goods listed (tobacco, sugar, indigo, rice)
items: Only certain valuable goods listed (tobacco, sugar, indigo, rice)

cards.front: In the triangular trade described in the lesson, what did each region send: New England, the Middle colonies, and the South send to the West Indies?
cards.answer: New England sent fish, livestock and barrel staves / Middle colonies sent flour and grain / South sent rice and timber
items: New England sent fish, livestock and barrel staves
Middle colonies sent flour and grain

cards.front: Why did colonial merchants regularly smuggle French sugar and molasses despite the Navigation Acts?
cards.answer: French sugar and molasses were cheaper, and cheap smuggled molasses often meant the difference between profit and loss for distilleries.

cards.front: Why did King George I issue a Proclamation offering pardons to pirates in 1717?
cards.answer: It aimed to thin pirate numbers by encouraging surrender before a fixed date, without needing military force.

title: The Catholic Church, the Pope and Veneration of Mary
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Why does the Catholic Church see divisions among Christians as a problem?
cards.answer: Because the Church is meant to be 'one', so division wounds that unity, which Catholics pray and work to heal through ecumenical dialogue.

cards.front: How does the Catechism explain 'outside the Church there is no salvation' in a nuanced way?
cards.answer: Those who know the Church is necessary but refuse to enter cannot be saved, but those without the chance to know the Gospel may still be saved through God's mercy.

cards.front: What did the Second Vatican Council achieve, according to the lesson (name the four effects listed)?
cards.answer: Transformed Catholic worship / Strengthened the role of the laity / Launched new ecumenical dialogue / Launched new inter-faith dialogue
items: Strengthened the role of the laity

title: Modern tactics: trenches, guerrilla and beyond
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four conflicts the lesson gives where British forces faced guerrilla campaigns.
cards.answer: Boer War (1899-1902) / Mau Mau in Kenya (1952-1960) / The Troubles in Northern Ireland (1969-1998) / Falklands (1982)

cards.front: Name the three types of trench in a typical British trench system.
cards.answer: Front-line trench / Support trench / Reserve trench

cards.front: Why was crossing No Man's Land so dangerous for attacking infantry?
cards.answer: It exposed men to machine gun fire across torn ground, barbed wire and shell craters with almost no cover.

cards.front: How did British forces overcome well-defended Argentine positions in the Falklands War?
cards.answer: They used night assaults with superior training, night-vision equipment and fire support to overcome defenders in difficult terrain.

title: Diodes, Half-Wave Rectification and Zener Voltage Regulation
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: How does a zener diode keep the output voltage constant when the input voltage rises?
cards.answer: It automatically increases its conduction current so the extra voltage is absorbed by the series resistor, keeping Vout equal to Vz.

cards.front: Why does a lamp not need a flyback protection diode?
cards.answer: A lamp is a resistive load that dissipates energy immediately and produces no voltage spike when switched off.

cards.front: List the seven standard zener diode voltage values the lesson gives.

title: Heat Transfer & Why We Cook Food
subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas

cards.front: Why can boiling never brown food, while frying, roasting and grilling can?
cards.answer: The Maillard reaction needs about 140°C but water limits boiling to 100°C, so browning can't happen.

cards.front: Why does gelatinisation of starch improve palatability, e.g. in a bechamel sauce?
cards.answer: Starch swells and thickens on heating, turning a thin liquid into a smooth, coating consistency.

cards.front: Why does yeast fermentation make bread dough rise?
cards.answer: Yeast ferments sugars in the dough to produce carbon dioxide, creating gas pockets that cause the loaf to rise.

title: The Prologue, the Brawl & the Ball
subject: english-literature-edexcel

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare have the Prologue reveal the ending before the play begins?
cards.answer: So the audience focuses on how the tragedy unfolds rather than what happens, darkening every happy moment with dramatic irony.

cards.front: Why does Prince Escalus's decision to banish Romeo instead of executing him still lead to tragedy?
cards.answer: His mercy of banishment over death indirectly causes Romeo's absence, leading to the failed plan and the deaths in the tomb.

cards.front: Name the four stages of genetic engineering described in the lesson, in order.
cards.answer: Cut gene out with restriction enzymes / Cut vector with same enzyme / Insert gene as sticky ends pair up / Seal with ligase and transfer to target organism
items: Cut gene out with restriction enzymes
Insert gene as sticky ends pair up
Seal with ligase and transfer to target organism

cards.front: Name the five kingdoms used in the traditional classification system.
cards.answer: Animals / Plants / Fungi / Protists / Prokaryotes

cards.front: Why can genetic analysis give a more accurate picture of evolutionary relationships than looking at physical features?
cards.answer: Physical similarity can be caused by convergent evolution, but DNA similarity directly shows how recently species shared a common ancestor.

cards.front: Why is genetically engineered bacterial insulin considered more reliable and ethical than insulin from animal pancreases?
cards.answer: Bacteria with the inserted human insulin gene can produce large quantities of insulin without needing to extract it from pig or cow pancreases.

title: Context: Gupta, Empire and the World of the Play
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Why were lascars often given jobs like stoking boilers on ships?
cards.answer: Because of the mistaken assumption that men from hotter countries could withstand the heat better.

cards.front: Why could an ayah's arrival in Britain still be dangerous for her?
cards.answer: Because the family could dismiss her the moment they no longer needed her once on land.

cards.front: Name the two parallel love stories that structure The Empress.
cards.answer: Rani and Hari / Victoria and Abdul Karim

cards.front: Why is the serang who bullies Hari not a straightforward 'British villain'?
cards.answer: He is himself Indian, enforcing the Clan Line's contract on behalf of a system built by British shipping companies, not acting as a British officer.

cards.front: Name the four forms of deception Shakespeare presents in Much Ado, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Benign (gulling scenes, faked death) / Malicious (Don John's window plot) / Performative (the masked ball) / Self-deception (Benedick and Beatrice denying feelings)

cards.front: What three elements does the lesson say each extract-question analytical point should follow?
cards.answer: Identify a technique / Quote it from the extract / Explain its effect on the audience
items: Explain its effect on the audience

cards.front: Why is Beatrice's demand 'Kill Claudio' both inside and against the honour code?
cards.answer: It requests a duel to avenge Hero within the code, yet exposes that women need men to act for them.

cards.front: How does the play's ending relate to Beatrice's gender critique?
cards.answer: The play ends in marriage restoring patriarchal order, even though Shakespeare has spent five acts exposing its flaws.

cards.front: The lesson pairs characters into four relationships to show contrast — name all four pairings given.
cards.answer: Holmes and Watson as complementary opposites / Small and Sholto mirroring men corrupted by treasure / Mary and Holmes representing emotion versus intellect / Tonga and the Irregulars as marginalised figures used by others
items: Holmes and Watson as complementary opposites
Small and Sholto mirroring men corrupted by treasure
Mary and Holmes representing emotion versus intellect
Tonga and the Irregulars as marginalised figures used by others

cards.front: Why does Thaddeus Sholto's wrongful arrest by Jones create dramatic irony?
cards.answer: Because the most morally honest of the Sholtos, who felt guilt and sent Mary the pearls, is the one punished.

cards.front: Name the three legal changes the lesson gives that progressively restricted cruel sports.
cards.answer: Cruelty to Animals Act 1835 (banned baiting) / Marquess of Queensberry rules 1867 (reformed boxing) / Hunting Act 2004 (banned fox hunting with dogs)
items: Hunting Act 2004 (banned fox hunting with dogs)

cards.front: Why was fox hunting not banned during the Victorian reforms that ended bull-baiting?
cards.answer: Its practitioners were politically powerful and argued it was pest control as well as sport.

cards.front: How did the RSPCA's founding reflect a shift in Victorian attitudes to animal cruelty?
cards.answer: It reflected the view that animals could suffer morally, so causing unnecessary suffering was wrong even if entertaining.

cards.front: Why did the crowd take part in public executions at Tyburn rather than just watch?
cards.answer: Executions were designed as spectacles to deter crime and show royal justice, so crowds cheered, jeered and sometimes rescued the condemned.

cards.front: In the night-light circuit, why is the LDR placed as R2 (bottom resistor) instead of R1?
cards.answer: So that in darkness, rising LDR resistance increases voltage across it, making V(+) HIGH in darkness.

cards.front: How does a comparator's HIGH output turn on the npn transistor in the night-light circuit?
cards.answer: The HIGH output forward-biases the transistor's base-emitter junction through a base resistor, saturating it.

title: Music for Stage and Screen: Showstoppers and Symphonic Scores
subject: music-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three typical musical features of a musical theatre showstopper, as described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Rising vocal line / Driving accompaniment that keeps energy up / Key change before the final climax
items: Driving accompaniment that keeps energy up
Key change before the final climax

cards.front: Why does the key change just before the final phrase of Defying Gravity matter dramatically?
cards.answer: It lifts the whole texture higher, giving the singer's belted top note an extra sense of triumph.

cards.front: How does John Williams's Star Wars Main Title immediately establish the story's heroic scale?
cards.answer: It opens with a bold ascending brass fanfare in a confident major key, played in unison by the full orchestra.

title: Restoring Order: PLA, Lin Biao and the End of the Cultural Revolution, 1968-76
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four turning points that ended the Cultural Revolution, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: PLA restoration of order 1967-68 / Lin Biao affair September 1971 / Zhou Enlai's Four Modernisations 1975 / Arrest of the Gang of Four October 1976
items: Arrest of the Gang of Four October 1976

cards.front: Why did Mao send the PLA into factories, schools and government offices from late 1967?
cards.answer: Red Guard factions had splintered, looted PLA armouries and turned cities into battlegrounds, so the army was needed to restore order.

cards.front: How did the Lin Biao affair damage Mao's plans for succession?
cards.answer: Lin, Mao's named successor, died fleeing after an alleged failed coup, destroying Mao's succession plan and worsening his health.

cards.front: Why did the radicals block public mourning for Zhou Enlai in early 1976?
cards.answer: They feared mourning would turn into a political demonstration against them, but it triggered the Tiananmen Incident instead.

cards.front: Name the five principles of training the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Specificity / Progressive overload / Reversibility / Variance (tedium) / Individual needs

cards.front: Name the three overtraining injuries the lesson gives as common examples.
cards.answer: Stress fractures / Tendinopathy / Muscle strains

cards.front: Why can changing the Type variable in FITT create a different physiological adaptation?
cards.answer: Switching training method, such as from continuous running to interval training, recruits the anaerobic energy system more heavily.

cards.front: Why does rest allow fitness improvements to happen after training?
cards.answer: During exercise muscle fibres are micro-damaged, and it is during recovery that the body repairs and strengthens them, producing adaptation.

cards.front: Name the four other resistive/analogue sensing types described besides the LDR and thermistor.
cards.answer: Pressure sensor (force-sensitive resistor) / Moisture sensor (copper tracks) / Sound sensor (electret microphone + amplifier) / Potentiometer (variable resistor)

cards.front: Why does an LDR as R1 with a fixed resistor as R2 give a LOW V_out in the dark?
cards.answer: In the dark the LDR's resistance is large, so most of the supply voltage drops across R1, leaving little across R2.

cards.front: Why should you write a one-line logic check before drawing a sensing circuit that must trigger when warm?
cards.answer: It confirms whether placing the thermistor as R1 makes V_out rise with heat, preventing the common orientation mistake.

cards.front: Why is a pulse generator never placed in the sensor position of a voltage divider?
cards.answer: It is used purely as a timing input feeding a clock, not to sense a physical quantity via resistance change.

title: The Boom: Consumerism, Mass Production and Republican Policy
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three Republican policies the lesson says powered the Boom.
cards.answer: Laissez-faire (minimal government interference) / High tariffs like Fordney–McCumber / Low taxation on the rich

cards.front: Name the five industries the car boom pulled along with it, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Steel / Rubber / Glass / Leather / Paint

cards.front: How did Mellon's tax cuts and the Fordney–McCumber Tariff together set up the Wall Street boom?
cards.answer: Tariffs and tax cuts meant factories sold more and profits rose, leaving shareholders spare cash to invest in the stock market.

cards.front: Why did advertising in the 1920s change from describing products to selling feelings?
cards.answer: Advertisers used psychologists and new techniques to sell how a product would make buyers feel modern, attractive and successful.

cards.front: Name the four features that always describe a Newton's third law force pair.
cards.answer: Same type of force / Act on two different objects / Equal in magnitude / Opposite in direction

cards.front: Why does an object moving in a circle at constant speed still count as accelerating?
cards.answer: Its direction is constantly changing, so its velocity changes even though its speed stays the same.

cards.front: Why is a loaded trolley harder to push than an empty one?
cards.answer: The loaded trolley has a larger inertial mass, so a larger force is needed to produce the same acceleration.

cards.front: Why does mass stay the same everywhere while weight changes?
cards.answer: Mass is scalar and constant, but weight depends on gravitational field strength, which varies from place to place.

title: The Sun: Structure, Fusion and Atmosphere
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the Sun's four internal regions from centre outwards.
cards.answer: Core / Radiative zone / Convective zone / Photosphere

cards.front: Which layer of the Sun dominates when observing in visible light, UV, and X-rays respectively?
cards.answer: Visible light: photosphere / Ultraviolet: chromosphere / X-rays: corona

cards.front: Why does energy take around 100,000 years to travel from the Sun's core to its surface?
cards.answer: Photons are repeatedly absorbed and re-emitted by plasma particles on their way outward, slowing their journey enormously.

cards.front: Why do bright granules and dark intergranule lanes appear on the photosphere?
cards.answer: Bright granules are tops of rising hot plasma columns and dark lanes are cooler plasma sinking back down in the convective zone.

title: Life in Stalin's USSR by 1941: Workers, Women and Minorities
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four rewards top Stakhanovite performers received under Stalin's USSR.
cards.answer: Cash bonuses / Larger flats with own kitchens / Holiday vouchers to Black Sea sanatoria / Access to closed shops
items: Holiday vouchers to Black Sea sanatoria

cards.front: Name the four things the 1936 Family Code did to family life in the USSR.
cards.answer: Banned abortion / Made divorce expensive and bureaucratic / Restored awards for mothers of large families / Criminalised male non-payment of child support
items: Restored awards for mothers of large families
Criminalised male non-payment of child support

cards.front: Why did ordinary Soviet workers have to work harder after the Stakhanovite movement began?
cards.answer: Stakhanovite record performances were used to raise official production norms higher across whole industries.

cards.front: Why did the Soviet regime roll back family policy from 1936 despite promoting women's work?
cards.answer: It was both ideological, showing the regime as morally conservative before the war, and demographic, since famine, Terror and falling births had cut the population.

cards.front: Name the four main trap types described for oil and gas.
cards.answer: Anticline traps / Fault traps / Unconformity traps / Salt dome traps

cards.front: Name the three rock types that must be present together for a commercial oil deposit.
cards.answer: Source rock / Reservoir rock / Cap rock

cards.front: Why can a rock be highly porous but still impermeable, like pumice?
cards.answer: Its pores are numerous but not well-connected, so fluids cannot flow through them easily.

cards.front: Why are unconventional shale source rocks unsuitable for conventional extraction, requiring fracking instead?
cards.answer: Shale is too impermeable for hydrocarbons to flow to a well without artificially fracturing it first.

cards.front: Name the four ferrous metals listed in the specification.
cards.answer: Cast iron / Low carbon steel / High carbon steel / Stainless steel

cards.front: Name the four smart materials specified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Shape memory alloy / Thermochromic pigment / Photochromic pigment / Quantum Tunnelling Composite

cards.front: Why does stainless steel resist corrosion so well?
cards.answer: Its chromium content forms a self-healing protective oxide layer on the surface.

cards.front: How does shape memory alloy (Nitinol) behave when heated above its transition temperature?
cards.answer: It deforms when cold but returns to its pre-set shape once heated above the transition temperature.

cards.front: Name the four types of radioactive emission the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Alpha / Beta / Gamma / Neutron emission

cards.front: Name the four scientists/models involved in the historical development of the atomic model, in order.
cards.answer: Dalton - solid sphere / Thomson - plum pudding / Rutherford - nuclear model / Chadwick - neutron

cards.front: How did the results of the Rutherford-Geiger-Marsden gold foil experiment show that the atom has a nucleus?
cards.answer: Most alpha particles passed straight through but some deflected sharply and a few bounced back, showing a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.

cards.front: Why is gamma radiation the most penetrating but least ionising type of radiation?
cards.answer: Ionising power and penetrating power are inversely related, so the weakly ionising gamma rays pass through most material instead of being absorbed.

cards.front: What three tactics does Lady Macbeth use to manipulate Macbeth in Act 1 Scene 7?
cards.answer: Attacks his masculinity / Uses the infanticide image / Presents a practical plan to frame the guards
items: Presents a practical plan to frame the guards

cards.front: What three reasons does Macbeth give against killing Duncan in his Act 1 Scene 7 soliloquy?
cards.answer: Duncan is his kinsman / Duncan is his subject / Duncan is his guest/host

cards.front: Why does the witches' second prophecy make the third seem inevitable to Macbeth?
cards.answer: Because the first title is already true and the second is confirmed within minutes by Ross, so the pattern makes kingship seem certain too.

cards.front: How does the power dynamic between Macbeth and Lady Macbeth change across the play?
cards.answer: Lady Macbeth starts dominant and controls Macbeth, but by Act 3 he acts without her and by Act 5 she is destroyed by guilt, reversing their roles.

title: Western, Russian and Regional Interests in the Gulf
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three overlapping interests the lesson says drove outside involvement in the Gulf.
cards.answer: Oil supply (Hormuz, OPEC) / Cold War alignments (Soviet-Iraqi arms ties, US-Saudi defence links) / Pull of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict
items: Cold War alignments (Soviet-Iraqi arms ties, US-Saudi defence links)

cards.front: Why did Saddam Hussein want oil prices to stay high in 1989-90?
cards.answer: He needed high prices to pay off Iraq's $80 billion war debt from the Iran-Iraq war.

cards.front: Why did Saddam misjudge how outside powers would react to invading Kuwait?
cards.answer: He thought the USA was distracted by Eastern Europe and the USSR weakened by Afghanistan, underestimating that a threat to Gulf oil would unite outside powers.

title: Why Europeans sailed: motives for the voyages of discovery
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three technological advances that made long ocean voyages possible.
cards.answer: The caravel / The magnetic compass / The astrolabe

cards.front: Why did sailors use dead reckoning alongside the astrolabe in the 1490s?
cards.answer: Longitude could not be calculated accurately, so sailors combined starting point, estimated speed and compass bearing to guess position.

cards.front: How did Columbus end up reaching the Americas instead of Asia?
cards.answer: He believed the westward distance to Asia was shorter than it actually was, so he accidentally landed in the Americas.

cards.front: Why did the fall of Constantinople in 1453 push Spain and Portugal towards sea exploration?
cards.answer: It blocked reliable overland trade to Asia, giving them an economic motive to find alternative sea routes instead.

title: The Respiratory System and Gas Exchange
subject: physical-education-ocr

cards.front: Name the six features that make alveolar gas exchange efficient.
cards.answer: Large surface area / Moist thin walls (one cell thick) / Short diffusion distance / Large capillary network / Large blood supply / Maintained concentration gradient

cards.front: During intense exercise, what happens to the rib cage on the inhale to move air faster?
cards.answer: Accessory muscles, the pectorals, help elevate the rib cage further and faster than at rest.

cards.front: Why doesn't breathing harder alone increase the surface area available for gas exchange?
cards.answer: Diffusion rate is limited by fixed alveolar surface area and concentration gradients, which effort cannot change directly.

cards.front: How does exercise increase the effective surface area for gas exchange at the alveoli?
cards.answer: More capillaries open up around active alveoli during exercise, increasing the surface area available for exchange.

cards.front: Name the four layers the speaker removes in 'Honour Killing', in order.
cards.answer: The coat (nationality) / The veil (religion) / The silks and jewellery (family/dowry) / The skin, flesh and bone (the body)
items: The skin, flesh and bone (the body)

cards.front: Why does Dharker's title 'Honour Killing' mislead the reader about the poem's content?
cards.answer: It suggests violent death, but the poem is really about a woman killing off imposed identities to reclaim her own honour.

cards.front: How does the structure of 'Honour Killing' enact its argument about identity?
cards.answer: Destructive verbs like 'taking off' shift to active, creative verbs like 'making, crafting, plotting', showing loss of imposed identity leading to self-invention.

cards.front: How does enjambment in 'Honour Killing' reflect the poem's central metaphor?
cards.answer: Lines running on without pause, as in 'the face, the flesh, / the womb', mimic peeling back one layer to reveal another underneath.

cards.front: Name the five key methods Wells uses that the lesson lists for analysis.
