cards.answer: First-person narration / Scientific register / Imperial analogy / Documentary realism / Anti-climactic ending

cards.front: Why is ignoring AO3 a mistake when analysing War of the Worlds?
cards.answer: Wells wrote the novel specifically to critique imperialism, so context is essential to understanding it.

cards.front: Why does Ralph feel a 'little fall of the heart' about his own filthy appearance in Chapter 7?
cards.answer: He realises he now sees his dirty, uncivilised state as normal and no longer minds it, showing civilisation slipping away unnoticed.

cards.front: Why do Ralph and Piggy deny their involvement after Simon's murder?
cards.answer: Their guilt makes them deny responsibility, showing how the mob absorbed even good people into collective violence.

cards.front: Name the four conditions from Surah 4:69–110 used to judge whether a modern conflict is a just war.
cards.answer: Just cause / Declared by legitimate authority / Last resort / Avoid harming non-combatants

cards.front: Why do most Muslims argue that WMD are unacceptable, based on Surah 5:32?
cards.answer: WMD cause indiscriminate mass killing that cannot separate combatants from innocent civilians, conflicting with the sanctity of every innocent life.

cards.front: How do Muslims respond to the claim that religion itself causes conflict and terrorism?
cards.answer: They argue most 'religious' conflicts are really driven by politics, land or power, and terrorism distorts genuine Islamic teaching.

title: Resistors in Series and Parallel; the E24 Series
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four things represented by the multiplier exceptions and colours (gold and silver) on a resistor band, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Gold = ×0.1 multiplier / Silver = ×0.01 multiplier / Gold = ±5% tolerance / Silver = ±10% tolerance

cards.front: Why does connecting resistors in parallel always reduce the total resistance below the smallest individual resistor?
cards.answer: Parallel resistors provide additional current paths, so the total resistance falls below any single resistor's value.

cards.front: What should you do if the calculated power dissipated in a resistor exceeds its power rating?
cards.answer: Choose a higher-rated resistor with the same resistance value.

cards.front: Name the three anthology poems the lesson pairs with 'Cousin Kate' for comparison.
cards.answer: Sonnet 29 (Elizabeth Barrett Browning) / Kamikaze (Beatrice Garland) / Catrin (Gillian Clarke)

cards.front: How does the dramatic monologue form in 'Cousin Kate' shape the reader's view of the speaker?
cards.answer: Because Kate never replies, we only hear the speaker's version, making her bitterness and self-justification feel raw and immediate.

cards.front: Why is the speaker's disgrace in 'Cousin Kate' described as unfair by Rossetti?
cards.answer: The speaker and Kate did nothing very different, yet society judges them oppositely, calling Kate pure and the speaker unclean.

cards.front: Why is a nested for loop needed to traverse a 2D list?
cards.answer: The outer loop gives each row as a list, and the inner loop processes each value within that row.

cards.front: Why must the field order of a record always be documented with a comment?
cards.answer: Because fields are accessed by index, not by name, so there's no other way to know what each position represents.

cards.front: Why did the usurpation of Prospero as Duke of Milan matter so much to a Jacobean audience?
cards.answer: Because overthrowing a rightful duke was seen as a crime against the natural order, like regicide in Macbeth.

cards.front: How does Prospero maintain control over the different characters on the island?
cards.answer: He controls Ariel with a promise of freedom, Caliban with threat of punishment, and the nobles through magic.

title: Notting Hill: Black Activism and the Mangrove
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four overlapping strands of Black activism in Notting Hill between 1958 and 1971.
cards.answer: Claudia Jones's West Indian Gazette (1958) / The indoor Caribbean Carnival (1959) / The Mangrove Restaurant (from 1968) / The Black Panthers and Mangrove Nine trial (1971)
items: The Black Panthers and Mangrove Nine trial (1971)

cards.front: Why did Frank Crichlow and his customers organise the August 1970 protest march?
cards.answer: Because the Mangrove had been raided by police nine times in eighteen months with no drugs found, which was seen as targeted harassment.

cards.front: How did the defence in the Mangrove Nine trial use jury selection to challenge racism?
cards.answer: They challenged 63 potential jurors over their understanding of 'black power', leaving two Black jurors on the panel of twelve.

cards.front: Why is it a misconception to say the Notting Hill Carnival began only in 1966?
cards.answer: Because its political and cultural source was Claudia Jones's 1959 indoor Caribbean Carnival, which the 1966 street festival inherited from.

cards.front: Why do the animals confess to crimes they did not commit in Chapter 7?
cards.answer: They are terrified of Napoleon's dogs, showing terror aims at submission rather than justice.

cards.front: Why can't the animals challenge the changes made to the commandments?
cards.answer: They can barely read, showing lack of education is used as a tool of oppression.

cards.front: Why does Napoleon ban 'Beasts of England' after the executions?
cards.answer: It reminded animals of the original revolutionary vision, exposing the gap between promise and reality.

cards.front: Name the three-step pattern the lesson gives for how commandments get changed.
cards.answer: Pigs commit a forbidden act / Animals check the commandment / Commandment has been altered to permit it
items: Commandment has been altered to permit it

title: Malcolm X, Black Power and radical movements
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the two fundamental points on which Malcolm X and King differed, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Malcolm X rejected integration and wanted separate Black institutions / Malcolm X advocated self-defence while King insisted on non-violence

cards.front: Why was Martin Luther King Jr in Memphis when he was assassinated in April 1968?
cards.answer: He was supporting striking Black sanitation workers, showing he was linking civil rights with economic justice.

cards.front: How did the methods used by COINTELPRO against the Black Panthers break the law?
cards.answer: It used illegal surveillance, informants and forged letters to cause internal conflict, and cooperated with police in violent raids, which the Church Committee found unlawful.

cards.front: Why did Malcolm X break with the Nation of Islam in 1964?
cards.answer: He discovered Elijah Muhammad's personal misconduct, and his pilgrimage to Mecca broadened his view of race.

cards.front: The lesson names twelve core Olympian gods, plus Hades sometimes as a thirteenth. Name six of the twelve.
cards.answer: Zeus / Hera / Demeter / Poseidon / Hephaistos / Apollo

cards.front: The lesson gives symbols for several Olympians. Which symbol identifies each of these four gods: Athena, Apollo, Ares, Demeter?
cards.answer: Athena - owl, helmet, olive branch / Apollo - lyre and laurel wreath / Ares - spear and helmet / Demeter - sheaf of wheat

cards.front: Why was Hades not usually counted among the twelve Olympians?
cards.answer: Although brother to Zeus and Poseidon, he lived in the underworld rather than on Mount Olympus.

cards.front: Why does the lesson say it is a mistake to think the Greek gods were morally perfect?
cards.answer: Gods like Zeus and Hera behaved badly, so they were worshipped from respect and fear, not because they were good.

title: Bystander Behaviour and Piliavin's Subway Study
subject: psychology-edexcel

cards.front: Why were passengers more likely to leave the carriage the longer a Piliavin trial went on without anyone helping?
cards.answer: Without help occurring, passengers were more likely to leave rather than assist, showing reduced willingness to intervene over time.

cards.front: How can safety campaigns use knowledge of diffusion of responsibility to increase helping?
cards.answer: By telling bystanders directly that they personally should act, rather than assuming someone else will help.

cards.front: Name the two pieces of legislation used to repress the Highlands after Culloden.
cards.answer: Disarming Act (1746) / Heritable Jurisdictions Act (1747)

cards.front: Why did the Jacobite army retreat from Derby in December 1745 instead of marching on London?
cards.answer: Charles's council of war voted against continuing, fearing government forces closing in from the south and west.

cards.front: How did the Heritable Jurisdictions Act (1747) lead to the Highland Clearances?
cards.answer: It abolished chiefs' power to hold their own courts, so stripped chiefs needed new income and converted estates to sheep farming, evicting tenants.

cards.front: Why did the Seven Years War contribute to the American War of Independence within a generation?
cards.answer: The war roughly doubled Britain's public debt, forcing new taxation including taxes on the American colonies.

cards.front: Name the three purposes of the family given in Christian teaching from Ephesians 6:1-4.
cards.answer: Procreation / Security / Education

cards.front: Name three practical ways the local parish supports families, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Sunday schools and youth groups / Marriage or new-baby preparation classes / Counselling for couples / Food banks and welfare support

cards.front: Why does the Catholic Church teach that artificial contraception is not permitted within marriage?
cards.answer: Because Humanae Vitae teaches every act of sexual intercourse in marriage should remain open to new life.

cards.front: Why do Christians disagree about whether same-sex sexual relationships are acceptable?
cards.answer: Traditional teaching holds sex belongs only between a man and woman in marriage, while others judge relationships by love and commitment rather than marital status or gender.

cards.front: Name the three internal sources of finance the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Retained profit / Selling unwanted assets / Owner's savings

cards.front: The lesson gives four factors that decide which finance source suits a business. What are they?
cards.answer: How much is needed / How quickly it's needed / How long it's needed for / How established the business is

cards.front: Why might family and friends be a risky source of finance despite often being interest-free?
cards.answer: Arguments over repayment can wreck the personal relationship between the owner and the lender.

cards.front: Why is a mortgage's interest rate usually lower than a normal bank loan?
cards.answer: Because the property acts as security, so it can be repossessed if repayments are missed.

title: The Six Beliefs, the Five Roots, the Nature of Allah and Risalah
subject: religious-studies-b-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six beliefs of Sunni Islam.
cards.answer: Allah / Angels (Malaikah) / Books (Kutub) / Prophets (Risalah) / Day of Judgement (Akhirah) / Divine decree (al-Qadr)

cards.front: Name the five roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam.
cards.answer: Tawhid / 'Adl / Nubuwwah / Imamah / Mi'ad

cards.front: Why do Sevener and Twelver Shi'a Muslims both still hold Imamah despite disagreeing about the Imams?
cards.answer: They disagree only on the number and identity of the Imams, but both accept the principle that leadership passed to Muhammad's family.

cards.front: Why is Risalah so important for Muslims today?
cards.answer: It provides the direct link between Allah's will and human life, making the Qur'an and Islamic guidance possible, and gives Muslims role models for persevering through hardship.

title: Sacraments, the Mass and Catholic Prayer
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: What three parts make up the Liturgy of the Eucharist in the Mass?
cards.answer: Offertory (bread and wine brought forward) / Eucharistic Prayer (priest consecrates bread and wine) / Holy Communion (congregation receives)
items: Eucharistic Prayer (priest consecrates bread and wine)

cards.front: What two types of prayer, beyond the Lord's Prayer, does Catholic tradition practise?
cards.answer: Set (formulaic) prayer / Informal (extempore) prayer

cards.front: Why do most Protestant churches recognise only two sacraments instead of seven?
cards.answer: Because only baptism and the Lord's Supper were explicitly commanded by Jesus with a physical element.

cards.front: Why do Catholics call the Eucharist the 'source' and 'summit' of Christian life?
cards.answer: Source means all Catholic spiritual life flows from the Mass; summit means everything is directed back towards it.

title: Spain in 1490: Crusading Spirit and Foreign Ambitions
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four Portuguese exploration milestones down the African coast given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Cape Bojador in 1434 / Cape Verde in 1444 / The Equator by the 1470s / Cape of Good Hope in 1488

cards.front: Name the four spices the lesson says made up the wealthiest trade in the world.
cards.answer: Pepper / Cloves / Cinnamon / Nutmeg

cards.front: Why did the end of the Reconquista push Spain towards overseas ventures?
cards.answer: It freed thousands of soldiers and hidalgos trained only for war and conquest, with no enemy left to fight.

cards.front: How did the crusading spirit link conquest to future ventures like Columbus's voyage?
cards.answer: It held that fighting unbelievers earned salvation and lawful spoils, so gold from new lands could fund another holy war.

cards.front: Name the four impulsive decisions the lesson says Romeo makes that drive the plot.
cards.answer: Attending the Capulet ball / Marrying Juliet within hours / Killing Tybalt in rage / Drinking poison too early

cards.front: Name the three foil pairings the lesson gives to show how Shakespeare sharpens character contrast.
cards.answer: Mercutio vs Romeo / Tybalt vs Benvolio / Nurse vs Juliet

cards.front: Why does Mercutio's death act as the play's turning point?
cards.answer: It removes the play's comic energy and replaces it with tragedy, suggesting even wit cannot survive the feud.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare give Tybalt a flat, unchanging character?
cards.answer: His unchanging hatred serves a structural purpose as the catalyst that triggers the crisis and Romeo's banishment.

cards.front: Name the four main methods of collecting primary data given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Experimental / Simulation / Questionnaire / Observation

cards.front: What three limitations does the lesson give for secondary data?
cards.answer: May not measure exactly what you need / Variable definitions may have changed / Source must be acknowledged and quality assessed
items: May not measure exactly what you need
Source must be acknowledged and quality assessed

cards.front: Why can observer presence be a problem when using observation to collect primary data?
cards.answer: Because the observer's presence can influence the behaviour being watched, so it may not show what people actually do.

cards.front: Why can sensitive topics like income or health lead to biased survey results?
cards.answer: People may give socially desirable answers rather than honest ones, or refuse to answer, creating response or non-response bias.

title: 'Invisible Mass of the Back Row' — Claudette Williams
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Why is Hortense's punishment described as a particularly pointed injustice?
cards.answer: She is punished for thinking and asking a fair question, not for misbehaving, showing the classroom silences critical thought.

cards.front: Why does the ending in England matter for the theme of voice?
cards.answer: It is the moment Hortense is finally listened to, after researching Black history herself and answering with real evidence.

title: Exploration, Drake's circumnavigation and the Virginia colony
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four motives the lesson gives for Elizabethan exploration.
cards.answer: expand trade beyond northern Europe / attack Spanish shipping for gold and silver / search for a north-west passage to Asia / patriotic and religious wish to challenge Spain
items: attack Spanish shipping for gold and silver
search for a north-west passage to Asia
patriotic and religious wish to challenge Spain

cards.front: Name the five causes the lesson gives for the failure of the 1585 Roanoke settlement and its 1587 successor.
cards.answer: colonists were soldiers not farmers / killing of Wingina ended Indigenous co-operation / Roanoke Island had a poor harbour / relief fleet diverted to fight Spain / White's return delayed by the Armada
items: killing of Wingina ended Indigenous co-operation
Roanoke Island had a poor harbour
relief fleet diverted to fight Spain
White's return delayed by the Armada

cards.front: Why did English trade need to expand into new markets in the 1560s?
cards.answer: Religious wars in the Netherlands disrupted the Antwerp cloth market, so merchants sought new outlets like the Baltic, Mediterranean, Russia and West Africa.

cards.front: How did new technology make longer Elizabethan sea voyages possible?
cards.answer: Galleons with longer, lower hulls, astrolabes and quadrants for measuring latitude, accurate charts and logbooks let captains plan long ocean voyages confidently.

cards.front: Name the four measures the lesson says almost every colonial protest after 1763 was a direct consequence of.
cards.answer: Proclamation Act / Sugar Act / Stamp Act / standing army of 10,000 troops

cards.front: Why did winning the French and Indian War actually weaken Britain's position in America?
cards.answer: It removed the French threat binding colonies to Britain, added frontier costs Britain couldn't afford, and left debt London wanted colonies to pay.

cards.front: Why did Britain issue the Proclamation Act of 1763?
cards.answer: To buy time and reduce frontier defence costs after Indigenous attacks, by banning settlement west of the Appalachians.

cards.front: Why did the Lenape fight alongside the French at the Battle of the Monongahela?
cards.answer: To defend their way of life, which was threatened far more by British settlement than by a French garrison.

cards.front: Name the three non-negotiable features of a top-band 16-mark essay.
cards.answer: An argument (thesis stated upfront) / Precise evidence (names, dates, acts, statistics) / A substantiated overall judgement (weighed conclusion)

cards.front: In a 16-mark essay, what paragraphs should you include besides the introduction and conclusion?
cards.answer: At least two paragraphs arguing one side / One paragraph engaging with the counter-argument
items: At least two paragraphs arguing one side
One paragraph engaging with the counter-argument

cards.front: Why does writing three pages of description without arguing a position cap an essay in the middle band?
cards.answer: Because it fails to construct a substantiated judgement, which requires arguing a position and weighing evidence, not just describing it.

cards.front: In the worked example, why does the essay argue the Second World War was more important than the New Deal for economic change?
cards.answer: Because by 1944 unemployment fell below 2% and GDP roughly doubled, achieving genuine full employment the New Deal had not.

title: The First World War and the Fall of the Tsar
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why Russian sea routes failed to support wartime industry.
cards.answer: Baltic closed by Germany / Black Sea closed by Ottoman Turkey (late 1914) / Only Vladivostok and Murmansk-Archangel left, the latter iced over half the year
items: Black Sea closed by Ottoman Turkey (late 1914)
Only Vladivostok and Murmansk-Archangel left, the latter iced over half the year

cards.front: Name the four key events, in order, of the eight days from 23 February to 2 March 1917 (Old Style) that ended Romanov rule.
cards.answer: Women's bread strike begins in Vyborg / Volynsky Regiment mutinies and joins protesters / Petrograd garrison mutinies and Duma forms Provisional Committee / Nicholas II abdicates
items: Women's bread strike begins in Vyborg
Volynsky Regiment mutinies and joins protesters
Petrograd garrison mutinies and Duma forms Provisional Committee

cards.front: Why did Russian soldiers sometimes go to the front with only one rifle between two men?
cards.answer: Russian industry produced barely a fifth of the rifles the army needed in 1915, causing severe shortages.

cards.front: Why was Nicholas II's decision to take personal command of the army in September 1915 politically disastrous?
cards.answer: It meant every subsequent defeat was blamed personally on him, since he had taken direct responsibility for the war.

cards.front: Name the three defining traits the lesson gives for Jo's character.
cards.answer: Resilience / Directness / Vulnerability

cards.front: Why does Jo struggle to accept help, even when Geof or the Boy offer it?
cards.answer: Her emotional armour, formed as a survival mechanism from years of neglect, makes her mock or deflect care instead of accepting it.

cards.front: Why is Peter described as the play's least sympathetic character?
cards.answer: He is brash and hostile, treats Helen as a convenience rather than a person, and calls Jo ugly, showing he sees women as objects.

cards.front: Why does Geof's departure from the play feel painful despite his kindness?
cards.answer: He leaves quietly without drama after Helen's homophobic bullying destroys his bond with Jo, showing kindness isn't enough to protect him.

cards.front: Why did strict Victorian respectability lead to a culture of hypocrisy?
cards.answer: Any improper behaviour could ruin a man's reputation, so many Victorians lived respectably in public but indulged privately.

cards.front: How does Jekyll's experiment challenge Victorian religious ideas about good and evil?
cards.answer: It suggests evil lives inside every person rather than being an external force resisted through willpower and faith.

cards.front: Name the three key employer duties in relation to PPE.
cards.answer: Assess whether PPE is needed / Select the correct PPE for the task / Train and supervise employees in correct use, storage and maintenance
items: Select the correct PPE for the task
Train and supervise employees in correct use, storage and maintenance

cards.front: How is each of gas, water and electricity isolated before work starts on site?
cards.answer: Electricity: switch off at consumer unit, lock-out/tag-out / Gas: turn off at meter or isolation valve / Water: close the relevant stop valve
items: Electricity: switch off at consumer unit, lock-out/tag-out
Gas: turn off at meter or isolation valve
Water: close the relevant stop valve

cards.front: Why is scaffold inspected at least every seven days when used for work at height?
cards.answer: The lesson requires regular inspection by a competent person before and during use, with scaffold inspected at least every seven days.

cards.front: How can an un-isolated gas pipe cause danger if it is cut during work?
cards.answer: It will release gas that can build up in the area and ignite.

cards.front: Name the four wastage processes the lesson gives for cutting metals and timber.
cards.answer: Sawing / Drilling / Milling / Turning

cards.front: Name the three deforming processes the lesson gives for shaping polymers.
cards.answer: Vacuum forming / Blow moulding / Injection moulding / Extrusion

cards.front: Why do textiles use a wider tolerance (10–15 mm seam allowance) than metal engineering components (±0.01 mm)?
cards.answer: Fabric garment construction needs looser seam allowances, while engineering parts need very tight tolerances to ensure interchangeability.

cards.front: Why do timber joinery products need wider tolerances (around ±1 mm) than metal components?
cards.answer: Wood is a natural material that expands and contracts with humidity, so frames need clearance gaps for seasonal movement.

cards.front: Name the five social groups the specification identifies for studying engagement patterns.
cards.answer: Gender / Race and religion (including culture) / Age / Family and friends (peers) / People with a disability

cards.front: Name the five cross-cutting factors that affect engagement across multiple social groups.
cards.answer: Role models / Media coverage / Accessibility / Attitudes / Education

cards.front: Why do older adults often face barriers to sport participation?
cards.answer: Declining physical capacity, higher injury risk, fewer accessible facilities and reduced social networks after retirement or bereavement discourage participation.

cards.front: Why do family commitments particularly reduce adult female participation in sport?
cards.answer: Childcare and caring responsibilities fall disproportionately on women, reducing the leisure time they have available for sport.

title: Buddhist Worship: Temples, Puja, Death Rites and Festivals
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four items typically offered during Theravada puja.
cards.answer: Flowers (impermanence) / Incense (spread of good reputation) / Candles or lamps (wisdom) / Prostrations before the buddharupa

cards.front: What are the three Theravada practices that structure the monastic calendar?
cards.answer: Vassa (Rain Retreat) / Kathina (robe offering) / Uposatha days (precept-keeping)

cards.front: Why do Buddhist offerings of flowers, incense and candles not count as gift transactions?
cards.answer: They are symbolic acts that cultivate the offering of oneself to the path, not gifts exchanged with a deity.

cards.front: Why is the body often cremated in Theravada death rituals?
cards.answer: Cremation reflects the teaching that the body is impermanent (anicca).

title: Film Music: Creating Mood, Time and Place
subject: music-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson says composers typically build tension across a cue.
cards.answer: Rising pitch / Thickening texture / Increasing dynamics / Mounting dissonance

cards.front: Name the four stages of the typical climax-and-resolution shape the lesson describes in exam extracts.
cards.answer: Calm thin opening / Thickening middle section / Climax with full orchestration / Calm consonant closing passage

cards.front: Why does the Phrygian mode often suggest Spanish or Middle Eastern settings in film music?
cards.answer: Its distinctive flattened second degree sounds unfamiliar to Western listeners, evoking those regions.

cards.front: Why did Jarre use wide, sparse string writing in Lawrence of Arabia's Main Title?
cards.answer: Avoiding a busy texture leaves space for the listener to imagine an enormous, empty desert landscape.

cards.front: What four things does Odimba establish through Act 1's exposition?
cards.answer: Setting / Relationships / Tension / Tone

cards.front: Name the four functions of Princess's imagination described in Act 1.
cards.answer: Coping mechanism / Dramatic device / Thematic statement / Audience connection

cards.front: Why does Mavis initially refuse to let Wendell into the house but accept Lorna?
cards.answer: Mavis rejects Wendell over his past and absence, but accepts Lorna, letting Princess and Lorna bond over shared identity.

cards.front: Why does Junior feel torn between belonging and exclusion in Act 1?
cards.answer: As a Jamaican-British teenager he understands the racism around him but feels British society won't fully accept him, creating tension.

title: Jesus as Messiah, Son of Man and the Baptism
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three different Jewish groups and their differing Messiah expectations described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Pharisees wanted a teacher to purify the law / Zealots wanted a military revolutionary / Essenes wanted a priestly Messiah from Levi
items: Pharisees wanted a teacher to purify the law
Essenes wanted a priestly Messiah from Levi

cards.front: Give the three explanations Christian traditions offer for why a sinless Jesus was baptised.
cards.answer: Solidarity with sinful humanity / Submitting to fulfil all righteousness / A public commissioning for ministry

cards.front: Why did Isaiah 53's 'suffering servant' change how early Christians understood the Messiah?
cards.answer: It showed the Messiah could fulfil God's purposes through self-giving suffering rather than military conquest, so Christians saw Jesus in it.

cards.front: Why is the baptism narrative seen as a historical problem from a non-religious perspective?
cards.answer: John's baptism implied Jesus needed to repent of sin, which contradicts the Christian claim that Jesus was sinless.

cards.front: Name the four stages of the Athenian wedding ritual described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Dedication of toys/hair to Artemis / Bathing in sacred water / Torch-lit procession to husband's house / Anakalypteria (veil-lifting)

cards.front: Why did Athenian citizenship law make men so concerned about their wives' fidelity?
cards.answer: Because a child needed both parents to be Athenian citizens to inherit citizen rights, so only a legitimate wife could produce citizen sons.

cards.front: Why were girls a significant economic commitment for poorer Athenian fathers?
cards.answer: Because fathers had to pay a dowry to secure a daughter's marriage, and poorer families struggled to afford this.

cards.front: Why did the husband continue sleeping in communal quarters after a Spartan wedding?
cards.answer: The couple did not live together immediately; he stayed in communal quarters and visited his wife secretly for a time.

cards.front: Name the four main design tools the exam requires you to know.
cards.answer: Flow chart / Mind map / Visualisation diagram / Wireframe

cards.front: Give three advantages of using a flow chart to plan a process.
cards.answer: Clear visual representation of logic / Easy for technical and non-technical stakeholders to follow / Standard symbols understood internationally / Helps identify missing steps or infinite loops
items: Easy for technical and non-technical stakeholders to follow
Helps identify missing steps or infinite loops

cards.front: Why are wireframes often used as the first design step in a project?
cards.answer: Because they are quick to produce and cheap to revise before more detailed design work begins.

cards.front: Why might a hand-drawn flow chart become a problem when a design changes?
cards.answer: Because updating a hand-drawn chart is time-consuming compared with editing a software version.

cards.front: Why should a beginner programmer choose a block-based editor or flowchart rather than a text-based language?
cards.answer: They are more accessible because block-based editors prevent syntax errors and flowcharts make program logic immediately visible.

cards.front: In a temperature alarm flowchart, why does the arrow loop back to the sensor-reading step when the answer to the decision is 'no'?
cards.answer: So the program keeps repeating the check, continually monitoring the temperature until the condition becomes true.

cards.front: Name the four people who provide Victor with a loving, privileged upbringing in Geneva, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: His affectionate parents / Elizabeth Lavenza (childhood companion) / Henry Clerval (best friend)

cards.front: How does Professor Krempe's treatment of Victor differ from Professor Waldman's at Ingolstadt?
cards.answer: Krempe dismisses the alchemists Victor admires as charlatans and humiliates him publicly, while Waldman praises modern chemistry and inspires Victor's ambition.

cards.front: Why does Shelley describe Waldman's language about science as an act of 'penetration' and 'violation'?
cards.answer: It frames science as forcing nature to reveal her hidden secrets rather than working with her, foreshadowing Victor's destructive ambition.

title: The Five Pillars of Sunni Islam
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five key rituals of the Hajj described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Circling the Ka'bah seven times (tawaf) / Walking seven times between Safa and Marwa / Standing in prayer at Arafah / Throwing stones at three pillars in Mina / Sacrificing an animal (qurbani)
items: Walking seven times between Safa and Marwa
Throwing stones at three pillars in Mina

cards.front: Name the four things Muslims must abstain from during the Ramadan fast between dawn and sunset.
cards.answer: Food / Drink, including water / Smoking / Sexual relations

cards.front: Why does Sawm require fasting during Ramadan, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It builds self-discipline, creates empathy with the hungry, shows gratitude for Allah's provision, and increases spiritual focus.

cards.front: How does the state of ihram during Hajj show equality among Muslims?
cards.answer: Ihram removes all distinctions of wealth, nationality, and status, with everyone dressed the same way.

cards.front: Name the five lustre types the lesson describes for minerals.
cards.answer: Metallic / Vitreous or glassy / Pearly / Silky / Dull or earthy

cards.front: Name the four everyday tools used to test mineral hardness, in order of increasing hardness.
cards.answer: Fingernail / Copper coin / Steel file / A harder mineral

cards.front: Why does calcite fizz when dilute hydrochloric acid is dropped on it?
cards.answer: Calcite is calcium carbonate, and the acid decomposes it, releasing carbon dioxide gas as it reacts.

cards.front: Why does quartz appear in several different colours even though it is one mineral?
cards.answer: Tiny amounts of impurities present during crystallisation change quartz's appearance without changing what mineral it is.

cards.front: Name the three groups of reasons the lesson gives for why people stay in hazard zones.
cards.answer: People don't choose to be there / The benefits outweigh the risks / They trust they can manage the danger
items: People don't choose to be there
They trust they can manage the danger

cards.front: Name the four benefits the lesson gives that attract people to hazard zones despite the risks.
cards.answer: Fertile volcanic soil / Economic opportunities / Tourism revenue / Geothermal energy

cards.front: Why are eruptions at constructive margins gentle rather than explosive?
cards.answer: The plates slide apart smoothly and the magma is runny basalt, so lava flows steadily rather than exploding.

cards.front: Why do continental-continental collisions like India and Eurasia form mountains but no volcanoes?
cards.answer: Neither plate is dense enough to subduct, so the rock buckles upwards instead of melting in the mantle.

title: Mechanical Calculations: Gears, Pulleys and Mechanical Advantage
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Name the two main types of bearing the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Plain (journal) bearing / Ball (rolling) bearing

cards.front: Why does a bicycle use a small front chainring and large rear sprocket in low gear for going uphill?
cards.answer: This gear ratio makes pedalling easier by increasing torque at the wheel, though it reduces speed.

cards.front: How does a ball bearing reduce friction compared with a plain bearing?
cards.answer: It uses rolling contact from steel balls instead of sliding contact, which dramatically reduces friction, heat and energy loss.

cards.front: Why is a gear train with a ratio greater than 1 used for a winch or robot arm?
cards.answer: It reduces output speed but multiplies torque, giving the high torque at low speed these machines need.

cards.front: Name the three key body systems affected by the short-term effects of exercise.
cards.answer: Cardiovascular system / Cardio-respiratory system / Muscular-skeletal system

cards.front: Why does losing too much fluid through sweat make it harder for the heart to work?
cards.answer: Sweating reduces blood volume, which makes it harder for the heart to maintain cardiac output.

cards.front: How is lactic acid cleared from the body during recovery after exercise?
cards.answer: Increased breathing and blood flow deliver extra oxygen used to convert lactic acid back into glucose in the liver (Cori cycle).

cards.front: Why does blood flow shift towards working muscles and away from organs like the digestive system during exercise?
cards.answer: Vessels to working muscles vasodilate while vessels to less active organs vasoconstrict, directing blood where it's needed most.

title: Reactions to the Treaty and the Wider Settlement
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three structural weaknesses that undermined the peace settlement from the start.
cards.answer: USA walked away / Russia was excluded / Germany treated as defeated outlaw

cards.front: Name the four ethnic groups the lesson says Yugoslavia bound together.
cards.answer: Serbs / Croats / Slovenes / different religions and scripts

cards.front: Why was Japan offended at the Paris peace conference?
cards.answer: Its proposed clause on racial equality was rejected, even though it gained former German Pacific islands as mandates.

cards.front: Why did Britain, unlike France, worry the Treaty of Versailles was too harsh on Germany?
cards.answer: Lloyd George privately predicted the harsh terms would cause another war within a generation.

cards.front: Name the four abiotic factors the lesson lists that affect where organisms live.
cards.answer: Light intensity / Temperature / Moisture level / Soil pH and mineral content

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says energy is lost at each trophic level.
cards.answer: Movement / Keeping warm / Other metabolic reactions

cards.front: Why is decomposition faster in warm, moist conditions?
cards.answer: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down matter faster when conditions are warm, moist and aerobic.

cards.front: How does golden rice help combat vitamin A deficiency?
cards.answer: It has been genetically modified to produce beta-carotene, which is a source of vitamin A.

cards.front: Name the three stress management techniques used to reduce over-arousal.
cards.answer: Deep breathing / Mental rehearsal / visualisation / Positive self-talk

cards.front: Name three techniques coaches use to increase arousal in an under-aroused athlete.
cards.answer: Energetic music / Team talks raising emotional intensity / Fast-paced warm-up drills / Raising the perceived stakes

cards.front: Why does over-arousal cause a basketball player to miss free throws after dominating a physical post-up battle?
cards.answer: High arousal that helps gross, physical skills disrupts the fine motor control needed for the precise free throw technique.

cards.front: Why might an experienced elite athlete have a higher optimal arousal threshold than a beginner in the same sport?
cards.answer: They have built mental skills to channel arousal into performance, so they can tolerate higher activation before over-arousing.

cards.front: Name the four stages of the emotional arc Sissay builds in the opening scenes of Refugee Boy.
cards.answer: Warmth (father-son bond) / Unease (audience senses something wrong) / Shock (discovery of the letter) / Isolation (Alem alone in a foreign country)
items: Isolation (Alem alone in a foreign country)

cards.front: How does Sissay use physical staging to convey Alem's isolation without dialogue?
cards.answer: He uses visual storytelling, like an empty room and a letter on a pillow, to show isolation without words.

cards.front: Name the four pressures the lesson gives for why traditional UK industry declined.
cards.answer: Cheaper foreign competition / Outdated machinery lowering productivity / Resource exhaustion (coal running out) / Government policy (closures and reduced subsidies)

cards.front: Name the four sectors of the economy described in the lesson, with a UK example of each.
cards.answer: Primary - UK fishing / Secondary - JCB diggers in Staffordshire / Tertiary - London banking / Quaternary - Cambridge biotech

cards.front: Why did remaining UK coal become more expensive to mine by the 1980s?
cards.answer: Easy-to-mine coal seams had run out, so extracting the rest cost more than importing coal from abroad.

cards.front: Why did unemployment and low wages persist in former mining and steel towns even years after decline?
cards.answer: They lost their main single employer with no comparable replacement, and new service jobs were often located far away in London or the south-east.

cards.front: The lesson says the pigeon represents three things about Harri's life on the estate — what are they?
cards.answer: His innocence / His loneliness / The fragility of life on the estate
items: The fragility of life on the estate

cards.front: Why does Harri smash-fail the fire alarm during his gang initiation test?
cards.answer: The glass will not break, so he runs away, showing his moral compass resists gang pressure.

cards.front: Why does Kelman treat the desensitisation of estate residents as itself a form of violence?
cards.answer: When people can walk past bloodstains without flinching, something essential in their humanity has been destroyed.

cards.front: Why does Kelman refuse to present Harri's death as inevitable or deserved?
cards.answer: It is the direct result of a system that failed to protect him, not a natural consequence of his innocence.

cards.front: Name the four key quotations the lesson gives for the theme of ambition.
cards.answer: vaulting ambition, which o'erleaps itself / Unsex me here / fruitless crown and barren sceptre / signifying nothing

cards.front: How does Macbeth's guilt after Duncan's murder affect him, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It is visceral and overwhelming, shown by the dagger hallucination and unwashable blood, but it doesn't stop him killing again.

cards.front: How much of an extract-based Shakespeare answer should focus on the printed passage itself?
cards.answer: Roughly half, spent on close language analysis, with the other half linking to the wider play.

cards.front: Why is Duncan's excessive trust presented as his flaw in the play?
cards.answer: Because he trusts Macbeth's outward appearance, failing to see the deceptive reality, which leads to his murder.

title: Engineering Drawing — Orthographic, Isometric & Sectional Views
subject: engineering-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five BS 8888 line types used in engineering drawings.
cards.answer: Continuous thick line / Continuous thin line / Thin dashed line / Thin chain line / Thick chain line

cards.front: Why must engineering drawings always show a projection symbol in the title block?
cards.answer: Because BS 8888 permits both first-angle and third-angle projection, so the symbol shows which layout is used to avoid misreading dimensions.

cards.front: Why do circles appear as ellipses in isometric projection?
cards.answer: Because lengths are only drawn true to scale along the three axes, so curved features must be constructed indirectly by plotting points.

cards.front: Why is a sectional view used instead of just dashed lines to show an internal bore?
cards.answer: Because internal features like bores are hard to describe with dashed lines alone, so cutting through the object shows them more clearly.

title: Searching Algorithms: Linear and Binary Search
subject: computer-science-aqa

cards.front: Name the three conditions the lesson gives for when to use binary search.
cards.answer: Dataset is large / Data is already sorted or sorted once and searched many times / Fast repeated look-ups are a priority
items: Data is already sorted or sorted once and searched many times
Fast repeated look-ups are a priority

cards.front: Why did linear search need 6 comparisons to find 23 in the 9-item sorted list, while binary search only needed 3?
cards.answer: Linear search checks items one by one from the start, but binary search halves the search area each comparison, reaching the target much faster.

cards.front: What three functions does code-switching serve in Leave Taking?
cards.answer: Characterisation / Thematic (patois vs standard English tension) / Dramatic (exposes Enid's contradiction)

cards.front: Why does the audience hear irony when Enid argues for English respectability?
cards.answer: Because she makes the argument in Jamaican patois, so the audience hears the contradiction she is living.

cards.front: Name the four ways De Waal presents Leon's bond with Jake in Part 1.
cards.answer: Physical closeness / Responsibility / Promises / Leon's identity

cards.front: Give three signs of Carol's deterioration described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Stops cooking / Sleeps for days / Brings home frightening men / Disappears leaving children alone

cards.front: How does De Waal use tactile language to show love between Leon and Jake?
cards.answer: She uses words like 'warm,' 'soft,' and 'tucked in' to show love expressed through touch rather than words.

cards.front: Why does the bureaucratic language of social services create a power imbalance for Leon?
cards.answer: Words like 'placement' and 'permanency' describe devastating changes he doesn't understand, leaving him no voice in decisions about his life.

title: Nuclear Radiation: Uses, Fission and Fusion
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the three categories of nuclear waste described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Low-level waste / Intermediate-level waste / High-level waste

cards.front: Name the four safety precautions the lesson gives for handling radioactive materials.
cards.answer: Keep exposure time short / Maximise distance from source / Use shielding / Monitor exposure with dosimeters

cards.front: Why does gamma radiotherapy aim beams at a tumour from multiple angles?
cards.answer: To concentrate the radiation dose on the cancer while minimising damage to healthy tissue.

cards.front: How does a thickness monitor detect if a material becomes too thick during manufacturing?
cards.answer: If the material gets too thick, less radiation passes through to the detector, triggering an adjustment.

cards.front: Why does Jane refuse to become Rochester's mistress despite loving him?
cards.answer: She chooses principle over feeling, believing laws and principles exist precisely for moments of temptation like this.

cards.front: Why does Brontë make Jane leave Thornfield with no money or help from Rochester?
cards.answer: Her independence would be worthless if funded by the man she refuses, so moral agency must be material as well as spiritual.

title: The Oneness of Humanity and Equality
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the three composers included in the Guru Granth Sahib whose castes/backgrounds show its teaching of equality.
cards.answer: Kabir, a low-caste weaver / Sheikh Farid, a Muslim mystic / Ravidas, a leatherworker of very low caste
items: Ravidas, a leatherworker of very low caste

cards.front: How did Guru Gobind Singh's founding of the Khalsa in 1699 abolish caste hierarchy?
cards.answer: He chose the Panj Pyare from different castes and initiated them as equals, then gave all Sikhs shared names instead of caste surnames.

title: Types of Retail Business and Activity
subject: l12-retail-business

cards.front: Name the eight main types of retailer given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Supermarket / Hypermarket / Department store / Convenience store / Specialist/independent / Discount/variety store / E-tailer / Market trader

cards.front: Why do discount and variety stores like Primark and Poundland rely on high footfall?
cards.answer: Their business model relies on selling high volumes of products at low prices with tight cost control.

cards.front: Why does e-commerce tend to lead to higher return rates for retailers?
cards.answer: Customers cannot physically inspect or try products before buying, so more items get sent back.

cards.front: Why can a global retailer like Amazon or IKEA achieve huge purchasing economies compared to a local independent shop?
cards.answer: Its large scale gives it much greater buying power than a local independent, though it must manage different markets and regulations.

title: Depression and Addiction: Symptoms and Impact
subject: psychology-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four ICD symptoms of depression besides low mood and loss of interest.
cards.answer: Low energy and fatigue / Poor concentration / Disturbed sleep or appetite / Feelings of worthlessness or guilt

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why reported incidence of depression and addiction has risen.
cards.answer: Increased challenges of modern living / Increased recognition of symptoms / Lessening of social stigma

cards.front: Why does the ICD require several symptoms to occur together rather than just one?
cards.answer: This separates ordinary sadness, which everyone experiences, from clinical depression that affects a person's ability to function.

cards.front: Why can reduced face-to-face contact and constant connectivity increase risk of depression and addiction?
cards.answer: They can increase loneliness, which is a known risk factor for both depression and addictive behaviour.

title: Lollards, Luther and English criticism of the church
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Why did Henry VIII write the Assertio Septem Sacramentorum in 1521?
cards.answer: To attack Luther's ideas, which earned him the title 'Defender of the Faith'.

cards.front: Why did the Church's attempts to burn Tyndale's Bibles fail to stop them spreading?
cards.answer: Demand outstripped supply, so burning one edition simply created demand for the next.

cards.front: Why did word choices in Tyndale's translation matter to the Church?
cards.answer: He used words like 'congregation' instead of 'church', carrying Protestant theological meaning that challenged Catholic teaching.

cards.front: Why did the Richard Hunne case in 1514 increase anti-clerical feeling in London?
cards.answer: Londoners believed the Church had murdered Hunne while he awaited trial for heresy in the Bishop's prison.

cards.front: Name the five characters and the idea each one embodies in Lord of the Flies.
cards.answer: Ralph = democracy / Jack = dictatorship / Piggy = reason / Simon = spiritual truth / Roger = sadism

cards.front: Why is Ralph ultimately unable to stop civilisation collapsing on the island?
cards.answer: He lacks ruthlessness to enforce his rules, so he can only appeal and argue rather than compel obedience.

cards.front: Why does Jack succeed in gaining followers when Ralph struggles to keep them?
cards.answer: Jack offers immediate rewards like meat, excitement and protection from the beast, understanding people follow strength, not rules.

cards.front: How does the decline of the signal fire reflect the boys' journey in the novel?
cards.answer: Its decline mirrors their descent into savagery, and its abandonment marks the present's triumph over hope of rescue.

title: Challenges to the settlement: Puritans and Catholics
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What three features of the Church did Puritans want removed, according to the lesson's Key Fact?
cards.answer: Vestments / Ornaments / Bishops

cards.front: Why did Elizabeth's government toughen its treatment of Catholics after 1570?
cards.answer: The Pope's 1570 bull, the 1571 Ridolfi plot, and fear that Catholic loyalty meant disloyalty to England pushed the shift.

cards.front: Why were the Earls of Northumberland and Westmorland already alienated from Elizabeth's government before 1570?
cards.answer: They lost influence at court to reformers like Cecil, and their remote northern lands with Catholic tenants were hard to control.

title: Lenin, Trotsky and the October Revolution
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three Bolshevik strengths the lesson gives for why they won in 1917.
cards.answer: A clear popular slogan no rival could match / A tightly disciplined party that could act fast / Trotsky's organisational skill with the Military Revolutionary Committee
items: A clear popular slogan no rival could match
A tightly disciplined party that could act fast
Trotsky's organisational skill with the Military Revolutionary Committee

cards.front: Name the three groups the Bolsheviks used to seize key buildings on the night of 24-25 October.
cards.answer: Kronstadt sailors / Bolshevik Red Guards from the factories / Pro-Bolshevik units of the Petrograd garrison
items: Bolshevik Red Guards from the factories
Pro-Bolshevik units of the Petrograd garrison

cards.front: Why did the slogan 'Peace, Land, Bread' work so well for the Bolsheviks in 1917?
cards.answer: Peace appealed to war-weary soldiers and cities, Land to peasants wanting noble estates broken up, Bread to workers facing inflation, and no other party offered all three.

cards.front: Why was the Bolshevik party so effective in 1917 despite its small size in April?
cards.answer: Discipline meant central committee decisions bound every cell, Pravda repeated consistent slogans, and agitators gave trained answers, so they acted while rivals debated.

cards.front: Why is the handwriting on Hyde's forged letter actually the same as Jekyll's?
cards.answer: Because Jekyll wrote it himself as Hyde, so the writer of both is literally the same person.

cards.front: Why does Stevenson set Jekyll's cabinet above the dissecting theatre inside a layered house?
cards.answer: The layered house mirrors a mind with a respectable surface, a working intellect, and a hidden appetite locked away.

cards.front: Why do Utterson and Enfield leave the window scene in silence?
cards.answer: Stevenson uses their silence to show there is nothing respectable Victorian gentlemen can say about what they saw.

cards.front: How do Chapters 5-8 change Stevenson's technique compared to earlier chapters?
cards.answer: He switches from planting clues to accumulating them until the reader can no longer resist the conclusion.

title: Short and Long Term Effects of Exercise
subject: physical-education-ocr

cards.front: Why does lactic acid production increase during high-intensity exercise?
cards.answer: Because exercise intensity rises beyond the aerobic threshold, so the body supplements aerobic energy with anaerobic pathways.

cards.front: How does capillarisation improve resistance to fatigue?
cards.answer: New capillaries increase oxygen delivery and speed up waste removal, letting muscles delay lactic acid accumulation and sustain effort longer.

title: The Cabal, Party Politics and Rule Without Parliament
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the five members of the Cabal ministry (1668–1674) whose initials gave it its nickname.
cards.answer: Clifford / Arlington / Buckingham / Ashley / Lauderdale

cards.front: Name the two reasons Charles II could afford to rule without Parliament from 1681.
cards.answer: Booming customs and excise revenue / French subsidy of around £385,000 from Louis XIV
items: French subsidy of around £385,000 from Louis XIV

cards.front: Why did the discovery of the Rye House Plot in 1683 help Charles II tighten his grip on local government?
cards.answer: It let him press legal challenges to borough charters much harder and purge Whig sympathisers from the corporations.

cards.front: Why did Charles II deliberately keep the five Cabal ministers divided rather than letting them act as a unified team?
cards.answer: So that no single one of them could dominate government or gain too much power over him.

cards.front: What four things does Richard report about the group's fragmentation to Phil in Act 4 of DNA?
cards.answer: John Tate joined the Jesus Army / Brian is heavily medicated and may be sectioned / Danny hates his dentist work experience / Cathy is running things and cut off a finger
items: John Tate joined the Jesus Army
Brian is heavily medicated and may be sectioned
Danny hates his dentist work experience
Cathy is running things and cut off a finger

cards.front: Why does Phil's plan in Act 3 mark a moral escalation from his plan in Act 1?
cards.answer: In Act 1 his plan was deception that harmed no one physically, but in Act 3 he implies ordering Adam's murder, a far darker step.

cards.front: Why is it ironic that Cathy is the one 'running things' by Act 4 of DNA?
cards.answer: The character who showed the least remorse and enjoyed the violence most is the one who thrives, while others are damaged.

cards.front: Name the four key Space Race achievements given in the lesson, in order.
cards.answer: Sputnik satellite launched (1957) / Yuri Gagarin first human in space (1961) / NASA receives massive US investment / USA lands on the Moon (1969)
items: Yuri Gagarin first human in space (1961)

cards.front: Why did the USSR crush the Hungarian uprising in 1956?
cards.answer: Hungary tried to leave the Warsaw Pact, so Soviet tanks intervened to maintain control over its satellite states.

cards.front: Why did MAD (Mutually Assured Destruction) make direct war between the superpowers less likely?
cards.answer: Both sides had nuclear arsenals capable of devastating retaliation, so any first strike would trigger destruction for the attacker too.

cards.front: Why did the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan (1979) put such strain on the USSR?
cards.answer: The nine-year war killed around 15,000 Soviet soldiers and vast numbers of Afghans, worsening existing Soviet economic strain.

title: Elizabeth I: background, character and the royal court
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four languages Elizabeth I read and wrote fluently, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Latin / Greek / French / Italian

cards.front: Which four royal palaces does the lesson name that the court moved between?
cards.answer: Whitehall / Greenwich / Hampton Court / Richmond

cards.front: Why did Elizabeth rely on image-making, such as her portraits, to rule?
cards.answer: She could not rely on a husband or a strong army to enforce her authority, so used image as a political tool.

cards.front: How did the patronage system stop ambitious nobles from uniting against Elizabeth?
cards.answer: Because she controlled rewards, ambitious men competed for her favour rather than challenging her authority, as long as rewards kept flowing.

cards.front: Name the four main ways the lesson says Christians worship.
cards.answer: Liturgical / Non-liturgical / Informal / Private

cards.front: The Lord's Prayer covers four things according to the lesson's Key Fact — what are they?
cards.answer: Praise of God / Submission to God's will / Requests for daily needs / Forgiveness

cards.front: Why do supporters value liturgical worship's use of a set lectionary?
cards.answer: Because readings follow a set pattern so all congregations worldwide hear the same Bible passages on the same day.

cards.front: Why does Quaker worship involve sitting in silence with no leader?
cards.answer: So there is no fixed structure, allowing God to communicate directly with individuals when they feel moved by the Holy Spirit.

title: Themes: continuity and change in twentieth-century Germany
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six turning points in German history from 1919 to 1991 that the lesson identifies as strongest candidates.
cards.answer: 1919 Treaty of Versailles/Weimar Constitution / January 1933 Hitler's appointment / 1945 total defeat and division / 1949 creation of two German states / 1963 Élysée Treaty / 1989–1990 fall of Wall and reunification

cards.front: Name the five distinct economic conditions Germany experienced between 1919 and 1991.
cards.answer: Weimar inflation, recovery, then Depression / Nazi rearmament recovery then war devastation / post-1945 total economic collapse / Wirtschaftswunder in the West vs planned economy in the East / 1990 merger of dynamic and declining economies
items: Nazi rearmament recovery then war devastation
Wirtschaftswunder in the West vs planned economy in the East
1990 merger of dynamic and declining economies

cards.front: Why was West Germany's democracy after 1949 able to survive economic downturns that would have destroyed Weimar's?
cards.answer: The Basic Law's structural safeguards embedded democracy so deeply it survived crises like the 1970s oil shock that Weimar could not withstand.

cards.front: Why is a change like 1945 or 1990 considered more significant than a single-track change in German history?
cards.answer: It transformed both Germany's internal situation and its external position simultaneously, making it harder to dismiss as less important.

title: The Rise of Trade Unions: Tolpuddle to New Unionism, 1834-1889
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What three phases did trade unionism develop through, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Tolpuddle (1834) showed state hostility / New Model Unions (1850s onwards) won legality and respectability / New unionism (1888-89) brought in unskilled workers
items: New Model Unions (1850s onwards) won legality and respectability
New unionism (1888-89) brought in unskilled workers

cards.front: The lesson gives four factors that come together in the story of trade unionism. What are they?
cards.answer: The economy / The role of the individual / Government / Communication

cards.front: Why did the Tolpuddle case backfire on the authorities?
cards.answer: The harsh transportation sentence provoked a national petition of 800,000 signatures and huge demonstrations, forcing the government to pardon the men.

cards.front: Why did New Model Unions win legal recognition and respectability by the 1870s?
cards.answer: Their high subscriptions, benefits and cooperation with employers made them respectable, winning the Trade Union Act 1871 and the 1875 Conspiracy Act.

cards.front: Why does the cyclical structure of 'When We Two Parted' make the speaker's grief feel unresolved?
cards.answer: The opening and closing 'silence and tears' show the pain has not diminished, trapping the speaker in the memory of loss.

cards.front: Why is the speaker in 'When We Two Parted' unable to publicly grieve?
cards.answer: Because the affair was secret, so the forced silence intensifies the emotional damage.

cards.front: How do the half-rhymes in 'When We Two Parted' reflect the speaker's grief?
cards.answer: Half-rhymes like 'morning'/'warning' create a sense of incompleteness, reflecting the unfinished nature of the grief.

cards.front: Why does Dooley describe souls 'tapping out messages' in 'Letters from Yorkshire'?
cards.answer: It gives their spiritual bond a physical action, like a signal sent along a wire, showing connection can survive distance without technology.

cards.front: What are the three sections of 'Odour of Chrysanthemums'?
cards.answer: Waiting for Walter / Arrival of the body / Washing of the body

cards.front: How does Lawrence use prose register to build up to the story's ending?
cards.answer: The cool, flat register of the waiting sections contrasts with the lyrical, interior prose of the final scene, making its emotion more powerful.

cards.front: How does Walter escape the pressures of the pit and home life?
cards.answer: Walter escapes through drink, while Elizabeth manages the house with an efficiency that displaces her feelings.

cards.front: Why does Lawrence use the chrysanthemum motif across the story?
cards.answer: It links love, birth and death, suggesting death was always present in the marriage and touched even its happy moments.

cards.front: Name the five workshop safety essentials the lesson gives for using machinery safely.
cards.answer: Wear appropriate PPE / Secure workpieces with clamps or vices / Never leave machines running unattended / Keep guards in place / No loose clothing, jewellery or untied hair
items: Secure workpieces with clamps or vices
No loose clothing, jewellery or untied hair

cards.front: Name the four hand tool categories the lesson groups by function, with one example each.
cards.answer: Marking and measuring - steel rule / Cutting - tenon saw / Shaping - chisels / Joining - clamps

cards.front: Why must work never be held by hand when using a pillar drill?
cards.answer: It must be secured with a machine vice or clamp because the drill needs precise vertical holes made safely, not held by hand.

cards.front: Why is laser cutting chosen for cutting or engraving sheet materials like acrylic or MDF?
cards.answer: Because a focused laser beam gives extremely high precision and clean edges with minimal kerf.

title: 11 September 2001: The Attacks That Changed the World
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four countries the nineteen 9/11 hijackers came from.
cards.answer: Saudi Arabia / United Arab Emirates / Egypt / Lebanon

cards.front: Give the four locations struck or crashed into during the 9/11 attacks.
cards.answer: North Tower, World Trade Center / South Tower, World Trade Center / The Pentagon / A field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania

cards.front: Why did 9/11 become the most intimately documented atrocity of its time, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Mobile phones, then widespread, let trapped victims call relatives, and those voicemails were recovered and reconstructed by the 9/11 Commission.

cards.front: Why is it a misconception to call 9/11 simply a 'Middle Eastern attack on America'?
cards.answer: The hijackers trained in Afghanistan, met in Malaysia, planned in Hamburg, learned to fly in Florida/Arizona and struck New York, Virginia and Pennsylvania, showing a transnational geography.

cards.front: Name the four towns where Huguenot refugees mainly settled in England.
cards.answer: London / Canterbury / Southampton / Norwich

cards.front: Name three fields the lesson credits Huguenot refugees with contributing skills to.
cards.answer: Silk-weaving / Silversmithing / Medicine

cards.front: Why did the arrival of the Palatines in 1709 provoke hostility despite them being fellow Protestants?
cards.answer: The sheer scale of arrivals strained charitable resources, and they had fewer skills and greater economic needs than Huguenots.

cards.front: Why were Huguenot silk-weavers sometimes resented by native English weavers in Spitalfields?
cards.answer: Native weavers resented the economic competition from Huguenots, leading to periodic riots.

cards.front: Name the three narrative functions the lesson gives for Spider the dog.
cards.answer: Provides emotional companionship / Confirms the haunting is real / Creates vulnerability Arthur must protect

cards.front: How does Hill's changing prose style track Arthur's deterioration across the novel?
cards.answer: Prose moves from measured, controlled early chapters to fragmented, breathless writing at Eel Marsh House, ending quiet and broken.

cards.front: Why does Sam Daily break Crythin Gifford's code of silence to warn Arthur?
cards.answer: Because unlike the other townspeople, Sam values practical caution and cannot let Arthur walk into danger unwarned.

cards.front: Why does Mr Jerome fail to protect Arthur despite knowing about the curse?
cards.answer: He is overwhelmed by fear rather than malicious, and his silence makes him complicit through moral cowardice.

cards.front: Name the five conservation strategies the lesson describes for protecting biodiversity.
cards.answer: Protected areas / Captive breeding programmes / Seed banks / Fishing quotas and logging regulations / Reforestation projects

cards.front: Name the four lines of evidence the lesson gives for evolution.
cards.answer: Fossil record / Comparative anatomy / DNA analysis / Peppered moth example

cards.front: Why did the dark (melanic) form of the peppered moth become more common during industrial pollution?
cards.answer: Soot darkened tree bark, making pale moths more visible to predators, so dark moths were better camouflaged and survived better.

cards.front: How does speciation lead to two populations becoming separate species?
cards.answer: Isolated populations face different environmental pressures and accumulate different mutations until they diverge too much to interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

title: Form and Methods: Thirty Scenes, Songs and Languages
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: What years does Act Two of The Empress jump between, in order?
Why does Act One repeatedly cut between Tilbury docks and Windsor Castle?
cards.answer: It invites the audience to compare Rani being dismissed with Abdul being welcomed into service on the same afternoon of empire.

cards.front: Why is every foreign phrase in the play's text printed with its English translation?
cards.answer: So a design or performance choice never needs to guess at translation, as the play already tells you what is being said and to whom.

cards.front: What three functions do the supporting characters Margot and Leon serve in the play?
cards.answer: Show diversity of response / Provide comic relief / Demonstrate solidarity

cards.front: Why did Wendell turn to crime?
cards.answer: Racist discrimination denied him the good job he was promised after serving in the English army, so crime was a response to systemic exclusion.

cards.front: How does Lorna's identity differ from Princess's?
cards.answer: Lorna, being mixed-race, feels she belongs nowhere fully, unlike Princess whose experience is specifically as a Black girl in 1960s Bristol.

cards.front: Why does Margot's help for Princess in Act 3 show solidarity is personal rather than political?
cards.answer: Margot shelters Princess after she runs away yet still dismisses the boycott campaign, so her care crosses race lines without changing her views.

title: Johnson's War: Tonkin and Rolling Thunder
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why Operation Rolling Thunder failed to break Hanoi.
cards.answer: Bombing of Hanoi and Haiphong was restricted / Aid from China and USSR replaced losses / North dispersed industry and dug shelters / Ho Chi Minh Trail could not be cut
items: Bombing of Hanoi and Haiphong was restricted
Aid from China and USSR replaced losses
North dispersed industry and dug shelters
Ho Chi Minh Trail could not be cut

cards.front: Name the four Vietcong guerrilla tactics the lesson gives that neutralised US technological superiority.
cards.answer: Moving at night / Mining trails / Setting bamboo punji-stick traps / Digging tunnel networks like Cu Chi
items: Digging tunnel networks like Cu Chi

cards.front: Why did Johnson pursue 'graduated escalation' rather than full-scale war or withdrawal in Vietnam?
cards.answer: He feared withdrawal would discredit US commitments worldwide but full-scale war would discredit him at home, so he used just enough force to try to win without provoking China.

cards.front: How did North Vietnam's workforce help the country survive the bombing of Rolling Thunder?
cards.answer: An estimated 500,000 workers, mainly women, repaired roads and bridges almost overnight, keeping supply routes open despite the bombing.

cards.front: Name the three stages of Macbeth's escalating violence given in the lesson, in order.
cards.answer: Duncan's murder (reluctant, political) / Banquo's murder (paranoid, independent) / Macduff's family (vindictive tyranny)

cards.front: Why does the king's healing touch of Edward the Confessor contrast with Macbeth's rule?
cards.answer: It symbolises legitimate, God-given kingship, unlike Macbeth's rule which has made Scotland itself sick.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare show Lady Macduff and her son in a tender domestic scene before the murderers arrive?
cards.answer: To make the massacre emotionally devastating and highlight the horror of murdering innocent children.

cards.front: Name the six stages of the geographical enquiry process in order.
cards.answer: Pose questions / Collect evidence / Process and present / Analyse patterns / Draw conclusions / Evaluate

cards.front: Why is choosing a fair sample site location important in a river study of channel shape down a tributary?
cards.answer: Sites at intervals down a single tributary fairly test how channel shape changes with distance, while mixing rivers would mix variables and weaken conclusions.

title: Classical Sociologists: Durkheim, Marx and Weber
subject: sociology-aqa

cards.front: According to the reliable pairing list, what four concepts are associated with Durkheim?
cards.answer: Social facts / Solidarity (mechanical/organic) / Anomie / Scientific method

cards.front: According to the reliable pairing list, what four concepts are associated with Marx?
cards.answer: Class conflict / Bourgeoisie/proletariat / False consciousness / Capitalism/means of production

cards.front: How did Marx argue the bourgeoisie exploit the proletariat?
cards.answer: By paying workers less than the full value of what they produce and keeping the difference as profit.

cards.front: Why did Durkheim warn that rapid social change increases crime and suicide?
cards.answer: Because it can produce anomie, a state of normlessness where the usual rules no longer hold.

cards.front: Name the four rival Anglo-Saxon kingdoms in Britain before the Viking raids began.
cards.answer: Northumbria / Mercia / East Anglia / Wessex

cards.front: What three reforms did Alfred make to Wessex's defences after Edington?
cards.answer: Built a network of fortified burhs / Redesigned the army so half fought half farmed / Ordered construction of larger ships
items: Built a network of fortified burhs
Redesigned the army so half fought half farmed

cards.front: Why did undefended monasteries look like an 'open vault' to Norse raiders?
cards.answer: Norse warriors did not share Christian taboos against attacking churches, so portable monastic wealth seemed easy plunder rather than sacred ground.

cards.front: How did religion end up uniting Anglo-Saxons and Danes rather than dividing them?
cards.answer: After Guthrum's baptism Norse settlers converted to Christianity, endowing churches and being buried in Christian cemeteries, making religion a shared glue.

cards.front: Name the four groups the lesson gives as readers of financial statements, and what each checks them for.
cards.answer: Investors, before buying shares / Banks, before lending / Managers, to decide next year's strategy / Employees, to judge if jobs are safe
items: Managers, to decide next year's strategy
Employees, to judge if jobs are safe

cards.front: Name the four items the income statement structure runs through from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Revenue / Cost of sales / Gross profit / Other operating costs / Net profit

cards.front: Why does a falling gross profit margin over time suggest a problem?
cards.answer: It suggests rising supplier costs or price cuts that haven't been passed on to customers.

cards.front: Why can a business with a high gross profit margin still end up with a very low net profit margin, as with Burberry?
cards.answer: A high gross margin does not guarantee a high net margin because overheads can still eat most of the profit made on products.

cards.front: What three dimensions does exercise improve at the same time, according to the Key Fact?
cards.answer: Physical (heart, body systems, disease prevention) / Mental (stress reduction, hormones, emotional control) / Social (friendships, teamwork, community)

cards.front: Why does chronically elevated stress hormone levels harm the body?
cards.answer: Long-term high cortisol and adrenaline damage the cardiovascular system, suppress immunity and impair sleep.

cards.front: Why might low-intensity activities like yoga or walking groups produce greater wellbeing gains for some people than competitive sport?
cards.answer: They are more accessible, enjoyable and sustainable, so people keep doing them regularly, which is what matters.

cards.front: Name the four strategies the lesson gives for combating a sedentary lifestyle.
cards.answer: Increasing active transport / Taking regular breaks to move / Joining a local sports club / Using activity-tracking technology

cards.front: Why does hypertension increase the risk of stroke and kidney disease?
cards.answer: Hypertension damages arterial walls over time, increasing the risk of stroke, kidney disease and cardiovascular damage.

cards.front: Name the four physical factors the lesson gives that increase flood risk.
cards.answer: Precipitation / Geology / Relief / Saturation

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says urbanisation increases flood risk.
cards.answer: Impermeable surfaces stop infiltration / Storm drains speed water to river / New housing on flood plains
items: Storm drains speed water to river

cards.front: Why does ground saturation increase flood risk, especially in November and December?
cards.answer: Ground already wet from previous rain cannot absorb more, so new rainfall runs straight off into the river.

cards.front: Why do farming practices increase how fast water reaches a river?
cards.answer: Heavy machinery compacts soil, autumn ploughing leaves bare fields exposed, and livestock paths channel runoff downslope.

title: Modern punishment: rehabilitation, abolition and alternatives
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: What three activities did community service require offenders to do, as given in the lesson?
cards.answer: Painting community halls / Maintaining parks / Working in charity shops

cards.front: Why did open prisons face criticism despite supporters' evidence in their favour?
cards.answer: Critics argued they were 'soft on crime', while supporters pointed to evidence they reduced reoffending compared to closed prisons.

cards.front: Why did short custodial sentences fall out of favour, leading to community service as an alternative?
cards.answer: They were expensive, disruptive to employment and housing, and widely seen as ineffective at reducing reoffending.

cards.front: How did borstals aim to reform young offenders differently from adult prisons?
cards.answer: Through a structured regime of education, vocational training, physical activity and discipline instead of punitive adult prison conditions.

cards.front: Name the five strategies the lesson gives for preventing human communicable diseases.
cards.answer: Vaccination / Hygiene and sanitation / Sterilisation of wounds / Contraception for STIs / Travel/movement restrictions

cards.front: Name the three traditional lab methods the lesson gives for identifying pathogens (before monoclonal antibodies).
cards.answer: Culturing samples on nutrient agar / Observing colonies under a microscope / Testing sensitivity to antimicrobials

cards.front: Why does the primary immune response allow symptoms to develop while the secondary response usually doesn't?
cards.answer: The primary response takes days to find the antigen and make antibodies, letting the pathogen replicate, whereas memory cells respond almost immediately.

cards.front: Why can herd immunity break down even if most people believe it protects them?
cards.answer: If enough individuals rely on others being vaccinated and skip vaccination themselves, immunity falls below the threshold needed, allowing outbreaks.

title: The Permanent Indian Frontier and the First Fort Laramie Treaty
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three pressures the lesson gives for why the Permanent Indian Frontier failed by 1851.
cards.answer: Migration along the Oregon Trail from 1836 / Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) adding new territories / The 1849 California Gold Rush
items: Migration along the Oregon Trail from 1836
Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) adding new territories

cards.front: Name four of the Indigenous nations who gathered at Fort Laramie in September 1851, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Lakota Sioux / Cheyenne / Arapaho / Crow
